paragraphs.text: There was an old enmity between the children of Israel and the people of Moab, who lived beside them, ever since Saul smote them (1 Sam 14:47). Then they became servants to David (2 Sam 8:2, 12; 1 Chr 18:2), and they were also subject to Solomon, and subject to Israel after the division, paying tribute to the children of Israel (2 Kgs 3:4). So when Ahab king of Israel died, Moab seized the opportunity and rebelled against Israel in order to be rid of the tribute.
Lattice: a window.
Upper chamber: an upper room in his palace.
Ekron: one of the five great cities of the Philistines, and the farthest of them to the north. Today it is "Aqir," a village about twenty km south of Jaffa.

Baalzebub: its meaning is the god of flies, and he was the god worshipped in the city of Ekron. The Jews called him Beelzebub, that is, the god of filth (refuse), to despise his standing. Baalzebub was the most important of the Philistine gods; for this reason the Jews called him the prince of the demons when they spoke with Christ (Mt 12:24). King Ahaziah fell through a window in an upper chamber of his palace and was severely injured. Instead of seeking healing from God, he turned to the pagan gods, and sent messengers to the priests of the god Beelzebub, the god of Ekron, to ask them by means of their god whether he would recover or not.

Two great troubles befell Ahaziah, the rebellion of Moab against him and his fall from the lattice, and neither drew him to examine himself, repent and pray. Do you examine yourself when trials befall you, and uncover your sins before God so that He may forgive you and you may change your life and receive His mercies? Or do you make light of it and persist in the snare? Behold, God has given us the opportunity of this life so that we may repent in it; do not waste it, and respond to His calls to you through the events that pass over you.

The Tishbite: that is, from the town of Tishbe, which lies in the tribe of Naphtali in the north of the land of the Jews. There is also an opinion that it was a town in Gilead, which lies east of the Jordan.

God was angry at Ahaziah's conduct and sent His angel to Elijah the prophet to meet the messengers of Ahaziah who were going to Ekron, and he rebuked them with the word of God, denouncing how they could go to a pagan god, as if there were no God among the children of Israel, though they knew the true God. We note that Elijah knew what had happened from the angel, and this was to show the king's messengers that Elijah's words were from God, because no one knew about this mission except the king and his messengers. The angel asked Elijah to go up because the city of Samaria was built on a hill, so he met the messengers as soon as they came down from the city, and told them God's judgment, and they quickly returned to the king.
Before Elijah left them, he told them God's judgment so that they might report it to the king, namely that he would not rise from his bed but would die.

The king's messengers did not complete their journey to the priests of Baalzebub, but returned at once to the king, who met them with the question why they had not completed the errand he had given them, since they had come back so quickly.

His messengers answered him that a man whom they did not know had met them on the way and commanded them to return to the king who had sent them, and tell him God's judgment on the king, that he would not recover but would die.
The king asked them to describe to him the appearance of the man who had met them and spoken these words to them.

His messengers told him that he was a hairy man with a girdle of leather about his loins. The king knew at once that he was Elijah the Tishbite. Naturally Ahaziah knew Elijah, because he had seen him when Ahaziah was a youth with his father King Ahab, and had heard much about the power of God that was with him, in addition to his mother Jezebel's distress over him. So he hated him, because Ahaziah was wicked and far from God.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elijah

paragraphs.text: The king commissioned a captain of a company of fifty soldiers to seize Elijah. Elijah was sitting on the top of a hill, and the captain called to him from below the hill by the title they were accustomed to address him with, "man of God," informing him of the king's command that he must come down to meet the king. The king did not intend to summon Elijah to receive his blessing, but sent fifty soldiers with their captain to seize him, in anger at the word he had spoken that he would die. Ahaziah sent fifty men because he knew the power of God that was in Elijah, but he did not realize that no number of men can stand before the power of God.

The captain called him "man of God" not out of faith in this title, nor with sufficient respect, but because the captain thought he had authority from the king to seize Elijah and that he was under the protection of the pagan gods whom he worshipped like the king, and who in his eyes were stronger than Elijah's God. It is strange that King Ahaziah rejected God's judgment of his death and did not try to repent, though he had been ready to accept a sentence of death by the authority of Baalzebub, for he had sent to ask him whether he would recover or die.

Do not resort to sorcerers and demons to know your future or to solve your problems, lest you fall under God's wrath and deserve death and eternal torment. If you are in need, or have fallen into any trial, seek God and be insistent with Him, and do not resort to anyone else, and He will rescue you from all your troubles by His fatherhood and tenderness.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elijah

paragraphs.text: Elijah answered the captain of fifty, saying: If I am indeed a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty. Indeed fire came down from heaven and consumed the whole company. Elijah said this by a revelation from God, for we see in (v. 15) that the angel told him to go down to the king. So Elijah was not avenging himself for the attempt to seize him; rather it was God who wished to show the weakness of the pagan gods, such as Baalzebub, on whom they relied, and He dealt with the king and the people in the way they understand, that is, with severity, that perhaps they might believe in Him and repent. This is, of course, different from the disciples' request that Christ send fire from heaven, for that contained vengeance and rage, and therefore Christ refused their request (Lk 9:51-56).

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elijah

paragraphs.text: When Ahaziah learned of the death of the fifty and their captain, he did not examine himself and seek God, but in hardness of heart sent another fifty with their captain with strict orders to seize Elijah. The captain said to him, Make haste and come down to meet the king. Then, as the previous time, Elijah commanded that fire come down from heaven and consume them, so that the king and all the people might know that God is stronger than all the pagan gods, and might respect His man Elijah and the word of God that was on his lips.
Here God's longsuffering toward Ahaziah appears, and at the same time Ahaziah's hardness of heart and his refusal to repent.

Do not be stubborn against the voice of God, but return to Him in repentance, and He will have mercy on you and forgive your sins. For who are you, that you defy God and provoke Him by your insistence on committing sin and by not benefiting from the events around you and the teachings of the Church, which calls you to repent?

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elijah

paragraphs.text: In hardness of heart Ahaziah refused to believe in the power of God and had no pity on his soldiers, so he again sent a third fifty, with their captain at their head. But this captain was different from his two predecessors; he was a devout man who feared God and worshipped Him. He did not call to Elijah as the former ones had done, but went up himself to the top of the hill, where Elijah was sitting, bowed down before him, and entreated him to spare his life and the lives of the fifty with him, asking him not to punish them with fire coming down from heaven, as had happened to the two previous missions.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elijah

paragraphs.text: Elijah moved only under the guidance of the Lord, so the angel of the Lord reassured him and told him to respond to the request of the captain of fifty and go down with him from the hill. He did so, and went with the captain to the king.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elijah

paragraphs.text: Elijah repeated before the king the same message as before, which he had sent to him by his messengers when the king resorted to Baalzebub. Here Elijah's courage and obedience to God appear, for he was ready to endure any hardship, even death, and he proclaimed the word of God with power, that perhaps the king might repent in the last moments of his life; but sadly he did not repent.

entries.section: (3) The death of Ahaziah and the reign of Jehoram

paragraphs.text: The word of the Lord, which He had spoken by the mouth of Elijah, was fulfilled, for King Ahaziah died. His brother Jehoram, the second son of Ahab and Jezebel, ascended the throne of Israel after him, because Ahaziah had no sons. This was in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat over the kingdom of Judah. It is noted that Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat reigned with his father in the seventeenth year of his father's reign over Judah, and about two years after Jehoram's reign with his father Jehoshaphat, Joram son of Ahab reigned over Israel in place of his brother Ahaziah who had died.

entries.section: (3) The death of Ahaziah and the reign of Jehoram

paragraphs.text: There are historical records of all the acts of Ahaziah and what he did during his reign, written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. It is a book that existed in the days of those kings and is not among the books of the Holy Bible, and it is different from the First and Second Chronicles.

The inevitable result of persisting in evil is destruction. This is what happened to Ahaziah after he made light of God's longsuffering. So remember the judgment, that you may be alert to your sins and hasten to repentance. Remember the judgment at the end of each day with the prayer of the Sleep hour, and when you wake and God gives you a new day, remember the Resurrection of Christ, that you may rise with Him and pray the prayer of the Prime hour from the Agpeya. These prayers help you to repent at the end of each day and to begin with hope at the start of each day.

The ascension of Elijah and Elisha succeeding him in prophecy. If the previous chapter tells us of the end of a wicked king, Ahaziah, with his sickness and death, since God's wrath came upon him, in this chapter we find the end of a great prophet, Elijah, who is taken up to heaven in his body, to live in a position of great standing and greatness with God.

entries.section: (1) The taking up of Elijah to heaven in the whirlwind

paragraphs.text: Gilgal: a city lying east of Jericho, four miles away, and north of Bethel, 13 km away, and it lies in the allotment of Ephraim. It is different from the Gilgal where Joshua camped when he entered the land of Canaan. When the Lord decided to take Elijah to heaven in the whirlwind, Elijah and his disciple Elisha were at Gilgal and about to leave it.

entries.section: (1) The taking up of Elijah to heaven in the whirlwind

paragraphs.text: Bethel: it lies twelve miles from Jerusalem.

Elijah wished to be alone on this journey, so he made Elisha understand that he had been sent by the Lord to Bethel and asked him to stay at Gilgal. But Elisha refused and swore not to leave his master. This shows how firmly Elisha held to being a disciple at the hands of Elijah, to receive his blessing and learn from him, especially as God had informed him that the end of Elijah's life was near, as we shall understand from the following verses.

We note that Elijah traveled between the towns to visit the sons of the prophets who were in them, to bless them and bid them farewell, since he knew that his departure from this world was near. He told Elisha to stay at Gilgal, perhaps because he wanted solitude with God at the end of his life, or to test how firmly Elisha held to discipleship at his hands. It may also be that the reason was Elijah's attempt to hide his ascent to heaven as a kind of humility.

entries.section: (1) The taking up of Elijah to heaven in the whirlwind

paragraphs.text: The sons of the prophets: they are the students in the school of the prophets, which Elijah supervised and in which he taught them the spiritual life.

When they reached Bethel, the sons of the prophets who lived there came out to meet Elisha and asked him whether he knew that the Lord would take away his master Elijah that day. He answered them that he knew it; let them keep silent, because the matter was grievous to him.

entries.section: (1) The taking up of Elijah to heaven in the whirlwind

paragraphs.text: Jericho: Jericho is a city lying eight kilometers west of the Jordan River and twenty-seven kilometers northeast of Jerusalem, and about twelve kilometers from Bethel. Again Elijah asked Elisha to stay at Bethel, because the Lord had sent him on a mission to Jericho. Elisha refused, as he had done the previous time, and accompanied his master to Jericho. Here Elijah continues his visiting of the schools of the prophets to reassure them, bid them farewell and encourage them. Elisha likewise continues to hold to his master, to be his disciple until the last moment of his life, and in this he surpasses the disciples of Christ, who slept in the garden of Gethsemane, though Christ had told them that His departure from this world was near.

It is also noted how much care Elijah took in visiting and tending his sons the prophets, for he walked long distances between one town and another, a distance estimated at several miles; and likewise Elisha's striving to cling to his master, for he walked with him these long distances, which are thirteen kilometers from Gilgal to Bethel, then twelve kilometers from Bethel to Jericho, then eight kilometers from Jericho to the Jordan River. These distances took long hours, about nine hours or more, and this shows the seriousness and care of these two great prophets.

Do not be slack in your prayers and prostrations, for your striving is very precious to God. Respond to His love, for He made light of sufferings for your sake on the Cross. Do not be slack in visiting His children and seeking every person who is far away, as Christ walked for long hours for the sake of the Samaritan woman. He awaits your love, so do not delay.

entries.section: (1) The taking up of Elijah to heaven in the whirlwind

paragraphs.text: At Jericho the same thing happened again as with the prophets of Bethel (v. 3), and Elisha gave them the same reply.

entries.section: (1) The taking up of Elijah to heaven in the whirlwind

paragraphs.text: For the third time Elijah told his disciple that the Lord had sent him to the Jordan, and this time also Elisha refused to stay and went on with his master toward the Jordan.

entries.section: (1) The taking up of Elijah to heaven in the whirlwind

paragraphs.text: The sons of the prophets learned of the coming of Elijah and Elisha, so they came to them, where they stood on the bank of the river, and stood opposite them, that is, at a distance from them, on the same side of the river, that is, the western bank. It is noted that the fifty prophets were from the school of the prophets at Jericho, and this shows the great number of the prophets; for if this number is only some of the prophets of this school, how great must be the number of the prophets in all the schools! This also shows how much Elijah cared about discipling a generation of prophets after him, and also how great God's blessing was in giving prophecy to a large number, and their care to be disciples at the hands of Elijah, all this in the midst of a wicked generation that worshipped idols and was led by wicked kings such as Ahab.

entries.section: (1) The taking up of Elijah to heaven in the whirlwind

paragraphs.text: Elijah took his mantle, wrapped it together, and struck the water with it, and it divided into two parts, which enabled Elijah and Elisha to cross over on the dry bed of the river to the opposite bank. Here the grace of God appears, which dried the bed of the river so that they might cross it easily.
Here a great miracle appears, repeated for the third time, after the dividing of the Red Sea by Moses and the dividing of the Jordan by Joshua, and this was done for the following reasons:

1- So that Elijah's ascent to heaven might take place quietly, and none might see it except Elisha his disciple, who was of a high spiritual level, for only the spiritual can bear these divine sights.
2- The dividing of the river proclaims Elijah's power before the prophets and all the people, that they may hold fast to his teachings and reject the worship of idols.

3- Elisha's passing with Elijah proclaims his standing before the prophets, which would grow more firm, as will appear in the following verses, so that they would submit to him as their leader after Elijah.

4- Elijah's crossing the Jordan with the waters standing on both sides signifies that death is nothing but a departure, as we remember in the Litany of the Departed, because Elijah afterward went up to heaven, and this is a declaration that there is no death for those who believe in God.

5- The crossing of Elijah and Elisha in the Jordan reminded the prophets and the people of the crossing of the Red Sea and of the Jordan before, and all this signifies the sacrament of Baptism, which brings us across from slavery, the worship of idols and evil to the new life with God.

entries.section: (1) The taking up of Elijah to heaven in the whirlwind

paragraphs.text: When they had crossed over, Elijah said to Elisha: Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee. Elisha asked that a double portion of the spiritual power Elijah had might rest upon him. The inheritance of a double portion is the share of the firstborn when the inheritance is divided, so Elisha asked to be counted as Elijah's firstborn son, because Elijah had chosen him to be a prophet after him (1 Kgs 19:19). Elisha felt his great need and asked for a power to support him in his great prophetic work and his leading of the people of God.

This does not mean that Elisha would become greater in spiritual stature than Elijah, but that he would receive a doubled power in working miracles, and this indeed happened, as we shall see in the following chapters.

Although Elijah was detached and poor, he possessed everything through his relationship with God, so he said to his disciple, What shall I give you by my prayer? And he gave him more than any gift a rich man gives to others.

You possess the greatest power in the world, which is prayer, to satisfy your soul and fill the needs of those around you. So trust in the power of God that is in you and lift up your heart in prayer, and do not look at your weakness, or your poverty, or the multitude of your sins, for repentance restores to you your sonship to God, and you ask of your heavenly Father all that you wish, and you will be answered.

entries.section: (1) The taking up of Elijah to heaven in the whirlwind

paragraphs.text: Elijah made clear to Elisha that his request was great and difficult, but God, who is able to do all things, would give it to him, because he had not asked for glory or wealth but for the power of God, which would help him in his ministry. He promised him the fulfillment of this request as soon as he saw Elijah's departure from the world, but before seeing it he would receive nothing, for this power is tied to his taking over the leadership of the ministry. His saying "if thou see me" means that spiritual sights are seen only by those to whom God grants it. Gehazi, Elisha's servant, did not see the heavenly hosts that supported his master Elisha until Elisha prayed for him, and his eyes were opened and he saw (ch. 6:17). So if Elisha saw the sight of Elijah ascending, this meant God's seal that Elisha's choice as spiritual leader of the people was confirmed, and He allowed him to see this spiritual sight, which is Elijah's ascent, and consequently to receive at the same time the power to begin his ministry.

The divine graces are abundant, and the Lord is ready to give them to those of His children who ask for them, but we must ask for them with persistence, in continual prayer, relying on the promise of the Lord Christ who said: "Seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you" (Mt 7:7), especially if you feel the greatness of the responsibility facing you and your need for God's support.

entries.section: (1) The taking up of Elijah to heaven in the whirlwind

paragraphs.text: After Elisha crossed the Jordan with his master Elijah, they walked on together on the eastern bank of the river, with Elisha trying to ask his master questions and benefit from him in the last moments of his life. And as they went on, a chariot of fire, drawn by horses of fire, came toward them from heaven. This chariot and its horses are angels, who appeared in this fiery form, as their appearance was repeated to Elisha in (2 Kgs 6:17). Elisha was afraid and drew back to one side, and the chariot parted him from his master Elijah, to proclaim that Elijah was of a high spiritual standing and would be joined to the heavenly ones. Then Elijah mounted this fiery chariot. At that moment Elisha saw a whirlwind carry this chariot and rise with it to heaven, in a great and awesome sight, and Elisha's eyes remained fixed on his master and his fiery chariot until he disappeared from view.

Elijah's ascent to heaven confirms that proclaiming the truth is a great virtue, over which heaven rejoices. Therefore Elijah was lifted up because of this virtue, to be with the heavenly ones, and to encourage every person to proclaim the truth whatever great cost it may bring him, even if it costs his life.
Perhaps Elijah's ascent in a chariot of fire accords with his fiery life, in his sense of God's presence with him and His power in proclaiming the truth.
Elijah's ascent to heaven is a type of Christ's Resurrection and His Ascension into the heavens, to prepare a place for us and to bring us up into the Kingdom after the end of our life on earth.

entries.section: (2) The beginning of Elisha's ministry

paragraphs.text: While Elisha was seeing the chariot rise with his master Elijah to heaven and almost disappear from his sight, he was crying out to his master with a loud voice and saying to him "My father," for he was bound to him as to a father and had been a disciple at his hands for long years, nearly sixteen years, in which he saw in his master a strong spiritual leader who led the children of Israel and called them to life with God. Therefore he called him the chariot of Israel and the horsemen thereof, for this chariot which announced the end of Elijah's life on earth is a declaration of his ministry, in which he led the people like one riding in a chariot, with the multitudes of the people following him in the way of God.

Elisha was in very great pain at his master's parting from him, and he expressed his deep grief by rending his clothes, which is an ancient Eastern custom practiced by many peoples and still continues today in Upper Egypt.
The rending of the clothes also meant his sense of the greatness of the responsibility that had come to him in leading this great people, most of whom were sunk in the worship of idols.

Let your eyes be fixed on heaven and on the saints, your fathers who intercede for you, so that you become a disciple of their lives and enjoy their friendship, and your life is lifted up toward heaven and you prepare for the Kingdom.

entries.section: (2) The beginning of Elisha's ministry

paragraphs.text: When Elijah went up in the chariot of fire, his mantle fell from him to the ground, and this was of course by God's arrangement so that Elisha might take it, not only as a blessing from his master but because this mantle holds a memory in Elisha's heart that he can never forget, for sixteen years before, Elijah had cast it upon him when he was plowing in his father's fields and called him to ministry, and he continued as a disciple, close beside his master, all that time. Now he begins to practice the ministry to which God had called him, so he took hold of the mantle, that is, of God's calling. And by God's power he is able to begin, and not by himself. This mantle also, only a few hours before, had divided the Jordan River, so that he and Elijah crossed on the dry ground of the river. So this mantle represents the power of God that supports him, like the rod of Moses with which he worked miracles. And when Elisha took hold of Elijah's mantle he stood before the Jordan River to work his first miracle.

entries.section: (2) The beginning of Elisha's ministry

paragraphs.text: Elisha wanted to cross the Jordan River to reach the prophets standing on the other bank, that is, the western bank of the Jordan. As he held Elijah's mantle he believed in the power of this mantle, so he struck the water of the river with it so that it would divide and he could cross, as had happened before with Elijah, but nothing happened. He felt that the power is not in the mantle but in God who works through it, so he cried out to God asking His help; and as He had worked with Elijah, he needed Him to work with him now. Therefore he said, Where is the Lord God of Elijah? Then his heart was filled with stronger faith and he did not doubt, but took up the mantle and struck the river with it, and it divided into two parts, so that Elisha crossed between them. Thus it appeared to the prophets, and consequently to all the people, that as Elijah had divided the river, so Elisha also divided it, that is, that the power of God that had been working in Elijah is the same that works in Elisha.

Be steadfast in your faith even if God does not answer you quickly. God may delay in order to teach you many things, just as He taught Elisha that the power is from Him and not in material things in themselves. And if you do not quickly understand God's purpose, you will understand it if you continue in prayer, and your heart will be at rest.

entries.section: (2) The beginning of Elisha's ministry

paragraphs.text: When the sons of the prophets who dwelt at Jericho saw him coming toward them, they were certain that the spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha, so they came to meet him and bowed themselves before him, a bowing of respect and honor, acknowledging and being convinced that he had taken the place of Elijah.

entries.section: (2) The beginning of Elisha's ministry

paragraphs.text: After the sons of the prophets bowed to Elisha, because he had worked the miracle of dividing the river and they saw him alone without Elijah, their eyes were asking about Elijah. So Elisha told them what he had seen and how Elijah went up in the chariot of fire and the whirlwind to heaven until he disappeared from his sight. But because of these prophets' attachment to the great Elijah, and because of their spiritual weakness, they could not understand that Elijah had been taken to heaven and they would not see him again. They imagined that this chariot of fire could carry him from one place to another, so that it was merely a declaration of the greatness of their prophet Elijah, for whom a chariot comes from heaven to carry him to another place. They understood that this chariot and its horses were angels, that is, that the Spirit of God was the One who lifted him up to heaven, and they thought that the chariot had carried him to one of the mountains or valleys. So they asked Elisha, to whom they had submitted as their new leader, to allow them to search for Elijah, especially as their number was large, fifty men. Elisha refused, being confident that his master had gone up to heaven. The prophets thought that Elijah had been taken to another place because they were accustomed to his disappearing from them for periods, for he loved solitude and prayer all his life, and they did not understand that this was the end.

entries.section: (2) The beginning of Elisha's ministry

paragraphs.text: Although Elisha forbade the prophets to search for Elijah, they repeated their request many times, until Elisha was ashamed before them. This shows the gentleness of his feelings, for he is mighty by the power of God that supports him, but his feelings are tender and as a man he is ashamed at people's insistence on him. So he agreed to go and search for Elijah, although he was not convinced of what they were doing and was confident that Elijah had gone up to the heavens.
Another reason for his agreement was that they might not think he loved leadership and was hasty to lead the people and did not want Elijah to return, so that he might be the leader.
They searched for Elijah three days and did not find him, and this was a certain declaration that he had gone up to the heavens and had not gone to some other place on earth.

entries.section: (2) The beginning of Elisha's ministry

paragraphs.text: Elisha stayed at Jericho three days, until the sons of the prophets returned to him and told him that they had not found Elijah. He said to them, Did I not say unto you, Go not? That is, why did you doubt what I told you? This was a second divine declaration, after his dividing the river, that they ought to obey Elisha in everything, because the Spirit of God was in him. And Elisha here is a type of Christ, who is longsuffering toward the doubters and all who do not obey Him, just as He bore with the doubt of Thomas.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the waters

paragraphs.text: Naught: unfit to drink and harmful to health, and it may be poisonous.
Barren: unfruitful.

Those responsible for the city of Jericho heard from the sons of the prophets what Elisha had done in dividing the Jordan River, and that he had become the prophet and leader of the people. So they seized the opportunity of his presence in their city for him to solve a basic problem from which they suffered, which was that although the position of their city was fine, at the foot of the mountain with the valley of the Jordan River in front of it, the main spring that watered the city had water that was unfit for drinking or farming. Perhaps they drank from small wells inside or outside the city, but farming was almost nonexistent for lack of sufficient water for farming.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the waters

paragraphs.text: Elisha cared about their problem and came forward to solve it for them, so that when they saw the miracle they might believe in God and turn away from the worship of idols. He asked for a new cruse, and this signifies the renewal of conduct and of life with God, so that He may bless us and work in us with power. Then he also asked for salt to be put in the cruse. Salt is not a substance for improving water but for spoiling it, for salty water does not become fit for drinking or farming; but this was to show that the power is from God and not from the substance. He used a substance to be visible to people's eyes and tangible, that they might be assured of the completion of the miracle, just as the Church uses materials in the performance of her seven sacraments. Salt signifies the believers who improve the earth by their pure conduct, as salt improves food so that its taste is good; therefore Christ said, Ye are the salt of the earth (Mt 5:13). Of course a little salt cannot improve a whole spring of water, but what is meant is the power of God, which works and uses a substance to reassure people's hearts.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the waters

paragraphs.text: Elisha took the dish and the salt and went out to the spring of water and cast the salt into it, and declared in faith that the water was healed, and that there was no longer in it any foreign substance that causes the death of man, or animal, or plant, that is, it became sweet and fit for drinking and farming. This water remained sweet until the days of Jeremiah, when this book was written, and it is thought that this spring still exists today and is called "the Sultan's Spring."

Do not be troubled by any problem that befalls you, but resort to God, intercede through the saints and seek the guidance of your spiritual fathers, confident that God will not leave you and will solve your problems, for He is able to do all things.

entries.section: (4) The children mocking Elisha

paragraphs.text: After Elisha worked his great miracle at Jericho, he went to Bethel to visit the school of the prophets and care for its people. Bethel was the seat of the worship of the calf that Jeroboam made, who was the first to divide the Jews into two kingdoms and made his people worship idols. We may recall that "Bethel" means "house of God," and it is the city and the place that Jacob set apart to the name of God after he saw Him in his dream there. Of course its inhabitants refused to hear the words of the prophets because of their unbelief in God, and even mocked them. So when the people of Bethel saw Elisha coming from afar, they stirred up their youths, who came out of the city in great numbers, perhaps two hundred or three hundred, and received Elisha with fierce mockery, taunting him that he was bald and repeating this more than once in derision of him. Perhaps by "go up" they meant, go up to heaven like your master Elijah, who you imagine went up to heaven, that is, they were mocking him because they did not believe that Elijah went up to heaven, nor in Elisha's dignity as a prophet. This is exceedingly strange, because they had certainly heard of his miracle in healing the water at Jericho and how all its people rejoiced in it.

entries.section: (4) The children mocking Elisha

paragraphs.text: The wilderness: desolate places not inhabited by people.

Elisha looked at the crowds of youths mocking him and was not troubled for his own sake, but was troubled by the city's insistence on rejecting God, showing it by mocking His prophet. He proclaimed God's wrath on the city by cursing those youths, so two she bears came out of the wilderness and fell upon the boys and killed forty and two boys of them. Because Elisha did not intend personal rage but the glory of God, God answered his curse on the children, and the two bears came out and killed a number of them, that perhaps the people of the city would fear God and leave the worship of idols and return in repentance.

God sometimes uses tenderness and love to draw His children to Himself, or wrath in severe afflictions, to draw them also to Himself, for He desires the salvation of all and uses various ways for the repentance of His children. I wish you would heed God's messages, whether His tenderness or His wrath, and return to Him in repentance and find the salvation of your soul.

entries.section: (4) The children mocking Elisha

paragraphs.text: Carmel: a range of mountains clothed with fruitful forests, near Jaffa, which is on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, and Carmel overlooks the plain of Jezreel.
Samaria: the capital of the northern kingdom, which comprises the ten tribes, and it lies in a middle place between Galilee in the north and Judea in the south.

Elisha went to Carmel, where Elijah killed the prophets of Baal, and from there he went to Samaria, the capital of the northern kingdom, and there he made his home (ch. 5:3, 9; ch. 6:32). King Jehoram and the war against Moab.

entries.section: (1) Joram (Jehoram) reigns over Israel

paragraphs.text: At the end of the first chapter (ch. 1:17) we learned that Ahaziah son of Ahab had no son, so the kingdom passed after his death to his brother Jehoram son of Ahab. The beginning of his reign over Israel was in the capital Samaria, in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and his rule lasted twelve years. At the time when Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel, it was the second year of Jehoram's sharing the kingdom of Judah with Jehoshaphat his father. Jehoram son of Ahab removed the image of Baal but did not kill the prophets of Baal (v. 13), so the inclination to worship idols remained in Samaria. On the other hand, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah married Athaliah daughter of Ahab, and by this the worship of idols entered the kingdom of Judah. This shows how widespread the worship of idols was in the two Jewish kingdoms, the northern and the southern, in the days of Elisha the prophet, which made his mission difficult in proclaiming the truth and bringing people back to the worship of God.

entries.section: (1) Joram (Jehoram) reigns over Israel

paragraphs.text: Jehoram was less than his father Ahab and his mother (Jezebel) in irreligion, for he removed the image of Baal that his father had made; yet he did not destroy the prophets of Baal, as is clear from Elisha's reply to him, saying: "Get thee to the prophets of thy father, and to the prophets of thy mother" (v. 13). He gave up outwardly the material appearances of pagan worship, but its spirit remained dominant, and Jehoram did not abandon the national religion founded by Jeroboam son of Nebat, who set up idols in his kingdom at Bethel and Dan (1 Kgs 12:29).

Jehoram removed the image of Baal but did not kill his prophets, nor remove the images of the calves at Bethel and Dan. So do not abandon one sin and keep the rest of the sins, for they will drag you into every evil. Offer complete repentance, confident of the power of God, which will support your weakness and free you from the dominion of the sins that rule over you. However often you fall, rise again, insisting on the new life, and God will value your labor and will give you a place in His Kingdom.

entries.section: (2) Jehoram's alliance to fight Moab

paragraphs.text: Mesha king of Moab used to pay tribute to Ahab from his great wealth in livestock, rendering him every year a hundred thousand lambs and a hundred thousand rams with their wool. This payment of tribute began in the days of Omri king of Israel, but when Ahab died Moab rebelled and no longer paid the tribute.

entries.section: (2) Jehoram's alliance to fight Moab

paragraphs.text: Jehoram was troubled, when he became king after Ahaziah, by the rebellion of Moab and their not paying the tribute to his brother Ahaziah. So he decided to subdue them to himself so that they would pay the tribute, and began to prepare for war. He ordered the numbering of his soldiers to know the fighting strength he possessed, and found it too small for fighting Moab; therefore he thought of allying with other kings to help him in this war.

entries.section: (2) Jehoram's alliance to fight Moab

paragraphs.text: Jehoram king of Israel sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah asking him to ally with him to fight the king of Moab, especially as there was kinship between them, since Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat had married Athaliah the sister of Jehoram king of Israel. Jehoshaphat at once declared his agreement and readiness to fight side by side with the armies of Israel and to share the same dangers for soldiers and horses. Although Jehoshaphat was a good king, he erred in marrying his son to the daughter of Ahab the wicked king of Israel, and then in agreeing to fight with Jehoram king of Israel, because of his attachment to the worship of idols. He had agreed before to fight with Ahab, his father, at Ramoth-gilead (1 Kgs 22:4).

entries.section: (2) Jehoram's alliance to fight Moab

paragraphs.text: Jehoram king of Israel asked Jehoshaphat king of Judah, who had agreed to ally with him to fight the king of Moab, and said to him, Which way shall we go up? There were two roads. The easy road was to go east to the Jordan River and cross it, then descend south and find Moab; or they could go south and pass through Edom and go around from west to east south of the Dead Sea, to fight Moab from the south. This was the hard road, and Jehoshaphat preferred that they take the hard road for the following reasons:
1- Because Moab would not expect them to come by this road, so their attack on Moab would be a surprise, and they would overcome it.
2- Because on the way they would pass through Edom, which was subject to the king of Judah, and would join it with its armies to them, so the alliance would become threefold and stronger.

entries.section: (2) Jehoram's alliance to fight Moab

paragraphs.text: The king of Israel went there in company with his two allies, the king of Judah and the king of Edom, and they wandered through the wide desert for seven days without finding a source of water, and the army ran out of water, so that none was left for the soldiers or for the beasts that accompanied the army.

It is noted that the kings erred in not praying before going out to war, and consequently did not receive God's help and guidance. They forgot to carry with them plenty of water sufficient for their long journey, or did not calculate carefully their need for water.

Do not be so occupied with the problem that faces you and with your plans to solve it that you forget to pray, for God's guidance and help are the foundation of success, and He keeps you from many dangers you do not expect. He loves you, so why do you neglect Him? He will give to you and will take nothing from you, so let Him into your life and into all your needs.

entries.section: (2) Jehoram's alliance to fight Moab

paragraphs.text: Because Jehoram king of Israel had turned away from God and was attached to the worship of idols, when he and the allied armies were exposed to thirst and death he feared God greatly, and because he felt the multitude of his sins he expected this death by thirst to be by God's arrangement, so that the armies of the allies would fall before Moab, for the soldiers would faint from thirst and fall in the war. The man far from God despairs quickly, but the one who believes in God takes refuge in Him and asks His help.

entries.section: (3) The kings resort to Elisha

paragraphs.text: If the king of Israel fell into despair and complaint, Jehoshaphat king of Judah, who knows God, noticed that this problem had happened because they had not sought God before going out to war. So he asked those around him, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord, that we may inquire of the Lord by him? One of the servants of Joram king of Israel came forward and said that Elisha the prophet, who had been a disciple and servant of Elijah, was in a nearby place. It is strange that Elisha should be in this place, because they were in the wilderness south of the Dead Sea, far from the northern kingdom of Israel and also south of the southern kingdom, the kingdom of Judah. Most likely the Spirit of God moved Elisha to accompany these soldiers, and he was near their place in the wilderness when they suffered thirst, so that when Jehoshaphat asked for him he would find him.

Of course the pagan king of Edom did not care about asking a prophet of God, while Joram king of Israel did not like to see Elisha, because his master Elijah was the one who prophesied about the death of his brother Ahaziah the king before him, and of his father and mother, Ahab and Jezebel; in addition he was occupied with the worship of idols and did not care to hear the voice of God from the tongue of His prophets.

entries.section: (3) The kings resort to Elisha

paragraphs.text: Jehoshaphat rejoiced at the news of Elisha's presence and said at once, The word of the Lord is with him, that is, he had found the means by which to hear the voice of God. This shows his godliness and his love for God. He arose to go to him with humility, because he was the one in need of God and of His prophet, and the other two kings, Jehoram king of Israel and the king of Edom, went down with him.

entries.section: (3) The kings resort to Elisha

paragraphs.text: Elisha spoke with courage, because the Spirit of God was in him, who had been in Elijah, with a doubled power. He rebuked Jehoram king of Israel, declaring his refusal to cooperate with him because he relied on the prophets of Baal, whom his parents Ahab and Jezebel had cared for and looked after. Although Joram was a Jew, he was attached to the worship of idols; and although he had removed the image of Baal, he still kept the prophets of Baal as his counselors. Even if he was doubtful about the worship of Baal, he was still insistent on that worship. Elisha's words show that God rejects the one who mixes His worship with the worship of idols. It is possible that he had brought with his army some of the prophets of Baal and their images, and asked them to rescue him from death by thirst and they did not rescue him; therefore he refused to consult them again when Elisha told him to go back to them.

It is noted that Elisha did not speak to the king of Edom, because he was a pagan and consequently rejects the worship of God. Why then did he come with the two to seek God's counsel? Of course he did not believe in God nor in hearing His voice. But Joram king of Israel answered Elisha that he would not go to the prophets of Baal, and that he felt despair, because he and all his soldiers were suffering thirst and were exposed to destruction at the hand of the king of Moab. This answer shows Jehoram's lack of trust in the idols he worshipped, otherwise he would have resorted to them; and at the same time he felt that by worshipping idols he angered God, so despair overcame him.

Rely on God alone and do not be troubled by whatever problems face you. If you use any means to solve the problem, that is only your duty, which you ought to perform; but be confident that the solution will come from God. Any means is worthless as long as you do not trust the power of God that is with you.

entries.section: (3) The kings resort to Elisha

paragraphs.text: Elisha swore by God, declaring by this that He is the only God and that the pagan gods are not gods. In the oath Elisha shows that he feels the presence of God and consequently the fear of Him, so he does not fear people, even if they are kings, because God is the Lord of hosts, that is, in Him is the fullness of power, and whoever stands before God has no fear of human power. This oath is the one his master Elijah the prophet always used, for he had been a good disciple at his hands. Elisha declared that for the sake of honoring Jehoshaphat he would convey the voice of God to the kings, so that because of the presence of righteous Jehoshaphat, Joram and the king of Edom would receive a blessing. On the other hand, despite Jehoshaphat's godliness, his carelessness in associating with the kings of Israel, whether Joram or his father Ahab, brought troubles upon him, for which God reproached him.

Look for your friends and choose them carefully, so that they may lift you up and support you on the way to the Kingdom, and beware of evil company, for it will certainly influence you, even if partially. If you are bound to them by work or neighborhood, let it be within the narrowest limits, and do not open your heart to them, lest their evil thoughts defile it.

entries.section: (3) The kings resort to Elisha

paragraphs.text: Elisha asked for a man to play music on the harp, so that it might accompany his praises raised before God, and after these prayers and praises the Spirit of God came upon him and guided him with the word of God. Prayers and praises are what prepare the heart to hear the voice of God. Indeed, prayer is a dialogue between man and God, in which man lifts up his heart and glorifies God, and God guides him to the truth and good conduct.

These praises, on the other hand, drive away demons. If there are those who worship idols, like the king of Edom and the king of Israel and the prophets of Baal who follow them, their power is nullified and their demons flee, so the atmosphere is cleansed and the word of God appears. This was repeated when David the prophet played on the harp and the demons that were in Saul the king fled (1 Sam 16:23). The prophets in the school of the prophets had been accustomed since the days of Samuel to use musical instruments, such as the harp, when praising God (1 Sam 10:5); therefore Elisha asked for a harpist to lift up his praises to God.

entries.section: (3) The kings resort to Elisha

paragraphs.text: Ditches: plural of a ditch, which is a well or a pit for keeping water.

God's command by the mouth of Elisha the prophet to the kings and those with them was to make in the valley where they stood many deep ditches to receive water. This was a strange command, which human reason does not accept, since there was no source of water and no expectation of rain falling. But this is a proof of faith and submission to God, and God requires this submission in order to work His miracles and pour out His goodness on man. Human striving is a necessary condition for receiving the grace of God, just as Christ asked them to take away the stone from the door of the tomb, and then He worked the miracle and raised Lazarus.

entries.section: (3) The kings resort to Elisha

paragraphs.text: God confirms the importance of the faith He asks of His children. He promises them much water that will fill the valley, though they will not see any natural source of water, for the expected source would be rain from heaven and what accompanies the falling of rain, namely wind. What was required of them was faith and carrying out God's command by digging the ditches; then they would enjoy watering and be satisfied with water, they and their beasts.

entries.section: (3) The kings resort to Elisha

paragraphs.text: God declared to them that if they believed they would see the valley filled with water and would drink. When they see this miracle they will be sure that it is very easy for God to give them victory over Moab, for their faith will grow and they will not fear the enemies.

I wish you would understand God's works and the goodness He gives you, and contemplate His care and thank Him always, so that your faith may be firm and not shaken before any trials or problems that may come upon you.

entries.section: (3) The kings resort to Elisha

paragraphs.text: Stop up: to fill in, that is, to fill them with earth and stones.

As a result of the multitude of the evils of the Moabites and their immersion in the worship of the pagan god Chemosh, God decided to destroy them severely, that perhaps they would believe in His power and leave the worship of idols. So He asked the three kings, by the mouth of Elisha, to destroy all the fenced and chief cities of the Moabites and to fell every good tree. They were also to stop all the wells of water and to mar the fertility of the land of the fields by casting stones on it.

entries.section: (4) The defeat of Moab

paragraphs.text: In the morning, at the holy time when the burnt offering is offered on God's altar in Jerusalem, which is a type of Christ the crucified Redeemer, by whose redemption all good things overflow upon humanity, at this time the kings and those with them saw abundant waters coming from the direction of the mountains of Edom, where the rains had fallen, which the kings had not seen, but it was abundant and reached them in the morning and filled the ditches that they had dug in the valley. Then they all drank and rejoiced and thanked God, for they believed, because of this miracle, that God alone is the true God who works miracles, and the pagan gods became small in their eyes. It is understood, of course, that the kings did not offer a sacrifice, but at the time of the offering of the sacrifice in Jerusalem the flowing of water toward the valley took place, for God wants to bind them to Jerusalem and His holy temple, which is the source of all blessings.

entries.section: (4) The defeat of Moab

paragraphs.text: Border: the boundaries.

When the Moabites sensed the movements of the armies of the three kings advancing toward them, they prepared to meet them, gathering on the border everyone able to put on armor, both the conscripts and those older than they who were able to bear arms, that is, they gathered the greatest number of their men because they felt the danger of the armies coming against them.

entries.section: (4) The defeat of Moab

paragraphs.text: At the time when the waters came from Edom and filled the valley, the Moabites saw the waters red as blood, because the sands of Edom are red, and the water coming from there carries these sands, so its color appears red, in addition to the reflection of the rays of the sun on these waters, so the water appeared like blood.

The Moabites were hoping for victory over the alliance of the armies coming against them, so in their pride they imagined that the kings had been divided against one another and had fought, and the blood of their soldiers had flowed and filled the valley. The proud man falls easily into what he imagines, however far from reality. Therefore when the Moabites saw the sight of the blood they had imagined, they rushed in pride to seize the spoil of the allied armies, which they thought had fled after dividing and killing one another.

Thus we see God's wonderful arrangement, which led the armies to this valley (v. 16) in Edom so that it would be easy to dig the ditches in it and the rain waters would flow toward it coming from the mountains of Edom, so that the army and its livestock could drink; and at the same time God tests the army's faith in digging the ditches before the waters came, then turns the sight of the waters before the eyes of the enemies into blood, so that they imagine the kings have fought one another and rush in to take their spoil. God mocks the enemies who come against His children and makes them fall in their own evils.

The valley signifies humility, and the digging of the ditches to keep the water signifies caring for God's gifts and keeping them, as the disciples gathered the fragments when the multitudes were fed (Mt 14:20). The coming of the waters in abundance signifies God's generosity in His gifts to His children, so that they suffice them and overflow.

entries.section: (4) The defeat of Moab

paragraphs.text: The Moabites indeed set out to the camp of Israel, to plunder and not to fight, and were surprised by the attack of the allied armies upon them. Before this unexpected attack the Moabites could not hold together, so they fled in fear and panic to their land, and the Israelites pursued them, killing everyone who fell into their hands.

entries.section: (4) The defeat of Moab

paragraphs.text: Slingers: plural of sling, which is an instrument for throwing stones.
Kir-haraseth: the old capital of Moab. Its place today is the city of "Karak" in Jordan, about eighteen kilometers east of the southern part of the Dead Sea.

The army of the kings in its advance was destroying the cities, and every soldier cast stones on the arable lands and fruitful fields until they were spoiled. They also stopped all the wells of water and felled every good tree, and nothing remained but the capital of the Moabites, called Kir-haraseth. This was a fortified city with walls built of stones, so it was not easy to demolish them, but the soldiers who use slings advanced and cast many stones upon it to ruin it.

entries.section: (4) The defeat of Moab

paragraphs.text: Drew swords: trained in the use of swords.

When Moab found the allied armies victorious over him, he tried to save the situation by allying with the king of Edom, with whom he had had relations before (2 Chr 20:22, 23). So the king of Moab took seven hundred fighting men of his trained soldiers and tried to break a way for himself through the allied armies, especially the armies of Judah and Israel, so as to reach the king of Edom and ally with him, and by this alliance be able to stand against Judah and Israel allied together; but he failed to break through the ranks of his enemies.
God was with the allied armies, so the enemies' attempts failed. Be confident that as long as God is with you, the threats or wrongs of others will not affect you.

entries.section: (4) The defeat of Moab

paragraphs.text: Then the king of Moab took his eldest son and offered him for a burnt offering upon the wall of the city to the idol Chemosh, the god of the Moabites. The people of the children of Israel shuddered at this dreadful sight and raised the siege and withdrew, returning to their homes without any celebration of victory. Perhaps the king of Moab thought that the withdrawal of the kings meant victory for him, and that it was because of the human sacrifice he had offered to his gods; but in reality he remained defeated amid the ruin and destruction that had come upon his cities.

Perhaps the allied armies felt that this victory was enough for them, that is, the offering as a sacrifice of the enemy's crown prince, who was reigning with his father and in his place, so they departed.

"There was great indignation against Israel" happened, that is, Edom and Judah were indignant at Israel, who caused the crown prince to be offered as a sacrifice, and this displeasure made them depart from the king of Israel who had drawn them into this war. In general the war ended, but Moab had been laid waste, as divine discipline, and at the same time the power of God appeared, which supported the allied armies because of the presence of believing Jehoshaphat with them.

The departure of Edom and Judah from Israel signifies that the outward worship that Israel offers, while it mixes its worship of God with idols, makes the pagans in the end turn away from it, and those who worship God turn away from it also.

Do not try to mix your way as a child of God with the evil ways of the world, for the world will not be pleased with you and God will of course be angry with you. Do not be lukewarm but hot, so that you may receive God's power and blessing and find your salvation.
The miracles of Elisha

entries.section: (1) The widow and the blessing of the oil

paragraphs.text: Creditor: one who lends to the needy and takes interest on it.

If Elijah concentrated his work on the wicked King Ahab and on proclaiming the truth about the worship of God, instead of Baal, before the people, Elisha did not care about King Joram and refused to deal with him and did not help him, except for the sake of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he concentrated his ministry on those who believed in God and the sons of the prophets, to solve their problems, especially the poverty from which they suffered.

One of the sons of the prophets died, a man who feared God, from the school of the prophets whom Elisha led after Elijah, and he was known to Elisha because he was their leader, and he was probably young. He left a widow and two sons, and his family was exposed to severe poverty. The widow began to take some gifts, but they did not suffice her, and she was forced to give up many of her possessions, even the necessary ones. Then she resorted to borrowing from the creditor, and the debts and their interest increased, and she found no means to repay what she owed. Here the creditor threatened to take her two sons as bondmen to himself, or to sell them, which the Law allows. So the widow resorted to Elisha, as the leader of the prophets, the man of God, and the father who feels for his children. Although Elisha was a celibate, he bore a fatherhood toward all his people, especially the prophets who serve God and their families, and even more toward this family and the like of it, who had lost their chief provider.

entries.section: (1) The widow and the blessing of the oil

paragraphs.text: Elisha cared about this widow and did not try to come to an understanding with the creditor, because he might be greedy and hard-hearted; so he took care to examine the widow's possessions and discovered her great poverty, to the point that she had nothing of furniture or food except a pot of oil in one of the vessels, enough only to anoint a piece of bread.

entries.section: (1) The widow and the blessing of the oil

paragraphs.text: Elisha believed in the power of God, who is able to do all things, so he was not troubled by the great poverty from which this widow suffered, but in confidence asked her to borrow empty vessels from her neighbors and to borrow as many as she could. This borrowing shows the following:
1- God cares about man's striving and his readiness to receive the grace of God.
2- According to the widow's faith she would gather many vessels, to be filled, all of them, with the blessing of God.
3- The cooperation of her neighbors helps in working the miracle.
4- The grace of God is given with a generosity that surpasses reason.

5- Elisha did not care to postpone the creditor's demand, or to give him part of the money, but wanted to enrich the widow so that she would pay what she owed and have a surplus, that she might live honored and loved by God, with her needs met and her husband, who feared God, honored.

entries.section: (1) The widow and the blessing of the oil

paragraphs.text: Elisha commanded the widow, after gathering the many vessels, to shut the door of her house upon herself, so that she and her two sons would be alone, for the following reasons:
1- Elisha did not go with her, so that she would trust that the miracle was from the hand of God and not Elisha's personal power. This shows Elisha's humility and his glorifying of God.

2- Only those who believe in the miracle would enjoy seeing it, that is, the widow and her two sons, who were at a high level of faith, and their need made them cling to God, since they had probably learned the fear of God from the provider of the family who had departed.
3- It shows the faith of Elisha, who commanded her to pour out the oil, then lifted up a prayer for God to complete the miracle, for he was confident of God's fatherhood, His love and His power.

4- Elisha's command to pour out the oil shows the widow's faith in obeying his command, so she received the blessing of the miracle, for she had nothing but a pot of oil, and she believed that the vessels would be filled, and she set aside one vessel after another as it was filled.

5- Perhaps the neighbors, if they saw the miracle, would covet this oil and take from her, relying on the fact that the vessels were their vessels and that they had some right to this oil; but the miracle depends on the widow's faith.
6- Shutting the door signifies the importance of man's inner life, such as prayer, fasting and reading the Holy Bible ... and all private spiritual striving.

entries.section: (1) The widow and the blessing of the oil

paragraphs.text: The woman obeyed all that Elisha commanded her. She gathered as many vessels as possible and went into her house and shut the door upon herself and her two sons, and perhaps she stood praying with her sons, while they brought her one vessel after another, and she poured oil into it.

She saw with her own eyes the wonderful miracle, how the pot of oil became a continuous spring of oil, flowing to fill one vessel after another, and of course her heart and her sons' hearts were lifted up in praise and thanksgiving to God.

entries.section: (1) The widow and the blessing of the oil

paragraphs.text: All the vessels were filled, and she asked her sons whether there was still an empty vessel, to bring it to her. They answered that all the vessels were full and there was not one empty vessel left. Then the flow of the oil stopped.

The grace of God is very generous and ready to give you all that you need, according to your care to come to God, and He fills you with His grace; and according to your readiness to give, God gives you largeness of heart and strength, so you give generously and rejoice and make everyone around you rejoice.

entries.section: (1) The widow and the blessing of the oil

paragraphs.text: The widow returned to tell Elisha what had happened, and he told her to go and sell the oil that had gathered in the vessels she had, and pay the debt with the price of what she sold of it, and live on the remainder, she and her two sons. We note that the woman took care to return to Elisha and ask him what to do after the miracle had happened, and this means two things:
1- We ought to return with thanksgiving to God after every grace He gives us.

2- We ought to ask Him in the matters of our life, even if they are clear matters. She now had oil to sell and with which to pay her debts, but her submission to God made her return and ask the man of God. Your asking your father of confession and spiritual guide is a return to God to hear His voice, not out of doubt about what you are doing but out of readiness for a constant hearing of the voice of God, even if He commands you the opposite of what you expected.

You are indebted to God and to His children with all your life, because Christ bought you and paid your price when you had been sentenced to death. So take care to pay your debts by offering love to everyone, and offer love to others before you care for your personal needs. The woman paid her debts before spending on her living. Be confident that God's goodness is abundant and will guarantee all your needs, even if matters become critical and reach distress or severe poverty, for God is ready to work miracles in every generation.

entries.section: (2) The Shunammite woman honors Elisha

paragraphs.text: Shunem: a city opposite Mount Gilboa, called today "Solem," in the land of the tribe of Issachar, about six kilometers east of Jezreel and twenty-five kilometers from Mount Carmel, where the Shunammite woman went to look for Elisha.

Elisha traveled much, to visit his people and the schools of the prophets, and Shunem was in a middle place between many regions, such as Carmel, the plain of Jezreel, Nazareth and Galilee, so he passed through it often. In this city there was a woman who was rich and of a known standing in the city, and she invited him to her house to eat bread, and this hospitality was repeated whenever Elisha passed by Shunem. This shows:
1- The virtue of generosity and hospitality to strangers, for which this woman was distinguished.

2- This woman's care and faith in the blessing of the man of God, for her greatness and their wealth did not distract her from receiving the blessing of God, and this was not a kind of pride or show, as the coming verses show her humility and quietness.

Your offering love to every needy person, or to one passing through special circumstances, opens many doors for you to receive God's blessing in your life, and even gives you things you did not ask for, for God cannot be in debt to anyone. If you give something to His children, He gives you manifold more.

entries.section: (2) The Shunammite woman honors Elisha

paragraphs.text: Table: a board for food.
Candlestick: a lamp.

The woman sensed the holiness and righteousness of the man of God through his brief visits to her house, and longed to receive a greater blessing from him. So she said to her husband that Elisha passed by them often, and suggested to him that they prepare for him a little chamber on the roof of the house and put in it a bed and a table and a stool and a lamp, so that when he visited them on one of his journeys he might rest and sleep in the chamber.

This shows that the woman saw in Elisha's conduct a spiritual way of life and not only that he was a prophet, so she wanted to learn and be a disciple at his hands, and at the same time she took care to prepare for him his necessary needs, so that he might rest amid the toils of travel, by preparing a place in which the needs of rest are provided, namely a bed, and a table on which to eat or to read, and a lamp to help him read. She did not care to show her wealth as a display of greatness before people, but to provide for the needs of this great servant.

Elisha must have found his rest in this house; therefore he passed by it repeatedly, as Christ was accustomed to pass by the house of Lazarus in Bethany. This means that this woman and her house were marked by spiritual qualities in which the man of God found rest. Here we see God's care in providing for the needs of His servants and their rest; if Elisha cared about visiting his people, God provides everything that gives him rest materially and not only spiritually.

entries.section: (3) The promise of a son to the Shunammite

paragraphs.text: On one of Elisha's journeys he passed through the city of Shunem and entered the house of the great woman to rest there, and after he slept in his upper chamber in her house, he asked Gehazi his disciple to call the woman and convey to her his great appreciation for her toil for him and his disciple, in hosting them and her care in building the chamber and furnishing it and everything connected with their hospitality, and to make clear to her Elisha's readiness to repay her kindness by solving any problem she met, which needed intercession with the king or the captain of the host. Although Elisha kept apart from Jehoram king of Israel because of his evils and idol worship, in love he was ready to go to the king and speak to him about this woman's requests, and the king respected and feared Elisha because of his connection with God. This shows Elisha's appreciation of the services done to him and his wish to return the love, to serve her in any need she might have. Although this woman was great and had possessions and of course had some problems, as most rich people meet, she asked nothing of Elisha and said that she dwelt among her own people, though her people, the kingdom of Israel, were Jews among whom the worship of idols had entered; but she focused on the fact that they were the people of God who believe in Him, and therefore she lived in security through this faith. This shows the extent of her faith and her reliance on God. Wealth drives many to love of money and greed, but this woman stood firm in her faith and thanksgiving to God, and so was an example for the godly rich. Besides, as a human being she must have had needs, as will appear in the following verses: she was deprived of children, but her great reliance made her not ask even for this necessary thing.

Elisha's carefulness appears in that the woman did not enter his private chamber, but only his disciple Gehazi, because it was like the monk's cell. The woman's courtesy also appears, despite her greatness, and her respect for the man of God, although his chamber was part of her house.

How beautiful it is to be content with the grace of God that is with you, and to thank Him for everything and enjoy His care and richness, so that He gives you what you need without your asking, and you touch the hand of God and His fatherhood and tenderness.

entries.section: (3) The promise of a son to the Shunammite

paragraphs.text: After the woman went away, Elisha's heart remained occupied with repaying her kindness, and he began to consider with Gehazi his disciple what to do for her. This shows Elisha's humility in taking his disciple's counsel. With familiarity Gehazi said that he had noticed that she had no children, and the woman was not young, and in addition her husband was much older than she and had become old. So Elisha accepted his disciple's drawing his attention to this need.

entries.section: (3) The promise of a son to the Shunammite

paragraphs.text: According to the time of life: the period of pregnancy, that is, nine months.

Elisha responded at once to his disciple's reminder, for he had found the way to honor the woman. So he called her, and she stood reverently at the door of his chamber and did not enter, and he gave her the good news that after nine months God would give her a son. This news was a surprise beyond the woman's reason, and she did not believe it, so that she said to Elisha: Do not lie unto thine handmaid. She did not mean to accuse the man of God of lying, but she was expressing the difficulty of believing this joyful news, because human logic makes this matter almost impossible.

The woman's words show her great humility, for she said to him "my lord" and described herself as his handmaid. She did not use her reason in pride in not believing the news, because she was very humble, but the matter indeed surpasses human reason.

I wish you would trust the love of God, who wants to give you many blessings that surpass reason. The multitude of your sins does not hinder the work of God as long as you are pressing on in the way of repentance; rather, the grace of God abounds with the weak.

entries.section: (3) The promise of a son to the Shunammite

paragraphs.text: The woman's doubts began to recede and she took in the joyful miraculous news, then the news was confirmed by her conceiving, and she was in great joy beyond expression, and the joy was completed by her bearing a son.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: The years passed and the child grew. One day he went with his father to the fields they owned, to oversee the reapers as they gathered the harvest. The city of Shunem had fertile lands. The Shunammite woman's husband was rich and owned many fields, and he went out to oversee the reaping himself. The gathering of the harvest is the most important stage in farming, because from it he gets the toil of the whole year, and sells it.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: Suddenly the boy felt a severe pain in his head which made him cry out, "My head, my head." His father commanded one of his workers to carry him to his house, to his mother. It was a severe sunstroke which the little boy could not bear, and his father felt the seriousness of the situation, so he did not wait until the end of the day but carried him quickly to his house to rest. It seems that because everyone was busy with the harvest they did not care to keep the boy out of the rays of the sun, whose heat he could not bear.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: The servant brought him to his mother, and she held him on her knees all the morning, until noon came and the boy died. The mother in her tenderness was trying to calm the child, not knowing what to do for him, while the dryness inside him increased until he lost consciousness and then departed from life.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: Despite the horror of the sudden event, the woman's faith was not shaken, so she carried her dead son and went up with him to the chamber that she had prepared for Elisha and laid him on the bed of the man of God. Perhaps she remembered Elijah the prophet's raising of the son of the widow of Zarephath of Sidon from death (1 Kgs 17:17-21), and believed that Elisha, who had given her this son from God, was able also to raise him from the dead. As her barren womb, unable to bear, that is, dead to conceiving and bearing, God had brought this life out of, so He is able also to bring out of death new life for her son. Perhaps she remembered her mother Sarah, the wife of our father Abraham, and how God brought out of the deadness of her womb a new life, namely Isaac, for God is able at all times to give life out of death. Perhaps she resembled our father Abraham, who believed, when he went forward to sacrifice Isaac, that God was able to raise him from the dead.

Perhaps her faith that God was able to raise her son made her hold herself together and not weep, so she rose above the feelings of motherhood which could tear her heart, and was at peace and trusted God, who would not leave her.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: Asses: female donkeys.

In faith the woman sent to her husband, telling him that she would go to the man of God at Carmel, where he dwelt. She asked her husband for one of his workers and a donkey, to take her there. Her husband wondered and asked her why she was going, since it was not the day of a religious celebration, which was what he used to do on the sabbath or the new moon. It seems that Carmel, where Elijah had built an altar and the fire consumed his sacrifice and he killed the prophets of Baal (1 Kgs 18:30), had become a holy place where Elisha held religious celebrations and sacrifices.

It is remarkable that in complete faith the woman answered her husband and reassured him that all was well and peaceful, and that it was a visit to be blessed by the man of God. This shows the extent of the woman's faith and her peace that surpasses reason, which is a divine grace that God gave her because of her faith.

If you remember the God who is with you and His power that supports you, you will not be troubled by any problem or distress, confident that God by your prayers will intervene and rescue you from it; indeed, from the steadiness of your peace you can reassure those around you.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: The woman rode on the donkey and commanded the servant to drive the donkey fast, without fearing to cause her fatigue, unless she herself asked him to slow down. This shows the feelings of motherhood that moved her in longing for the raising of her son, so that she might rejoice in him.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: She set out on her journey until she reached Elisha, who was then on Mount Carmel.
Elisha saw her coming while she was still a long way from him, and recognized her, and told his servant that it was the Shunammite woman coming toward them.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: He asked his servant to run to meet her and to inquire about her welfare and that of her husband and her son, and she said to him, It is well. Here the heart of Elisha, full of love, appears, and how he sensed the woman's need from her hastening toward him, so he quickly sent to her his disciple Gehazi to ask about her welfare and that of those with her. It is remarkable that in strong faith she said, It is well, for she was confident that Elisha would raise her son.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: The Shunammite woman reached Elisha, who was staying on Mount Carmel, and she got down from the donkey and hurried to him and bowed down and caught him by the feet, in a clinging that proclaims how much she needed the prophet. Elisha felt the bitterness of her heart and her pains and had compassion on her. But his disciple Gehazi felt that catching Elisha by the feet was lacking in respect for him and tried to push her away from Elisha, but the man of God stopped him, by his sense of her troubles. Gehazi, because of the hardness of his heart, did not feel the woman's pains and condemned her because she did not respect the man of God, but Elisha, the man of prayer, felt for her and had compassion on her.

God hid the boy's illness from Elisha, so that he would not go to him and heal him and it would become an ordinary healing miracle, and He allowed him to die so that the power of God would appear, by the hand of Elisha, in raising him, and God would be glorified; and at the same time it was a showing of the extent of this woman's faith, so she deserved this great miracle, which will appear after some verses.
