From this it appears that the revealing of the unseen to the prophets and the gifted men of God is only to the extent that God allows and not in all things, for God lets them know some matters to help them in ministry and for the glorifying of His holy name.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: With bitterness of heart the woman told Elisha that she had not asked for a son, and when he gave her the good news of bearing a son she had said to him: "Why do you lie to me and deceive me?" since she saw herself unworthy of this son. Elisha understood that her son had died and that she would have preferred to have no son rather than to bear a son and become emotionally attached to him and then have him die. Her saying, Did I not say, Do not deceive me, does not mean that Elisha deceived her, but means her confidence that Elisha had not deceived her and consequently would raise her son, because God, who spoke by the mouth of Elisha, cannot lie. Although she did not prefer to have a son who would die, at the same time she trusted that God was able to raise him.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: As the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth: an oath by the life of God and of Elisha.
Gird up thy loins: that is, to put on the clothes that are worn about the waist down to the thighs, and what is meant is readiness for the journey.

Elisha commanded his disciple Gehazi to prepare for the journey, to go to Shunem to the woman's house, and not to be occupied on the way with blessing anyone in need of a blessing, or accepting good words and blessing from others, that is, not to be occupied with anything on the way, even other services, in order to hasten to reach the dead boy. He asked him to carry Elisha's staff to lay it upon the face of the dead boy, that he might rise. Elisha forgot that the power is not in the staff but in the prayer he lifts up, as he thought in the past when he took Elijah's mantle and tried to divide the Jordan River, and it did not divide until he prayed and asked for the power of God that was with Elijah, and then he divided the river.

The woman did not accept Gehazi's being sent, but clung to Elisha and declared with an oath that she would not leave him. The woman understood the right course and drew Elisha's attention to it by her clinging to him, so he arose with her to go to her house; for since she was confident that Elisha was the source of the blessing, she insisted that he come with her.

We note that the woman's oath, "As the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth," is the same oath that Elisha said to Elijah when he tried to part from him, before Elijah's ascent. So God reminds him of Elijah's faith and the power of God working in him, so that he might rise with the woman and pray for the dead boy.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: Gehazi carried out the word of his master Elisha and hastened ahead of him to the woman's house, to lay Elisha's staff on the boy's face, but there was neither voice nor hearing, and he remained dead, so he returned and told Elisha of the uselessness of what he had done. This is a confirmation of the necessity of the coming of Elisha, the man of God, to pray for the boy. Gehazi's obedience is blessed because it confirmed to Elisha the necessity of prayer and that he should serve in person and care for this boy.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: Elisha reached the woman's house and went up to his chamber and found the boy lying on his bed, so he shut the door of the chamber upon himself and the dead boy, that he might pray to God in quiet. Shutting the door in prayer means casting away the thoughts and preoccupations of the world and concentrating on speaking with God, the only source of power for our life.

God rejoices in your prayer, especially if you give yourself wholly to Him, rejecting all the preoccupations of the world and all reliance on human power, and so you experience the power of God and His care for you. And when you shut the door of your closet, shut also the door of your senses and thoughts, so that you may be wholly with God.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: Elisha was not content with praying beside the dead boy's bed, but lay upon the child and stretched himself upon him, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands, and continued his prayers. That is, Elisha completed his striving, asking for the power of God, and the power of prayer worked and its warmth passed from Elisha's body to the body of the dead boy, so that warmth went through it, that is, life began to stir in him, but he remained in a coma and did not move. We note that God did not work the miracle quickly, so that Elisha might offer continuous striving in prayer with steadfast faith, and so his faith would be strengthened and he would see with his own eyes the greatness of the miracle when it is accomplished in stages.

God allowed Elisha to use material means, namely his lying upon the boy, as He used in his earlier miracles salt and meal ... and as the Church now uses materials in her most important works, namely the holy sacraments, so that man may offer what he has and touch with his hands the material part of the miracle, and not doubt, but by his faith perceive the power of God that works the miracle. Striving is necessary for receiving grace, which does everything and works the miracles.

Perhaps Elisha's lying upon the boy and putting his mouth upon his mouth was meant to transfer life from himself to the dead body, as Christ united with us in His Incarnation, and taking our mortal body gave us His life and raised us in Him, that we may live forever with Him, as we say in the Friday praise, "He took what is ours and gave us what is His," that is, He bore our death for us and gave us His life.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: After Elisha's prayers and his stretching himself upon the dead boy until his body grew warm, he arose to continue the prayer, having been encouraged and his faith strengthened when the boy's body grew warm. He walked to and fro in the house, standing in more than one place inside the house, continuing the prayer with insistence for God to intervene. And after he felt peace in his heart, he stretched himself upon the boy again, and the miracle was accomplished, in that the boy sneezed seven times, then opened his eyes, declaring that he had returned to life.
The miracle was accomplished for the following reasons:
1- The faith of Elisha the prophet, which appeared in his many prayers.
2- Elisha's love for his children and his people, that is, this woman, and his going with her to her house to pray over the dead.
3- Elisha's striving and perseverance and his lying twice upon the boy.
4- The woman's faith and her clinging to Elisha, that he might come and pray for the boy.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: Elisha opened the door of the chamber, where Gehazi was standing watching the situation, and commanded him to call the boy's mother, who came in haste. He called her to enter, and when she entered he said to her, Take up thy son.

We see in this verse that Elisha called the woman three times, in (vv. 12, 15, 36). The first time her reliance on God appeared, the second time she received the joyful news of the birth of the child, and the third time she received the raising of her only son. She signifies the soul that believes in God and obeys His call, for if it relies on Him it receives joy in its life and the experience of resurrection with Christ in all its conduct.

entries.section: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

paragraphs.text: When the woman learned from Gehazi of the raising of her son, she hastened to Elisha to bow down before him, offering her deep thanks and her submission to God in the person of Elisha, and her readiness to hold fast to the commandments of God and His teachings, which the man of God proclaims. After this she went to her son, lying on the bed, to embrace him and rejoice in him.

Take care to offer thanks to God before you are occupied with His gifts, for God is the giver of these gifts; how then can you be occupied with them rather than with Him! And thank also the saints who have helped you and every person who has done you a service.

entries.section: (5) The healing of the poisoned food

paragraphs.text: After the raising of the Shunammite's son, Elisha left Shunem and did not return to Carmel, but went east to Gilgal, beside the Jordan River, to visit the sons of the prophets. It is clear from Elisha's life that he cared about visiting his children, strengthening their faith, tending them and providing for their needs. He gathered with the sons of the prophets and they sat before him, as he taught them his life-giving teachings. After this he had to care for their material food, as Christ taught the multitudes and also took care to feed them with the two fishes and the five loaves. But there was a dearth in the land for some time, that is, they had no food, and Elisha, the man of faith, was not troubled, but asked his disciple Gehazi to bring the great pot in which they prepared food, though there was no food, for he was confident that God would feed His children. He asked Gehazi to bring any kind of plants and boil them to feed the men.

entries.section: (5) The healing of the poisoned food

paragraphs.text: Wild gourds: the wild cucumber, and it is probably the colocynth, whose taste is bitter and which causes violent diarrhea, colic and vomiting.

It seems that Gehazi did not hasten to bring something to boil, as Elisha had commanded him. One of the sons of the prophets was commissioned to gather herbs from the field. But it seems that he found none, because of the famine, but he found wild gourds, and thought them fit for eating, so he gathered a quantity in his lap and brought it to the house and cut it up and put it into the pot.

Here the lack of care and the danger of negligence appear, into which Gehazi fell, and likewise one of the prophets who gathered harmful food. So be careful in your words and actions, lest you harm those around you and wrong them without intending to, and so trouble and distress them. Be obedient to your spiritual fathers, quick to carry out their words; then God will support you and guide you and protect you from many troubles.

entries.section: (5) The healing of the poisoned food

paragraphs.text: After the gourds were boiled, the men began to eat, and they felt the bitterness of the food and expected death because of this poisonous food, so they cried out to Elisha their leader to rescue them.

Perhaps God allowed the famine, and then also allowed the presence of these poisonous plants, to warn His people Israel, who had mixed their worship with the worship of idols, so that they might take heed through these distresses and put away their evils to live with Him. Sin causes death and prevents blessings; on the contrary, when the children of God are present, blessings spread and they rescue others from destruction, as will happen at the hand of Elisha.

entries.section: (5) The healing of the poisoned food

paragraphs.text: Elisha commanded that the poisonous food be gathered and put again into the pot, then commanded them to bring a little meal, and blessed it, then cast it into the pot, and in faith in the love of God and His care he asked them to pour out for the men in their dishes, confident that God had removed the poison from this food. The men came forward in faith also to eat, trusting Elisha's command, and they ate and found it good, delicious food, and found it completely different from the first food. The meal signifies the Body of Christ, as the offering of the grain offering anciently in the days of Moses signified it. So also the bread that is changed into the Body of Christ in the Divine Liturgy, for Christ is able to save us from death and to put away from us all the evils of the devil.

When sin enters our daily life it becomes death for us, as it enters into smoking, wine and drugs, and into cheating in dealings between people, and into every evil thought that accompanies our works and words, so that death goes through us within, and there is no way of escape from it except prayer and repentance. When we return to God He rescues us from our evil deeds.
Believe in God in all your circumstances, however difficult they may seem, and He will turn evil into good and put away from you everything harmful, and you will live in assurance.

entries.section: (6) The blessing of the twenty loaves

paragraphs.text: Baal-shalisha: a city that was perhaps near Gilgal.
Bread of the firstfruits: God commanded the offering of the firstfruits of the cultivated plants to Him (Lev 23:14). Full ears of corn: parched grain, which is wheat that has not completely ripened.
Husk (sack): a bag of cloth in which a man carries his belongings.

The famine was still general in the land, but God does not forget His children. A man who cared about carrying out the Law came to Elisha to offer the firstfruits of his farming, and gave the man of God twenty loaves and some parched grain for his own food. But Elisha did not care for himself but for his children, so he gave this gift to his children gathered around him, despite their great number, for he believed in the blessing of God. And as Christ blessed the two fishes and the five loaves, so also Elisha, who is a type of Christ, blessed the twenty loaves, and they fed the whole multitude.

entries.section: (6) The blessing of the twenty loaves

paragraphs.text: Gehazi wondered at his master's words, for he saw that twenty loaves would of course not suffice a hundred men, just as the disciples wondered when they found only two fishes and five loaves and said, what are they among so many? (Jn 6:9). It is human weakness, for they did not look to the power of God. But the beautiful thing is that Gehazi obeyed his master, though not convinced, and when he distributed the food Elisha's word was fulfilled, for the loaves satisfied all and some was left over, as food was left over when Christ fed the multitudes. We note God's tenderness, for He worked the miracle despite Gehazi's weak faith; God is longsuffering and does not withhold His blessings, until our faith is perfected as long as we are obedient to His commands.

Obey the commandments of God, even if they surpass your understanding, confident that God will not leave you and will provide all your needs and protect you, and will even glorify you amid the hardest circumstances, because He is your Father and He loves you.
The healing of Naaman's leprosy

entries.section: (1) Naaman is sent to the king of Israel to be healed

paragraphs.text: The king of Syria: Aram, which is Syria, whose king was called Benhadad.
Honourable (lit. lifted up of face): of great standing with the king.

Leper: afflicted with leprosy, a skin disease that appears as patches different from the color of the skin. It is closest to the disease of leprosy (Hansen's disease), but it existed only in the Old Testament and was a result of sin. The army of Aram had a commander, Naaman. He was a man loved by all, of high standing and great esteem among his people, because he was a hero, having delivered the people of Aram from invaders; he was a strong and courageous warrior, but he was a leper. His affliction with leprosy was a proof of his sin, so he represents the Gentiles fallen in sin, who will believe in Christ, as Naaman the Syrian believed after his healing at the hand of Elisha, and so be freed from their sins.

entries.section: (1) Naaman is sent to the king of Israel to be healed

paragraphs.text: In one of the raids the Arameans had made against the people of Israel, they took captive a little Israelite maid, who was given to Naaman's wife to serve her.

entries.section: (1) Naaman is sent to the king of Israel to be healed

paragraphs.text: The maid told her mistress that in Samaria there was a prophet able to heal disease, whose name was Elisha, and she wished that her master Naaman would meet Elisha and be healed of his disease. This maid, despite her young age, had learned faith at the hands of her parents from her childhood. She bore witness to the power of God in His prophet Elisha and gave the good news to her mistress and her husband, that they might believe in God in a convincing way, since their problem, the disease of leprosy, would be solved for them. She was strong in her faith, though a captive, in contrast to Naaman, who was strong in position but weak because of his sins which caused him this disease, for the disease of leprosy is connected with sin. Her faith was strong, for she was sure of Naaman's healing if he met Elisha, because she knew the miracles of Elisha and the power of God that was in him.

If we compare the faith of this maid we find it very great in comparison with Joram king of Israel, who did not believe in the power of God that was with him in Elisha the prophet and was greatly afraid when Naaman came to him, as we shall see in (v. 7). We understand from this verse that Elisha had a house in Samaria where he stayed, and from which he went out to visit his people and to which he returned, in contrast with Elijah his master, who lived in the wilderness and appeared at times to proclaim the voice of God, then returned to the wilderness. God has His many ways; He works in His children who live among people, or those who live the life of solitude in the wilderness.

Be courageous like this little maid, and let no one despise your youth or your weakness, but proclaim the truth among people and hold fast to the commandments of God, and all will see Christ dwelling in you.

entries.section: (1) Naaman is sent to the king of Israel to be healed

paragraphs.text: Talent of silver: a talent ranges between 17-40 kg of silver.
Shekel of gold: ranges between 11.3 and 11.5 grams of gold.
Changes of raiment: probably costly embroidered garments, worn by kings and the rich.

Naaman told the king of Aram what the Jewish maid had said to her mistress. The king gave him a letter of recommendation to Jehoram king of the children of Israel, and Naaman went and took with him ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold and ten changes of raiment, all as gifts.

The king of Aram sent the letter to the king of Israel, for a king addresses only a king like himself, as a kind of honor and pride; and on the other hand, because he did not know the God of Israel nor His prophet Elisha, in his eyes the greatest person was the king. But in the view of the believing maid who worked for Naaman, Elisha was the greatest person.

entries.section: (1) Naaman is sent to the king of Israel to be healed

paragraphs.text: Naaman reached Samaria and met the king of Israel and gave him the letter, in which the king of Aram addressed him, saying: When this letter is come unto thee, behold, I have therewith sent Naaman my servant to thee, that thou mayest recover him of his leprosy.

entries.section: (1) Naaman is sent to the king of Israel to be healed

paragraphs.text: When Naaman the Syrian reached Joram king of Israel and gave him the letter and he read it, he was greatly troubled and afraid, because he was unable to heal this hard disease and did not look to the power of God that he had in Elisha the prophet. His unbelief made him fear and tremble and despair, to the point that he rent his clothes as a sign of complete despair. Indeed, he felt that the sending of Naaman to him was a means of seeking a pretext to attack Israel. Elisha was beside Joram in Samaria, and Joram did not believe in the power of God that was in Elisha, while at the same time the little maid who lived far away in Aram believed and had pity on her master and moved him by faith to go and be healed by the man of God, Elisha.

entries.section: (2) Elisha heals Naaman

paragraphs.text: When man's complete helplessness appeared in the person of the king of Israel, who rent his clothes, God intervened. When Elisha heard of the king's despair, he sent to him to rebuke him for his unbelief in the power of God that was with him in the person of the prophet of God. He asked him to send Naaman to him, so that he would receive healing and know and be sure of the power of God in Israel; and I wish the king of Israel would then believe also.
Here Elisha appears as a spiritual leader solving problems when the civil leader is helpless; that is, God is the leader of the kingdom and not the king.

I wish God would be the leader of your life, so that you return to Him in everything and obey the teachings of the Church, and are not exposed to the disturbances that the world suffers, but live in constant peace.

entries.section: (2) Elisha heals Naaman

paragraphs.text: The king of Israel found in Elisha's messenger a solution to his problem, so he told Naaman that Elisha the prophet was able to heal him and that he should go to him to heal him. So Naaman went with his greatness, his chariots and horses to Elisha's simple house. This shows two things:
1- Naaman's humility, for he did not ask that Elisha come to him.
2- It shows that material greatness is nothing before the power of God, for despite Naaman's power he needed healing at the hand of the prophet of God, Elisha, the simple man.

entries.section: (2) Elisha heals Naaman

paragraphs.text: Elisha did not come out to meet Naaman but sent him a messenger telling him Elisha's command to him, to go to the Jordan River and wash seven times, and he would receive healing and be cleansed of the leprosy, which represents uncleanness. Elisha asked of him a thing contrary to reason and above it, namely washing in the Jordan River, because many people wash in it, and the Jordan River is not known to heal leprosy, especially as Elisha commanded him to wash seven times, to confirm the importance of obedience to the word of God, so he would not wash once but seven times, because obedience is the foundation of receiving the gifts of God.

If you want to solve your problems and come out of your troubles, do not be content with asking God to rescue you from them, but first obey His commandments, however strange they seem in your eyes or however unimportant you feel them to be, for they are the foundation of your deliverance from all your troubles.

entries.section: (2) Elisha heals Naaman

paragraphs.text: Strike his hand over the place: move his hands over the places of the leprosy.

Naaman was angry that Elisha did not come out to him and felt that he had treated him lightly when he sent a messenger to him, and in the intensity of his anger he went away back to his country, since he did not believe Elisha's word, namely washing in the Jordan, to receive healing.

What happened to Naaman was contrary to all his expectations, for he had thought that Elisha would come to him at the king's house and would lay his hands on the places of the leprosy and pray, and he would receive healing, because this is what happens in the pagan rites in the temples in his country. Therefore he was angry and went away.

entries.section: (2) Elisha heals Naaman

paragraphs.text: Abana and Pharpar: two rivers that pass by the city of Damascus and make the surrounding lands fertile, indeed among the most splendid lands in the world; these two rivers are now called the Barada and the A'waj.

Naaman continued his speech, wondering and angry at the word of Elisha, who had commanded him to wash in the Jordan, and said that the waters of the rivers Abana and Pharpar are abundant and strong, and if washing in river water heals, it would have been better for him to wash in the river Abana and Pharpar. He turned and went back to his country in anger and rage, because he did not believe or understand Elisha's commands to him.

entries.section: (2) Elisha heals Naaman

paragraphs.text: God intervened here by means of his servants, who loved him and had boldness with him, for they called him, "My father," and said to him that he had labored on the journey this long distance and was ready to do anything Elisha asked in order to receive healing; so why was he angry, when the prophet had asked only something easy? What harm would it do him if he obeyed his word? Naaman's humility appears in his listening to their words despite his anger, and even obeying them, as will appear in the next verse. Thus God confirms that what matters is obedience to Him and not the greatness of the works we do, for obeying His commandment, however simple it seems, gives us complete salvation.

entries.section: (2) Elisha heals Naaman

paragraphs.text: Naaman finally obeyed Elisha's commands, encouraged by his servants, and went down in humility to the waters of the Jordan and dipped in them seven times, and his leprosy departed from him and his skin returned healthy, like the skin of a little child, without any blemish. The grace of God surpasses man's request, for the most Naaman asked was that his skin become like that of other men, but he received something greater, the skin of a tender child, with a freshness and softness he did not expect, as God promises us to receive more than we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us (Eph 3:20). Naaman's obedience appears here in his dipping seven times, for until the sixth time he did not receive healing, but in the seventh time he received complete healing, so man must obey God's commands completely. The dipping in the Jordan River signifies Baptism, in which man is immersed and receives healing from his sins.

entries.section: (2) Elisha heals Naaman

paragraphs.text: A new virtue appears here in Naaman, the virtue of thanksgiving, for after he was healed he returned to Samaria to thank the man of God, though the road to his country would have been easier and quicker had he gone from the Jordan to Aram. This reminds us of the return of the leper to thank Christ, apart from the other nine, and this thanksgiving greatly rejoices the heart of God (Lk 17:12-19). We note Naaman's humility in returning to thank Elisha, though he knew that he would send a messenger to him as in (vv. 8, 10); but since Naaman believed and was cleansed of his uncleanness, he became ready to receive Elisha's blessing, and Elisha allowed him to enter to him.
Naaman declared before Elisha his faith in the God of Israel, that He is the only God, who is stronger than all the pagan gods, who could not heal him in his country.
Although Naaman had carried gifts when he came from his country, as the price of healing, now he wanted to offer them as an expression of his thanks, in humility and faith in God.

entries.section: (2) Elisha heals Naaman

paragraphs.text: Elisha swore by God that he would take nothing of Naaman's gifts. But Naaman tried, in love, to offer something of the gifts to Elisha and urged much, but the prophet insisted on taking nothing, to confirm to Naaman the power of God, which does not need his material things and gifts, and this increased Naaman's faith and humility before the man of God, who abstained from all the wealth of the world and its positions.

entries.section: (2) Elisha heals Naaman

paragraphs.text: Naaman confirms his faith in God, whom he wants to worship alone throughout his life and not worship any other pagan god. And since he felt the blessing of the man of God, who blessed the Jordan River and all the land of Israel, he asked his leave to take two mules' burden of earth from the land of Israel, that is, what two mules could carry of earth, for he felt that the whole land was holy and wanted to take some of this earth to put it on any stones or earth in his country, to offer sacrifices on it to the God of Israel. Naaman's asking leave to take the earth declares:
1- His strong faith in God, who dwells among His people and blesses even the earth of the land.
2- His courtesy and humility in asking leave to take the earth, which fills all the land of Israel.

As Naaman took care to take the blessing of the earth of the holy land, how much more ought we to care not only to receive a blessing but to partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord and so be united with Him, and this fixes our hearts on the Kingdom of Heaven, where we see Christ face to face and enjoy His fellowship forever.

entries.section: (2) Elisha heals Naaman

paragraphs.text: Rimmon: a pagan god worshipped by the Arameans, whom they call the god of rains, storms, lightning and thunder, and this god had a temple in Damascus.

Naaman thought of the situation he would certainly meet, namely his entering the temple of Rimmon the pagan god with the king and being forced to bow down with the king before this god, and this is contrary to Naaman's wish and faith. So he asked Elisha to pray for him, that God might forgive him, for he did not mean by this bowing the worship of idols, since he worshipped God only. Elisha answered Naaman to go in peace, that is, he was permitted to take the earth, and he did not object to his bowing before the god Rimmon, but at the same time he did not agree, for he left Naaman to be established in his faith in God, and then God would help him not to bow to Rimmon.

Thus we see that healing and salvation can be received by man through obeying the commandments of God, even if they are above man's reason, and by his faithfulness and carefulness in obedience, namely dipping seven times. This salvation is free from God and not in return for any gifts, but God expects the one who receives this salvation in the Church to continue in the worship of God and not worship other gods of the world such as money and position.
We also see how Naaman left his paganism and believed in God in:
1- His obedience to Elisha's commands to dip seven times in the Jordan, and so he was healed.
2- His returning to thank Elisha.
3- His declaring that God is the only God.
4- His asking leave to take of the earth of the holy land, to offer sacrifices on it to Him alone.
5- His asking forgiveness for the sin of bowing before Rimmon, for it is an outward bowing and not from his heart, because he will worship God alone.

entries.section: (3) Gehazi's treachery and punishment

paragraphs.text: After Naaman left Elisha and went some distance on his way back to his country, Gehazi, Elisha's disciple, thought of Naaman's wealth and his gifts, of which his master Elisha had taken nothing, and his heart was filled with the desire to possess and with greed, so he decided to carry out a plot to take something of these gifts.

It is strange that Gehazi did not learn from the miracles he had seen with his own eyes from Elisha his master, and did not learn from his master's abstinence, and thought about material things and left aside the spiritual riches that come from the grace of God. Elisha was truly a disciple at the hands of Elijah, but Gehazi kept evil in his heart despite his constant companionship with Elisha. It is strange that Gehazi used the spiritual words Elisha used, namely the oath by God, for he said, As the Lord liveth, but sadly used them to confirm his clinging to material desires. Gehazi represents superficiality and hypocrisy.
He reminds us of Judas Iscariot, who was a disciple at the hands of Christ and benefited nothing, because his heart was occupied with material things, until he sold his Master in the end.

By this the sin of greed appears in Gehazi, which made him make light of this new faith in Naaman's heart, so he distorted the image of God by his asking for material things and distorted the image of his abstinent master. Sin ruins in every direction.

If you have tasted the grace of God and enjoyed fellowship with Him, why do you return to fall into lust and leave God? All lusts are passing and are nothing before the grace of God. Therefore take care to practice abstinence when you live your life with God, for prayer and abstinence are not separated, that you may receive salvation.

entries.section: (3) Gehazi's treachery and punishment

paragraphs.text: In carrying out Gehazi's wicked plan he hastened, running after Naaman, to ask him for material things. When Naaman noticed this, he stopped his chariot and got down in humility and love to receive Elisha's disciple and to ask about the well-being of Elisha, and this confirms Naaman's humility and love.

entries.section: (3) Gehazi's treachery and punishment

paragraphs.text: Gehazi reassured Naaman about Elisha's well-being, then with deceit made up an imaginary story and told it to Naaman, namely the arrival of two of the sons of the prophets to Elisha after Naaman's departure. It seems that the fame of Elisha and his fatherhood and his care in hosting the sons of the prophets had reached Naaman, so he listened with attention to Gehazi's words, who pretended that his master Elisha was asking Naaman for a talent of silver and two changes of garments for the sons of the prophets whom he was hosting.
Thus we see that the sin of greed drags other sins after it, such as lying, while the abstinent man protects himself from everything.
Do not make light of it and lie to obtain your worldly desires, and do not anger God over passing things; rather, if you are satisfied with God, it will be easy for you to abstain from everything.

entries.section: (3) Gehazi's treachery and punishment

paragraphs.text: Bound: he put the two talents of silver in two bags, that is, two sacks.

Naaman welcomed the request in Elisha's name and believed Gehazi's words, and this was by the grace of God, so that Naaman, the new believer, would not stumble because of Gehazi, the deceitful, lying disciple. Then a new virtue appeared in Naaman, generosity, for he did not give as requested a talent of silver but two talents, in addition to the two changes of garments. Out of his love he sent two of his servants to carry the silver and the garments before Gehazi to Elisha's house.

entries.section: (3) Gehazi's treachery and punishment

paragraphs.text: The tower (lit. the hill): a hill.

When Gehazi and the two young men reached the hill near Elisha's house, Gehazi thanked the two young men and sent them back to their master Naaman, and took from them the silver and the garments to hide them, so that Elisha would not see him. Gehazi knew that what he was doing was sin, but sadly he insisted on it.
If God warns you that your words or actions are wrong, do not persist, but return in repentance to God and confess your sins, and He will forgive you.

entries.section: (3) Gehazi's treachery and punishment

paragraphs.text: Elisha knew, by the Spirit of God who was in him, what Gehazi had done, so he tried to help him to repent. He asked him, Whence comest thou? that he might confess his sins, as God asked Adam in the garden after he fell and said to him "Where art thou?" (Gen 3:9). But sadly Gehazi lied and said to Elisha, Thy servant went no whither, that is, he insisted on his sins and did not repent.

entries.section: (3) Gehazi's treachery and punishment

paragraphs.text: At last Elisha was forced to reveal to Gehazi his sin. He declared to him that he had been concerned for Naaman the new believer and had prayed that he not stumble because of Gehazi's sin, because he knew by the Spirit of God his greed for material things. Therefore he rebuked him for his clinging to the lust for silver and garments and his care to buy with the silver olive yards and vineyards and sheep and oxen and menservants and maidservants. That is, Elisha, by the Spirit of God, discovered Gehazi's wicked thoughts and rebuked him that this time, that is, the life we live on earth, is set apart for life with God and the service of souls, to draw them to faith. How then does Gehazi leave spiritual aims and busy himself with material things? This is against all that he learned from Elisha; he ought to have cared about Naaman's faith and not about taking his gifts.

entries.section: (3) Gehazi's treachery and punishment

paragraphs.text: In the end Elisha declared to Gehazi a punishment for his sins, that he and his seed would be struck with leprosy, because he loved sin, so its uncleanness came upon him, namely the disease of leprosy. Thus by faith man is saved and cleansed from his sins and their consequences, and if he does not keep his faith like Gehazi, he falls into sin and its consequences come upon him, namely leprosy. The leprosy came upon Gehazi's seed, perhaps so that this would move Gehazi to repentance and make his seed keep away from the sin which caused this leprosy; for the leper is saved if he repents of his sins, and leprosy does not hinder him from entering the Kingdom of Heaven.

Naaman the Syrian, his faith and his cleansing from leprosy, is a declaration before the Jews of the acceptance of the Gentiles, which Christ accomplished in the fullness of time on the Cross, and His pure Apostles preached it.
A group of sins appeared in Gehazi which caused this punishment:
1- His thinking of the lust for material things and greed.
2- His lying to Naaman, then to his master Elisha.
3- By this conduct he nearly made Naaman stumble, had it not been for Elisha's prayer.
4- His lack of care to establish Naaman's faith.
5- His persistence in sin, by hiding the stolen goods, because he took gifts without right.
6- His forgetting the power of God in his master Elisha, which is able to uncover the hidden things of Gehazi's heart.
Be careful in the life of repentance, even if you are a servant or a consecrated person, lest you fall into sin and justify yourself, and its punishment come upon you.
The Arameans' war against Samaria

entries.section: (1) The floating of the iron

paragraphs.text: Under Elisha's care and visiting of the sons of the prophets their number increased and the place where they dwelt could no longer hold them, so they thought of dwelling beside the Jordan River, where there was a spacious place, and building houses for themselves there, and it would become easy for Elisha to visit them and teach them. They asked Elisha's leave for this and he agreed. Because they were poor, they built the houses themselves and made simple houses of timber. But the most important thing is that they asked Elisha to come with them, for the most important thing was that they keep his fatherhood, care, blessing and life-giving teachings, and this confirms their care for spiritual discipleship, as it confirms Elisha's fatherhood to them.
Take care to learn from your spiritual father and receive his blessing and carry out his guidance, and God will rejoice in your obedience and bless you, and you will grow in quietness and strength.

entries.section: (1) The floating of the iron

paragraphs.text: Elisha went with them, and as soon as they reached the Jordan they began to cut down timber and gather it. Perhaps he shared the work with them, or at least directed and supervised the work, and this shows his fatherhood and his love in sharing his children's work.

entries.section: (1) The floating of the iron

paragraphs.text: Borrowed: lent.

While one of them was felling timber, the iron axe head fell into the water, and he cried out at once, calling on Elisha for help and saying that the axe that had fallen was borrowed, for he did not own it and could not pay its price to its owner, since the sons of the prophets were poor and iron was a costly metal at that time. But out of this man's love for the work and sharing in his brothers' labor, he had borrowed this axe from a friend of his, and his position became embarrassing after it fell to the bottom of the river and it was very hard to recover it. But his sense of Elisha's fatherhood made him call on him, confident that he would not leave him.

entries.section: (1) The floating of the iron

paragraphs.text: Elisha asked him where it fell, and the man showed him the place, and Elisha cut down a stick and cast it in at the same place, and the iron swam on the surface of the water. Then Elisha said to him to take it up, and he put out his hand and took it.

The stick of wood is a type of the Cross of Christ, which restored to man the pure nature that he had lost through sin. We note here that Elisha uses a material in working the miracle, namely the stick of wood, as he used before the meal and the salt; he uses tangible and visible materials to suit man's bodily senses and to assure him of the completion of the miracle. Although the miracle seems small, since this axe could be done without, Elisha cared to work the miracle for the following reasons:
1- To show his fatherhood and care for his children, for he feels their feelings and how this man was in embarrassment before his friend, from whom he had borrowed the axe.

2- To declare to the sons of the prophets their human helplessness, and that they might feel the power of God that supports them, not only in building houses for themselves but in all their life, and so rely on Him.

Elisha did not lift the iron with his own hand, but made the man put out his hand and take the floating piece of iron, to strengthen his faith in the completion of the miracle, and on the other hand to have him share in it; man ought to do his duty, even if it is small, and the difficult thing God will do for him.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: The state of Aram was a strong state, which is present-day Syria, but David the prophet subdued it to Israel, and it remained subject in the days of Solomon (1 Kgs 10:29). But afterward it began to rebel and fight the kingdom of Israel. The king of Aram at that time was called Benhadad, while the king of Israel was Joram. The king of Aram made secret plans with his servants for a surprise attack on Israel. He would set an ambush and fix a place to encamp, which no one knew except his private servants.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: Elisha used to inform the king of Israel of the place where the king of Aram would be with his army, and warn him not to approach that place, because he would have to face the Aramean army encamped there.

The king of Israel would send watchers to the place that Elisha told him of, to verify what he told him, and to make sure of the truth of what he had foretold him ... Elisha's warnings to the king were repeated many times, and King Jehoram always took heed.
By God's guidance of Elisha and his uncovering of the plans of the king of Aram, two things were accomplished:

1- A proof to the king of Israel that God is with him, by the tongue of His prophet Elisha, that he might believe and submit and repent of his sins, namely the worship of idols. But sadly, although the king of Israel verified the truth of Elisha's word, which protected him from every ambush the king of Aram set, he did not repent of his sins and leave the idols. It is certain that Elisha had warned him much to leave the idols.

2- By this He declared to the king of Aram the power of God in His people Israel, that perhaps he might believe in God and leave his idols, especially after the event of the healing of the commander of his army from leprosy (ch. 5).

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: Which of us is for the king of Israel: who is a spy for the king of Israel.
The king of Aram was troubled by this matter, so he gathered his commanders and asked them to uncover the person among them who was plotting against him for the benefit of the king of Israel.

The king of Aram suspected treachery within his ranks, while the idea of God's intervention was always outside his thinking. So the world also thinks, ascribing the events of life to various causes, more than they see the hand of God in all of them.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: One of his commanders answered him that it was not so, that there was no traitor plotting against the king for the benefit of the king of Aram, but that Elisha the prophet, who is in Israel, has all the secrets revealed to him by God and tells the king of Israel the most precise details of the plans that the king of Aram lays in the greatest secrecy, even in his bedchamber. It is strange that the king of Aram did not understand for himself the power of God that was in Elisha, despite the healing of the commander of his army, Naaman, from leprosy at Elisha's hand; but one of the servants of the king of Aram understood this truth and drew the king's attention to it. Perhaps this private servant close to the king was his army commander Naaman, with whom the miracle happened, who believed in God and in His prophet Elisha.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: Dothan: a town near Shechem (Nablus). Its place today is a deserted mound called "Tell Dothan," about eighteen kilometers east of Samaria.

Because the king of Aram did not believe in God, he thought that Elisha was like one of the sorcerers, so that if he seized him and took him to his kingdom he could deprive the king of Israel of his guidance, and the king of Aram himself would use him, and he would guide him in his war plans. He did not understand that Elisha is the voice of God, who knows everything and supports only those who believe in Him, and hates evil and the worship of idols; he did not even understand that his power is nothing before the power of God that is in Elisha, and thought it easy to seize him, for he was merely a man. But he will learn, as will appear in the following verses, the irresistible power of God.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: A great host (lit. heavy): that is, large, armed and trained for fighting.

The king of Aram sent a huge military force which reached Dothan by night and surrounded the city, for he felt that Elisha was a great sorcerer who needed great force, so that he might not escape them by his cunning and sorcery. Here he reminds us of the sending of many forces and soldiers to seize Christ in the garden of Gethsemane, though He was one unarmed person.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: Early the next morning, when Elisha's servant rose and went out and looked around, behold, an army surrounded the city. The servant was alarmed and ran to his master to tell him how they should act in facing this great army. This shows the weakness of the servant's faith, which is completely different from the faith of his master Elisha, for he was alarmed when he heard the sound of the horses and chariots and rose early to see them, and so his fear and despair increased.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: Elisha reassured his disciple, saying: "Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them," because the faith of mighty Elisha made him trust in the power of God that supports him, then he saw the heavens filled with hosts of angels, so his faith was strengthened and he reassured his disciple.

Fear not. This word is repeated often in the books of the Old and New Testaments. It is repeated constantly so that the believer besieged by difficulties and sorrows may be certain of the Lord's intervention by the working of His grace.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: Elisha prayed and asked the Lord to open his servant's eyes that he might see. The Lord opened the servant's eyes, and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about them. We see here that Elisha's intercession for his disciple gave him grace to see this vision. We note that it is of the same kind as the Aramean army surrounding the city (v. 14), that is, chariots and horses, but of fire, that is, heavenly and immeasurably stronger than human soldiers and earthly chariots, so that the servant might be completely reassured; as for Elisha, he was assured even without seeing this vision, because of his strong faith.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: When the army of Aram advanced toward Elisha, he prayed to the Lord, asking that the members of this army all be struck with blindness. The Lord answered Elisha's prayer and smote them with blindness. Thus we see Elisha's courage and great faith, which made him go down himself in assurance because God was with him, to meet these great armies. When the armies saw a person advancing toward them, since they were standing on a high place, they came down to him, and in the meantime Elisha prayed that God smite them with blindness, not because he was afraid of them, but that they might know that the power of God surpasses all human power, and perhaps they would understand that their pagan life far from God is error and blindness, and realize that there is a power in the people of God to which they must submit, namely the power of God, the only God above all gods.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: Elisha advanced toward the blind army. The blindness here was not complete, according to the interpretation of the original Greek word, for it does not mean the complete loss of sight but the loss of the ability to distinguish, to distinguish persons and things, that is, a great weakness of sight, and this of course made all the Aramean warriors feel their weakness, so they were easily led by the word of the man who spoke to them, who was Elisha, though they did not know him. He said to them, This is not the way, neither is this the city, meaning that it was not the way God had chosen nor the city God wanted them to reach. He promised them that he would bring them to the man whom they sought, that is, Elisha, so they were reassured, and because of their weakness they submitted, and he led them on the road to Samaria, which is about eighteen kilometers from Dothan, that is, they walked several hours until they reached Samaria with Elisha.

Elisha did not want to destroy them by the power of God, or to send them back to their country in this weakness, but wanted to declare to them the power of God which they did not know, so he led them to the capital of the kingdom of Israel, which is Samaria. There, when they would find themselves surrounded by the soldiers of the children of Israel, he forgave them and fed them, so that they might feel the power of God in Elisha, who was able to destroy them but forgave them, that perhaps they would believe in his powerful and merciful God.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: Elisha reached Samaria with the army of the Arameans and brought them into the great square in the city, and the armies of the children of Israel gathered to surround this strange blind army. Then Elisha prayed, and the eyes of the Aramean army were opened, and they were surprised to find themselves in the midst of Samaria, surrounded by the armies of the children of Israel, and that Elisha stood before them and that he was the one who had led them all this way from Dothan to Samaria. They were very afraid and trembled, whether at the power of the man of God who had led them on the way and now stood before them, or at the power of the armies around them. Elisha did not threaten them, but the power of God in him troubled them. He is a type here of Christ at His arrest, how the soldiers feared Him when He told them that He was the Christ, and they fell on their faces from fear (Jn 18:6). They did not know what Elisha would do with them, whether he would torture them, or kill them, or ....

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: When Joram king of Israel saw all that had happened in the midst of Samaria, he believed in the power of God in Elisha and felt like a little child before his father and did not know what to do. So he asked Elisha, My father, shall I smite them? Shall I smite them? That is, he would command his armies to destroy them.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: Elisha forbade Joram to harm any of the Arameans. He said to him, You have not fought and taken captive these enemies that you should kill them, but this army has come in peace to our city, so they are our guests and we ought to honor them. So he offered them a feast to eat and drink, for they were tired from traveling on foot from Dothan to Samaria. These words have many effects, which are:

1- It shows Elisha's love for his enemies; they tried to seize him and he honors them and entertains them. He carried out the commandment "Love your enemies," which Christ said hundreds of years before He said it (Mt 5:44).
2- It is a lesson for the king of Israel and all the people of God in loving enemies, pardon and forgiveness.
3- He gave a lesson in hospitality to strangers, even if they are enemies.

4- A lesson the Arameans will not forget in knowing the power of the God of Israel, who is able to destroy them, for He smote them with blindness, and at the same time forgives them and even entertains them, so they feel the weakness of their gods, who did not protect them from this great God. At the same time they come to this merciful God, who entertained them and fed them, that perhaps they would finally believe in God.
5- They would feel the uselessness of human plans and of their king's cleverness in trying to seize Elisha, for all this is nothing before the power of God.

entries.section: (2) The attempt to seize Elisha

paragraphs.text: The king of Israel carried out Elisha's command, and prepared a feast for them, and they ate and drank, then he sent them away free, and they returned to their king. Because of this the armies of Aram refrained from invading Israel for a period of time.

entries.section: (3) The Arameans besiege Samaria

paragraphs.text: Samaria: it was the capital of the kingdom of Israel, which worshipped God but at the same time worshipped idols. Since God was angry with it, God allowed it the siege and the famine.

Peace with the king of Aram did not last a long time. The king of Aram forgot Israel's kindness to his army, when Elisha forgave them and fed them, so Benhadad king of Aram gathered his army and advanced toward Samaria and besieged it. This siege caused a severe famine. It is strange that Elisha feeds the Arameans, while the king of Aram besieges Samaria to put it into a severe famine. Why do we forget the kindness of others to us?!

entries.section: (3) The Arameans besiege Samaria

paragraphs.text: Because of the length and harshness of the siege a famine came upon the city and prices rose to unbearable limits. An ass's head was sold for fourscore pieces of silver (four hundred and sixty grams) and the fourth part of a cab (half a liter) of dove's dung for five pieces of silver (thirty grams). From this we understand that if the ass, which is not eaten, was at this price, the animals that are eaten would be far dearer. The famine was something God had announced beforehand to His people in the Law of Moses, that when they turned away from Him, by their worship of idols, they would be exposed to famines as discipline for them (Deut 28:56, 57).

entries.section: (3) The Arameans besiege Samaria

paragraphs.text: The wall: it was broad, so that a number of men walked on it, and a parapet was built on it to protect those who passed on it from the enemy's arrows.
While the king of Israel was inspecting his forces, passing along the wall of the city, a woman cried out to the king for help, saying, "Help, my lord, O king."

entries.section: (3) The Arameans besiege Samaria

paragraphs.text: Barnfloor: the place where grain is gathered after harvesting, and it is called the threshing floor.
Winepress: where grapes are pressed and the juice is turned into wine, or olives are pressed to give oil.

The king answered this woman who cried out to him, that if God did not save her by lifting the siege and removing the famine, how could he save her, or from where could he bring her food? From the barnfloor empty of any grain, or from the winepress which had no grape juice?

entries.section: (3) The Arameans besiege Samaria

paragraphs.text: Then the king asked her what ailed her, and she answered: A woman said, Give thy son, that we may eat him to day, and we will eat my son tomorrow. This shows the extent of the brutality to which the people had come, as a result of their worship of idols, for at hunger they lost the feelings of motherhood, which is a natural instinct, and their hands reached out to eat their children, in a cruelty beyond expression, because they had been accustomed, to please the gods, to offer their children as sacrifices to the idols.

entries.section: (3) The Arameans besiege Samaria

paragraphs.text: She told the king how the two had agreed to eat their children, so they boiled the first woman's child and ate him, then when the turn of the second mother came, she hid her child. The first woman asked the king to do her justice and to command the second woman to give her her child, that they might eat him as they had agreed. It is a disturbing story, which shows the violence of the famine, which disturbs the king, or any person who hears it.

entries.section: (3) The Arameans besiege Samaria

paragraphs.text: When the king heard the woman's words he rent his clothes as he was inspecting the wall, and his men around him saw that he had sackcloth upon his flesh, for the king could not bear what his people had come to in brutality as a result of the famine. The rending of clothes was a well-known Eastern custom and still exists in some countries such as Upper Egypt. The king's wearing sackcloth shows the extent of his grief and his supplication to God, but sadly he did not remove the idols, so his heart was still not upright before God, though he was grieved because of the famine. Perhaps the king's wearing sackcloth underneath was intended to hide his grief so as not to grieve his people.

entries.section: (3) The Arameans besiege Samaria

paragraphs.text: God do so and more also to me: an oath meaning that he must carry out what he says or else God will bring many afflictions upon him.
The head of Elisha shall stand on him: that is, he will cut off his head.

It seems that Elisha had rebuked Jehoram king of Israel for his worship of idols and threatened him that if he did not repent of this, his land would be exposed to famine, as God commanded in (Deut 28:56, 57). Perhaps the king of Israel had asked Elisha to lift the siege and remove the famine, and Elisha did not pray for it to be lifted until God's discipline was completed and they repented of the worship of idols. The king may have been accusing Elisha of not removing the famine, as being able to do so, though the king had not asked him but sees the famine and keeps silent and does nothing.

For all this, when the king of Israel felt the harshness of the famine, to the point that mothers eat their children, he was very angry, and instead of returning in repentance to God that He might lift the distress from him, he decided that the cause of the famine was Elisha and declared that he would kill him that day. This means Jehoram's immersion in evil and condemnation, for the famine showed the hardness of his heart and his insistence on the worship of idols, and consequently his deserving of this discipline.

When distresses meet you, know that they are by God's permission, and examine yourself, for perhaps there is a sin within that is the cause of this distress; repent of it and do not throw the blame on others, or circumstances, and then you gain your soul and are delivered from every evil and receive God's mercies.

entries.section: (3) The Arameans besiege Samaria

paragraphs.text: Hold the door fast: prevent him from entering, by shutting the door in his face, so that he is forced to stand before the door.

When Jehoram (Joram) declared that he would kill Elisha that day, Elisha was sitting in his house with a group of the elders of Israel around him, and God informed him of what the king intended, namely to kill him. So he said to the elders sitting around him, King Jehoram has sent a messenger to kill me now, and the king will follow this messenger; therefore Elisha asked one of his men to shut the door of the house, so that the king's messenger would not enter and kill him. He called King Jehoram the son of a murderer, because his father King Ahab had killed Naboth the Jezreelite. Elisha was not afraid of the king's messenger who was coming to kill him, but waited for the king to arrive, because Jehoram, after commanding Elisha's killing, repented and followed his messenger to prevent him from killing Elisha; and Elisha also waited for the king to arrive so as to declare the word of God before the king.

entries.section: (3) The Arameans besiege Samaria

paragraphs.text: While Elisha was speaking to the elders and telling them of the king's intention to kill him by means of a messenger coming to the house and told them, Shut the door, the messenger actually reached the door and found it shut and remained standing until the king caught up with him, and the king prevented his messenger from trying to kill Elisha. Here Elisha commanded the door to be opened and went out to meet King Jehoram and his messenger, and then the king declared his rebellion against God and his despair of escape from the hands of the Arameans, and perhaps he had even decided to surrender the city to the Arameans; so the king said that this evil, that is, the famine, is of the Lord, and that he would not wait for deliverance from the Lord, because Elisha His prophet does not move to rescue the situation. Thus the king reached complete despair. Here the grace of God will intervene to announce the solution and deliverance, after man's complete helplessness, and God is longsuffering toward this wicked king and his people who still worship idols, and rescues them from death, that perhaps they would believe and repent. This is what we shall see at the beginning of the next chapter in the first two verses. And if man, like Jehoram (Joram), throws the blame on God when a trial comes upon him, God bears with him and rescues him from the trial, that perhaps he will take heed to the cause of the trial and know that it is discipline from God, that he may repent of his sins. The lifting of the siege and the end of the famine

entries.section: (1) Elisha's prophecy of the end of the famine

paragraphs.text: Shekel: a shekel of gold, equal to about 11.3-11.6 grams.

After the king declared his helplessness and expected evil, namely the surrender of the city and death for himself and his men, God intervened through the mouth of His prophet Elisha to announce a solution that no one had expected. Elisha prophesied, in front of the king and his messenger, in front of the elders who were gathered with him, and in front of all the sons of the prophets who served with him, with the word of the Lord, that about this time tomorrow flour and barley would be available in abundance, so that their prices would fall enormously, and a measure of fine flour would be sold for a shekel, and likewise two measures of barley for a shekel, in the market of Samaria.

entries.section: (1) Elisha's prophecy of the end of the famine

paragraphs.text: Windows: the plural of a window (kuwwa), meaning an opening.

The king and all who were present heard Elisha's words and marveled. Some believed, and some were troubled by a measure of doubt. But the king's own officer, who was the king's bodyguard and adviser and on whom the king leaned as he walked, when he heard Elisha's prophecy about the end of the famine, scoffed at the prophet's words and said mockingly, "Behold, if the LORD would make windows in heaven, might this thing be?" Elisha answered him that he would see it happen but, as a punishment for his mockery, would not eat of it, that is, of the flour and barley that would be found in abundance. The king did not believe Elisha's prophecy, as is clear from (v. 12), but he kept silent; this officer, however, mocked the word of God, and so he deserved the divine punishment, namely death.

Elisha's words were illogical, for if good came upon the whole city, the first to receive of it would be the king, then his aide and personal guard on whom he leaned. But God's judgments surpass all reason, and He punishes the scoffers and blesses His humble children.

The Lord is very long-suffering toward sinners, but there is no salvation for those who scoff at His word. They exist today as they have in every age; they show unbelief and argue, and the word of God is vain in their eyes. Their destruction is certain. May you reject the thoughts of doubt that Satan casts into your mind against the promises of God, or the sacraments of the Church, or any spiritual blessings you can receive from the holy children of God, so that you do not lose the many graces that God wants to give you.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: There were four leprous men at the entrance of the city gate, talking together, and one of them urged them to take a positive step that would settle the matter, instead of resigning themselves to death by hunger.

These lepers were outcasts; because of their uncleanness they lived outside the camp, that is, outside the city, so that no one would become unclean by touching them. The people of the city used to throw them some food. When the famine became severe, no one threw them any food at all, and they were close to dying of hunger. So they began to think positively about a solution to the problem for themselves, and after that for the rest of the city, as we shall see in the following verses. God uses these lepers to solve the problem of the city, as we shall see.

Do not despise any person, however lowly he may seem, or weak, or rejected by people, for he is the image of God, and God is able to work through him and in him, giving you good by his means, and you may learn many things from him.

The severe distress that these four lepers suffered, being kept away from other people and exposed to death by hunger, made them look for a solution. A severe crisis that brings a person close to death makes him think of a positive solution. So do not be alarmed if the affliction increases and becomes unbearable, for this may be the beginning of the solution of the problem.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: The four lepers began to talk together and said that if we try to enter the city of Samaria and break the law that requires us to stay away from the cities because of our leprosy, we will find no food and will die of hunger; and if we stay where we are outside the city, we will also die of hunger. One of them made a suggestion: that they go over to the Arameans and surrender to them. If the Arameans accepted them, they would save their lives, live and find food; and if they killed them as enemies, so be it, since death would overtake them by any means. In this way God put this courage in them, so that they might save themselves and also their city. They did not give in to death and despair but moved, hoping to find life. Jewish tradition says that the four lepers were Gehazi and his sons; and since Gehazi knew God, perhaps he prayed and God guided him to this idea, so that he might save himself and his city.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: Twilight: that is, the evening, the time of sunset just before darkness.
The uttermost part of the camp of the Arameans: the farthest end of the Aramean camp, the part toward the city of Samaria.

The rest of the lepers approved their companion's suggestion, agreed to it and decided to carry it out. When evening came they arose and went to the camp of the Arameans, but they found not a single soldier there; the camp was completely empty of Arameans.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: The Holy Bible explains why the Aramean camp was empty of all the soldiers: they had heard the noise of chariots and horses, that is, the noise of a great army advancing against them. The noise was powerful because it was from God. So they thought that the king of Israel had hired against them the kings of the Hittites, who lived in the north of the Levant, that is, present-day Syria, and the kings of the Egyptians, for Egypt was at that time divided into more than one part, each part having a king. What the Arameans thought was illogical, for how could the king of Israel hire against them strong armies like these while he was besieged inside his city? But just as God had closed their eyes with blindness before Elisha, now He closes their minds, so that they imagine strange, frightening things and flee quickly, leaving all their possessions behind them.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: This conclusion terrified the soldiers of the Aramean army, for they imagined that they were certainly defeated. So they left their camp, their horses and their donkeys as they were, and fled to save their lives.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: When the four lepers found the camp quiet, with no one in it, they took courage and entered one of the tents at the edge of the camp. They found much food in it, and they ate and drank; then they took the silver, the clothing and everything of value that was in it, and went out, and dug a hole and hid the spoil in it. Then they returned to the Aramean camp and entered a second tent, took what was in it, went away, dug in the ground and hid what they had taken. And when they felt that they stood before a great treasure, they took from it as much as they were able to carry.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: After taking spoil from the two tents, the four lepers realized that before them was a camp full of tents, with much spoil inside them and around them. So they came to themselves and said that it was not right to delay bringing the good news to our brethren in Samaria, so that they too might come and eat and take much spoil. They decided to hurry to tell the king during the night, so that no harm would come to them, for if morning came the king might be angry with them for their delay in telling him. All the more would God be angry with them for neglecting to bring the good news to their brethren and sinking into selfishness, so that they did not feel their brethren's hunger. It is a beautiful thing that they hurried to tell the guards standing before the king's house; for delaying to bring good news to others and to make them glad is a grave matter that angers God.

And if these lepers were Gehazi and his sons, then Gehazi moved from the greed and selfishness that marked him in the story of Naaman, when he took gifts, to sensitivity toward others, feeling their needs and caring that they should share in God's grace and blessings, so that they might come out of hunger and be satisfied, and even enjoy abundance.

Take care to look after those around you spiritually and to encourage them to attach themselves to the Church, so that they may taste the sweetness of fellowship with God and you may win them for Christ. And be careful to taste first, yourself, fellowship with God in the Church, through the sacraments and the means of grace, so that when you have experienced the power of God within you, you may move with zeal to call others to be joined to God. So it was with the lepers: they ate and were satisfied, and their hearts were moved with love toward their brethren, and they hurried to bring them the good news, so that they too might go out and eat and take spoil.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: The four lepers came to the gate of the city of Samaria but did not enter, because entry was forbidden to them on account of their leprosy. So they called to the porter of the city, who, when he heard their shouting, opened the gate and came out to them. They told him that they had entered the camp of the Arameans and had found no one there, not a single soldier, but had found horses and donkeys tied and tents still standing with all their contents.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: The porter of the city told his fellow porters at the city gate, and sent word to the porters of the king's house during the night, charging them to tell the king. So they spoke to those in charge inside the house and informed the king of what had happened.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: When the king heard, he did not believe that the power of God had driven out the Arameans so that they left their possessions and fled, and that thereby the prophecy of the prophet Elisha was being fulfilled. Instead, with his reason, he doubted what had happened and thought it a trick of the Arameans, who had left their tents and hidden in one of the fields to ambush the people of Samaria, so that if they came out to take the spoil, the Arameans would fall upon them and kill them, then storm the city and occupy it. This doubting speech, if we examine it closely, is not logical. For although ambush in war was common and well known in those times, there are things that prevent this supposition, namely:
1- The people of Samaria were in great fear, so how would they dare to send spies to the camp of the Arameans? Of course they would not go out, lest they die.
2- The people of Samaria were in severe hunger and were almost surrendering, as the king showed in (ch. 25, 33); so the Arameans had no need to devise new plans to bring the city down.

Using your reason more than is proper makes you fall into distress, so that you refuse to believe the promises of God, because His promises surpass reason. So obey God's commandments, trusting in His power that supports you, that you may enjoy inexpressible blessings.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: When one of the king's servants and advisers saw the king's doubt, he offered a suggestion to make sure whether or not there was an ambush. He said: let us look for five horses that may have remained in the city, since the rest of the horses have died of hunger, or have become weak and unable to walk, or have been eaten by the people of the city; let us send them with their chariots and soldiers to the camp of the Arameans, that they may make sure that no one is in the camp and that there is no ambush. If they live and return to us, they are like all the multitude of the living in the city, and they will bring joyful news, and these living ones will live by the spoil they take. But if the Arameans rise against them and kill them, they will be like the multitude of people and horses that have died. That is, his suggestion was to send spies, or emissaries, to make sure there was no ambush.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: Their haste: their hurrying.

Indeed, two chariots with horses were prepared, and they set out with the soldiers in them until they reached the camp of the Arameans, which was empty of soldiers. Then they continued on, searching for the Arameans, until they reached the river Jordan. They noticed that the road was full of garments and vessels that the Arameans had thrown away in their flight, out of their fear and panic, as their aim was to cross the river Jordan and hurry back to their own country. The distance between Samaria and the river Jordan is great, and this shows the extent of the Arameans' terror, which lasted a long time, until they returned to their country. Most likely God made them hear the sound of armies pursuing them, so that they fled and returned to their country. And the messengers told the king all that they had seen.

entries.section: (2) The lifting of the siege and the flight of the Arameans

paragraphs.text: The hungry people went out and plundered the contents of the Aramean camp; they ate and were satisfied and possessed much spoil. In this the prophecy of Elisha was fulfilled, for a measure of fine flour became a shekel and two measures of barley a shekel, exactly as the Lord had spoken through the mouth of His prophet.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: The king made sure that the Aramean camp was empty of soldiers and that there was spoil and much food, and the news spread through the city. There was great joy among all the people, who had almost died of hunger, and they grew strong and hurried to plunder food, to eat and to live. The king hurried to organize the movement out of the city, lest the people trample one another in their eagerness for food in order to live. He sent his personal guard, that is, the officer on whom he used to lean when he walked, and most likely a group of soldiers was with him, to organize the going out of the people. This guard rejoiced, and at the same time was ashamed because of his mockery of the word of God, spoken through the mouth of His prophet Elisha, when he stood with the king at the door of the prophet's house. The guard tried to organize the going out as much as he could, but the rush of the hungry people was greater than any imagining, so that they threw this guard to the ground and trampled him under their feet, and he died, and perhaps others of the people also fell and died. Thus Elisha's word was fulfilled, that this officer would see the fulfillment of the word of God in the abundance of food but would not eat of it, because he would be dead.

Do not challenge God and reject His word. Even if doubts war against you, resist them, for who are you that you should rebel against God? The mercy of God comes upon the weak, but it rejects the scoffers and the rebellious, who receive nothing but divine wrath.
The return of the Shunammite, and the reigns of Hazael, Jehoram and Ahaziah. (1) The Shunammite recovers her land (vv. 1-6)

1- Then spake Elisha unto the woman, whose son he had restored to life, saying, Arise, and go thou and thine household, and sojourn wheresoever thou canst sojourn: for the LORD hath called for a famine; and it shall also come upon the land seven years. 2- And the woman arose, and did after the saying of the man of God: and she went with her household, and sojourned in the land of the Philistines seven years. 3- And it came to pass at the seven years' end, that the woman returned out of the land of the Philistines: and she went forth to cry unto the king for her house and for her land. 4- And the king talked with Gehazi the servant of the man of God, saying, Tell me, I pray thee, all the great things that Elisha hath done. 5- And it came to pass, as he was telling the king how he had restored a dead body to life, that, behold, the woman, whose son he had restored to life, cried to the king for her house and for her land. And Gehazi said, My lord, O king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life. 6- And when the king asked the woman, she told him. So the king appointed unto her a certain officer, saying, Restore all that was hers, and all the fruits of the field since the day that she left the land, even until now.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Elisha still appreciated the kindness of the Shunammite woman who had hosted him in her house.
