After giving her a son and then raising him from the dead, he now grants her a favor by telling her of a famine that would come upon the land of Canaan for seven years. He advised her to sojourn in another country. Most likely her husband had died, so she had to lead her household, that is, her son and her servants, and go to a place where there was no famine.

It should be noted that this famine prevailed over the whole land of Canaan and is different from the limited famine that occurred in Samaria when the Arameans besieged it. The problem was greater and would last seven years, so God took care to provide for His children during it. Perhaps this was a discipline from God, so that His people would repent and turn back from the worship of idols.

Elisha's concern to advise the Shunammite to sojourn abroad was necessary, because the Shunammite was most likely a widow and wealthy, and in famines there is disorder, plundering of property and killing. Because of her wealth, the Shunammite was exposed to being killed and having her possessions plundered.

God's gifts to His special children are many, and He cares for them more than for the rest of people, so that they may rely on Him and devote themselves to loving Him. So do not worry about tomorrow, and trust that God will provide for it for you; live today with God in prayers and meditations, and you will enjoy Him, for He loves you.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: The Shunammite obeyed Elisha's command, because she believed the word of God spoken through His prophet, and she went to the land of the Philistines, which lies south of the land of the Jews and was not struck by the famine. That is why Elisha agreed that she should sojourn there.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: When the seven years ended, the woman returned to her homeland from the land of the Philistines, where she had taken refuge during the famine, but she was surprised to find that others had taken possession of her property, the house and the field. So she went to the king to complain.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: At that time the king had summoned Gehazi, Elisha's servant, and asked him to tell him all the miracles that had been done by Elisha. Two things are understood from this:

1- That the king knew that the power of God was in Elisha, so he showed interest in hearing the stories of his miracles, even though he did not carry out Elisha's teachings and still worshiped idols and did not obey God's commandments. He represents the person who wants to know information about God but does not submit to it.

2- That Gehazi was near the king. Either the king had summoned him before the leprosy of Naaman came upon him, that is, before he was struck with leprosy, or he had tried to honor him after his bringing the good news of the Aramean camp and the spoil. It appears from the stories of Gehazi that he benefited from being Elisha's disciple, for he now teaches and proclaims the word of God.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: The wonderful providence of God appears here. He made the king summon Gehazi to hear from him the miracles of Elisha; then Gehazi tells some of the miracles, and the king's heart is drawn to love Elisha and his works; then he tells the story of the Shunammite and the raising of her son; then God allows the Shunammite to come to the king at that very time to appeal to him to rescue her and restore to her her land and the property taken from her, which people had seized during the seven years of her absence. The king was eager for the story and attached to it, and his attachment grew because, when the Shunammite woman came in to cry to the king to rescue her, Gehazi said to the king, "This is the woman I am telling you about, and this is her son, who died and whom Elisha raised." The king rejoiced and became eager to know more details from the woman of the story, and ready to grant any request she made, because of his admiration for her faith, her love and her generosity.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: The king asked the woman to tell him her story with Elisha, and she related to him greater details, which increased his admiration for her and for Elisha. When he heard her problem and the seizure of her land, he was ready to fulfill all her requests, so he hurried to restore her rights and gave her one of his servants, one of the eunuchs who worked for him, to restore to her, by the king's command, her land and all her property, and even all the produce that the land had yielded during the seven years, or its equivalent in silver and gold. From this we see several things:
1- God gave the woman more than she asked: she asked for the land, and God gives her the produce as well for the whole seven years.
2- The king is an instrument in God's hand, with which He does what He wills for the good of His children (Prov 21:1).

3- The land did produce during the famine, but its yield was meager and not enough for the people's food. This means that the Shunammite was exposed to people attacking her to take the produce of her land and to harm her, and God rescued her by her sojourn in Philistia.
(2) Hazael seizes the throne of Aram (vv. 7-15)

7- And Elisha came to Damascus; and Benhadad the king of Syria was sick; and it was told him, saying, The man of God is come hither. 8- And the king said unto Hazael, Take a present in thine hand, and go, meet the man of God, and enquire of the LORD by him, saying, Shall I recover of this disease? 9- So Hazael went to meet him, and took a present with him, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels' burden, and came and stood before him, and said, Thy son Benhadad king of Syria hath sent me to thee, saying, Shall I recover of this disease? 10- And Elisha said unto him, Go, say unto him, Thou mayest certainly recover: howbeit the LORD hath shewed me that he shall surely die.

11- And he settled his countenance stedfastly, until he was ashamed: and the man of God wept. 12- And Hazael said, Why weepeth my lord? And he answered, Because I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel: their strong holds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their children, and rip up their women with child. 13- And Hazael said, But what, is thy servant a dog, that he should do this great thing? And Elisha answered, The LORD hath shewed me that thou shalt be king over Syria. 14- So he departed from Elisha, and came to his master; who said to him, What said Elisha to thee? And he answered, He told me that thou shouldest surely recover. 15- And it came to pass on the morrow, that he took a thick cloth, and dipped it in water, and spread it on his face, so that he died: and Hazael reigned in his stead.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Elisha went to Damascus to fulfill what God had commanded Elijah in (1 Kgs 19:15), which was to anoint Hazael king over Aram. Although he did not anoint him, he declared to him that he would be king, because Hazael would become a Gentile king and persecute the people of God, so Elisha's coming was to meet Hazael and warn him of what he would do. God warns all people, righteous and wicked, so that all are without excuse before Him if they do evil, and so that He may give everyone an opportunity to repent.

Elisha the man of God was openly visible and not hidden, so when he reached Damascus, King Benhadad learned of his arrival. Benhadad was a general name for the kings of Aram, and it means "worshiper of the sun." This Benhadad was the one who sent Naaman to Elisha to be healed, and he was also the one who besieged Samaria, so he was wicked; yet he knew the power of Elisha, and because he was sick and weak, he longed for the man of God to heal him, or at least to prophesy to him of recovery.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: King Benhadad commanded one of his commanders, Hazael, to take a present and go to welcome Elisha and ask him to inquire of the Lord whether he, that is, Benhadad, would recover from his illness and regain his health. Perhaps Benhadad wanted by this present to honor Elisha so that he would prophesy his recovery, and forgot that this was the man of God, who speaks only the word of God and is not swayed by gifts, since he had not accepted the gifts of Naaman, whom he healed.

It is remarkable that Benhadad, the pagan king, inquires of God by means of His prophet Elisha, while Ahaziah king of Israel inquired of Baal-zebub to prophesy his recovery to him; therefore the divine sentence of death came upon him, and Ahaziah died in the days of Elijah (2 Kgs 1:2).

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Hazael carried out King Benhadad's command. He gathered of all the good things for which Damascus is famous, put them on forty camels, and came to Elisha, delivering to him the king's message and asking him to tell him whether he, that is, Benhadad, would recover from his illness or not.
The sending of this great present, carried on forty camels, means the following:
1- The wealth and power of King Benhadad.

2- His esteem for Elisha, especially since he called him father and considered him a father, saying "thy son Benhadad," as the kings of Israel call him. This is a great honor to the prophet of God, but unfortunately it was not accompanied by faith in God and a change of his conduct, for he still worshiped idols, and even compelled Naaman, the commander of his army, to share in this worship.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Elisha told Hazael God's answer to Benhadad's question about his recovery: that God tells him he will recover. But Elisha completed his words, saying that Benhadad would die, not from the illness but for another reason, which we shall learn from the following verses, for Hazael would kill him (v. 15).

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: After Elisha told Hazael God's answer, Elisha looked at Hazael with a strong and searching gaze and continued looking at him for a while. During this Hazael felt the power of the man of God and that he knew the hidden things of hearts by the power of God, that is, he knew the hardness of his heart and his intention to kill King Benhadad in order to reign in his place, so that Hazael was ashamed, because his evil intentions had been exposed before Elisha.
After this Elisha wept, and Hazael was greatly astonished and afraid and wondered why the mighty man of God was weeping.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Hazael asked him the reason for his weeping, and he told him the reason: that by the spirit of prophecy he knew what would happen in days to come, and the evil that would befall Israel at the hands of Hazael, when he would burn their strongholds with fire, kill their soldiers with the sword, destroy their children and rip up their women with child.

Hazael pretended humility and submission to Elisha and denied that he would ever do harm to the children of Israel; he even described himself as contemptible, like a dog, and too insignificant to do these great evils. But in truth his heart was hard and selfish, loving itself and hating the people of God, though he feared Elisha the man of God.
Elisha went on with his warning to Hazael by telling him prophetically that he would become king over Aram and would use his authority and his army to commit these atrocities.
God's warnings come in succession and continually to caution you against evil, so do not treat them lightly and reject the word of God, but return to Him in repentance, and you will gain your soul.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Hazael returned from Elisha to the palace of his master Benhadad, who immediately asked him what Elisha had told him. He answered him briefly, saying that he would recover from his illness, and he did not tell him the rest of the prophecy, that he would die after his recovery. So Hazael was a liar, for half the truth is not the truth.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Thick cloth: a piece of wool used either as a cover or as a rug.

It appears that on the following day Benhadad began to recover and be healed of his illness, as Elisha had prophesied to him. Hazael felt that Benhadad would not die, so he advanced with brutality and treachery and took the thick cloth, dipped it in water and put it on the face of Benhadad, whose body was weak because of the illness, and stifled his breath, since a wet cloth prevents air from getting through. So Benhadad actually died. Then Hazael announced that the king had died, as though he had died of his illness, and set himself up as king over Aram. As a military commander with authority, he was able, by means of the soldiers loyal to him, to proclaim himself king.
(3) Jehoram reigns over Judah (vv. 16-24)

16- And in the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, Jehoshaphat being then king of Judah, Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign. 17- Thirty and two years old was he when he began to reign; and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. 18- And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab: for the daughter of Ahab was his wife: and he did evil in the sight of the LORD. 19- Yet the LORD would not destroy Judah for David his servant's sake, as he promised him to give him alway a light, and to his children. 20- In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves. 21- So Joram went over to Zair, and all the chariots with him: and he rose by night, and smote the Edomites which compassed him about, and the captains of the chariots: and the people fled into their tents. 22- Yet Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day. Then Libnah revolted at the same time. 23- And the rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? 24- And Joram slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David: and Ahaziah his son reigned in his stead.

Note: These nine verses, 16-24, are a brief description of the period of the reign of Jehoram king of Judah. A fuller account of this king's reign is found in the whole of 2 Chronicles chapter 21, that is, verses 1 to 20.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: It is noticed that Jehoram king of Judah began to reign in the fifth year of King Joram (Jehoram) king of Israel. But in this book (ch. 1:17) it tells us that Joram king of Israel began to reign in the second year of Jehoram king of Judah. The explanation of this apparent contradiction is that King Jehoshaphat, the father of Jehoram king of Judah, when he went out to war with Ahab to recover Ramoth Gilead from the Arameans, gave his son Jehoram the regency over the kingdom, because he did not know whether he would return alive or not; and when he returned alive, he reigned together with his son Jehoram. Two years after Jehoram was set up as king over Judah with his father, Joram began to reign over the kingdom of Israel, and five years after his reign began, Jehoshaphat gave the whole kingdom, that is, the full regency, to his son Jehoram, so that he became sole king over the kingdom. This means that he reigned fully five years after the reign of Joram king of Israel.
This means that Jehoram king of Judah reigned seven years with his father, and then received the kingdom alone, while Jehoshaphat was still alive at that time.

The similarity of names among the kings is because Jehoram king of Judah married the daughter of Ahab. There was a relationship between Jehoshaphat and Ahab, and as a political courtesy they gave their sons the same names. Jehoram king of Judah also named his son Ahaziah, who is the second son who reigned before Jehoram king of Israel, and he is the maternal uncle of Ahaziah king of Judah. The genealogy of the kings of Judah and Israel in this period:
Jehoshaphat, Ahab, Jehoram (husband of Athaliah), Ahaziah, Jehoram, Athaliah, who is ascribed to Omri her grandfather (v. 26), Ahaziah

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Jehoram king of Judah was thirty-two years old when he began to reign alone, and his reign lasted eight years. The capital of his kingdom was Jerusalem.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: King Jehoram walked in evil, that is, the worship of idols and evil lusts, like the kings of Israel, the most evil of whom were King Ahab and his wicked wife Jezebel, because the wife of Jehoram king of Judah was Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab, and she influenced him and made him walk in evil.

Jehoshaphat thought that by allying himself with Ahab king of Israel he would grow stronger, but unfortunately he grew weak, because of the lack of God's blessing on him and the corruption of his descendants, due to their intermarriage with the house of Ahab. Strength is in a relationship with God and not with the wicked.

Examine your personal relationships carefully, the most important of which is marriage, followed by friends, for they certainly influence you. These persons should have a relationship with God, so that they help you in your spiritual life; otherwise their company is bad company, which corrupts your life and leads you away from God.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: In spite of the very great evil of Jehoram king of Judah, God did not destroy the kingdom of Judah, who had angered Him, for the sake of the great David, because He had promised him to keep his descendants as kings over the kingdom forever. So He was long-suffering toward Jehoram and toward all the kings of Judah, until Christ came from them, who reigns forever.

God's keeping a light in the kingdom of Judah means the continuation of the kingship for the descendants of David; for the presence of a light in a house means that there are inhabitants in it, and the putting out of the light means that there are no inhabitants, that is, that the house is abandoned.

God is long-suffering toward you at many times, not because of your righteousness, for your evils provoke Him, but because of the many prayers that are offered for you and because of the righteous to whom you are related. In this He gives you an opportunity to repent, so do not be negligent and lose the opportunity.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Zair: it is Seir, the chain of mountains where the Edomites live.

A rebellion arose from the Edomites against those living south of Judah, so Jehoram king of Judah went out with soldiers and war chariots to subdue them, and he was able to defeat them. But afterward a company of Edomite soldiers surrounded him to destroy him, yet he was able to break through it and return to Jerusalem, and the soldiers of the kingdom of Judah fled, each to his tent, when they found their king surrounded by this Edomite company. That is, Jehoram first triumphed over Edom, but he nearly perished when they surrounded him, and he was able to escape, and the soldiers of Judah also fled. It is noted that the text of this verse is very brief, so we have given this detailed explanation.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Libnah: a city in Judah located southwest of Jerusalem.

From the days of Jehoram, Edom rebelled against the kingdom of Judah and set up a king for themselves, and they remained in this rebellion until near the first century before Christ, when the Maccabees subdued them.

The revolt of Edom is the fulfillment of Isaac's prophecy to his son Esau, when he told him that he would be subject to the descendants of Jacob, but a time would come when he would break Jacob's yoke and rebel against him.

Because of the evil of Jehoram king of Judah, the city of Libnah rebelled against him; it is a city in Judah in which priests lived, who could not bear his evils, so they rebelled against him at the same time as the rebellion of Edom, and perhaps other cities of Judah rebelled against Jehoram. God allowed these rebellions, in the hope that he would take heed and turn back from his evil, but unfortunately he continued in it.
The phrase "unto this day" means: to the day this book was written.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: The rest of the deeds that Jehoram did are recorded in "the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah," a book the Jews had for recording the events of the kings of Judah, which is different from the Chronicles recorded in the Holy Bible.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Jehoram died and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Ahaziah inherited the throne. Because of Jehoram's evil, he was not buried in the tombs of the kings, but only in the city of David.
(4) Ahaziah reigns over Judah (vv. 25-29)
25- In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel did Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah begin to reign.

26- Two and twenty years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel. 27- And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the LORD, as did the house of Ahab: for he was the son in law of the house of Ahab. 28- And he went with Joram the son of Ahab to the war against Hazael king of Syria in Ramothgilead; and the Syrians wounded Joram. 29- And king Joram went back to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which the Syrians had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. And Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.
The story of Ahaziah is repeated in 2 Chronicles ch. 22, verses 1-9, and verses 1-6 agree with what is in 2 Kings, and 2 Chronicles adds in verses
7-9 some events of the end of Ahaziah's life that 2 Kings does not mention.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Ahaziah: he is called Jehoahaz in (2 Chr 21:17) and also called Azariah in (2 Chr 22:

6). After the death of Jehoram king of Judah, his son Ahaziah reigned over Judah, and it was then the twelfth year of Jehoram king of Israel. Although (ch. 9:29) mentions that Ahaziah king of Judah began to reign in the eleventh year of Jehoram king of Israel, that is because parts of a year are counted as a year; in this chapter they were counted, so it became twelve years, whereas in (ch. 9) they were not counted.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and his reign was very short, for he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother was Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab, the son of Omri king of Israel. Here is a pause for comparison between the mother and grandmother who were the secret of blessing in the life of Timothy (2 Tim 1:5), and the mother Athaliah and the grandmother Jezebel, who were the secret of misery and corruption in the life of Ahaziah.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: King Ahaziah walked in evil, that is, he worshiped idols and encouraged his people to do so. This was because his mother Athaliah was the daughter of Ahab, the most wicked of the kings of Israel, who led them in the worship of idols, so Ahaziah the grandson continued in the way of his grandfather Ahab, that is, in the way of evil.

The meaning of the name Athaliah is "whom Jehovah afflicts," and the meaning of the name Joram, Athaliah's brother, is "whom Jehovah exalts" or "supports." We notice from this that the wicked Ahab used the name of Jehovah in naming his children, but sometimes for good and sometimes for evil, for Ahab halted between two opinions, sometimes being with God and sometimes against Him, since Ahab worshiped idols. So his children and grandchildren became like him in evil, drawing near to God at times and then departing from Him. This of course angers God greatly and brings His wrath upon them.

Be obedient to your parents, but in what agrees with God. If they walk in evil, do not follow them, for God must be obeyed more than men; indeed, by holding fast to God you may be able to draw them to Him, in proportion to your humility and your prayers.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: Ahaziah king of Judah helped Joram king of Israel and went out with him to fight Hazael king of Aram. This was because Joram king of Israel was Ahaziah's maternal uncle, the brother of Athaliah his mother, and both walked in evil like Ahab. The cause of the war was Joram's attempt to recover the city of Ramoth Gilead. He was able to recover it from Hazael, as is proved by the anointing of Jehu as king while he was in it (ch. 9:1-15), who was the king after Joram king of Israel, but Joram was struck and wounded in the war.

entries.section: (3) The death of the scoffing officer

paragraphs.text: After the war with Hazael ended, Joram king of Israel went to Jezreel, a place where the kings spent the summer, that is, a beautiful place where Joram spent a period to be healed of the wounds he had received in the war with the Arameans. Ahaziah returned with his army to Jerusalem, then went down from Jerusalem, which is in the mountains, to Jezreel, which is in the valley, to ask after and care for the condition of his uncle Joram king of Israel. Jehu reigns and the house of Ahab is slain

entries.section: (1) Jehu is anointed king

paragraphs.text: Gird up your loins: to gird the loins is to put on clothing around the waist and below it, that is, a person putting on his clothes in preparation for a journey.
Box (vial): a small vessel in which the oil of anointing is kept; the oil may also be put in the horn of an animal.

Ramoth Gilead: a city located east of the river Jordan near the river Jabbok, in the portion of the tribe of Gad, and given to the Levites. It is one of the cities of refuge, and there were many wars between the Arameans and the children of Israel to take possession of it.

God had commanded Elijah to anoint Hazael king over Aram (1 Kgs 19:15-17), and this was done at the hand of Elisha, who did not anoint him with oil, because he was a Gentile who would not understand the meaning of anointing, but informed him of it (ch. 8:13). God also commanded Elijah to anoint Jehu king over Israel, and this is now done through Elisha, who sends one of the sons of the prophets with a vial of oil to Jehu, who was staying in Ramoth Gilead. God likewise commanded Elijah to anoint Elisha as prophet in his place, and this was done at Elijah's prayer, when the Spirit of God came upon Elisha in a double portion, just before Elijah's ascent into heaven (ch. 2:9-11). It is noted that Elijah did not carry out God's word at its time, because the appropriate time in God's providence had not yet come. And the carrying out of the divine command comes not only through Elijah himself but can be through his spiritual sons, like Elisha, or one of Elisha's disciples. Ahab repented when Elijah rebuked him, so God postponed his punishment to the days of his descendants, and this was by way of Hazael and Jehu, who were to be anointed after Elijah's ascent. From this it is understood that Elijah and Elisha and their sons from the sons of the prophets are one thing in God's sight, because the one Spirit of God is working in them.

entries.section: (1) Jehu is anointed king

paragraphs.text: Elisha charged one of the sons of the prophets, whom he sent to Ramoth Gilead, to look for Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi, and he would find him gathered among his brethren, the commanders of the army. He was to bring him into an inner room in the house, so that no one would see or hear him, and anoint him there as king. Jehoshaphat the father of Jehu is of course different from Jehoshaphat king of Judah. Because the anointing of Jehu was a grave matter, as we shall learn, for he would destroy and kill others, Elisha asked this prophet to do it in complete secrecy, going from room to room. Elisha did not go himself, because Elisha was a well-known person, and his going would raise questions in the whole city, and he could not anoint Jehu in secret. Elisha did not tell this prophet what to say to Jehu but contented himself with commanding him to anoint him, because God had commanded him only this, and God would give the words to this prophet, who would tell Jehu what was required of him. Here the obedience of the prophet Elisha to God appears: he does not interfere in His arrangements or His division of the work, that is, God wanted to tell the prophet Himself what to say to Jehu, and Elisha did not command him to say anything. Jewish tradition says that this prophet was the prophet Jonah. In this Elisha completes God's command to Elijah to anoint Jehu king (1 Kgs 19:15-17).

entries.section: (1) Jehu is anointed king

paragraphs.text: Elisha also commanded the son of the prophets, when he was alone with Jehu, to pour the oil on his head and inform him that he had become king over Israel, and then to flee at once, for fear for his life. For if there were among the army commanders anyone loyal to King Jehoram, he would of course kill the prophet; or if Jehu himself were loyal to Jehoram, considering himself only one of his army's commanders, he might rush and kill this prophet. That is, he was not to give Jehu a chance to think and speak with any of the commanders. Although God is able to protect His children, He asks them to do what is within their power, and then to rely on Him, and He will not leave them.

Be obedient to God's commands, and fulfill your responsibilities and your service, however difficult they may seem, trusting in God's protection of you, for He is responsible for you and works through you, so do not be troubled.

entries.section: (1) Jehu is anointed king

paragraphs.text: The young prophet went to Ramoth Gilead and entered where the army commanders were gathered. He addressed Jehu, saying, "I have an errand to thee, O captain." Jehu asked him whom he meant by his words, and he told him that it was he, that is, Jehu, who was meant. Perhaps Jehu asked the prophet whether he wanted to speak to all the commanders or to him alone, because he felt that prophets bring tidings of good news, so that he would not appear in the commanders' eyes to be monopolizing the good news; and when the prophet confirmed to him that he wanted him, he obeyed.

entries.section: (1) Jehu is anointed king

paragraphs.text: Jehu arose and went in to where he could be alone with the prophet, and the prophet quickly poured the oil on Jehu's head, saying, "Thus saith the LORD, I have chosen you king over Israel." God told Jehu that He was setting him over His people, so God still feels that Israel is His people, although they mix His worship with the worship of idols, but in His fatherhood He sends them prophets and anoints a king for them to destroy those who support the worship of idols, namely Ahab and his descendants.

entries.section: (1) Jehu is anointed king

paragraphs.text: The young prophet declares to Jehu the harsh judgment that he must carry out upon the house of Ahab.

He calls Ahab his master, because Jehu was in Ahab's service (v. 25), and then in that of his descendants after him, Ahaziah and Jehoram. The reason for this judgment is the way in which the king, on the counsel of his wife Jezebel, treated the servants of the Lord and His prophets, for he persecuted Elisha the prophet of God and all the sons of the prophets, and at the same time encouraged the worship of idols and the prophets of Baal.

If this prophet who anointed Jehu is Jonah, then he had heard Elijah when he declared to Ahab that God would destroy his descendants for his evil and theirs, and he now proclaims to Jehu the command of God, which he had earlier heard from the mouth of Elijah his teacher (1 Kgs 21:21, 22). Strangely, we read in the book of Hosea (Hos 1:4) and understand God's anger against Jehu for destroying the descendants of Ahab, because he destroyed them with brutality and for his own sake, that is, to secure his kingdom, and not merely in carrying out God's commands. God wants us to obey His commandments and not to add anything to them of our own thoughts and evils.

entries.section: (1) Jehu is anointed king

paragraphs.text: The prophet informed him that he must destroy every male in the house of Ahab ("him that pisseth against the wall"), without sparing anyone ("him that is shut up and left"), that is, the little ones who are in the houses, or the grown ones who move freely everywhere. He must make the fate of the house of Ahab like the fate of the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat (1 Kgs 14:10) and like the fate of the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah (1 Kgs 16:3, 4), that is, destroy them completely, because these three, they and their descendants, were very wicked, and God destroyed them.

entries.section: (1) Jehu is anointed king

paragraphs.text: The sentence was likewise that the dogs would devour Jezebel in the field of Jezreel and she would find no one to bury her.

As soon as the prophet finished speaking, he opened the door and hurried away. God's punishment of the proud and wicked Jezebel is that she not be buried with honor in a special tomb as queens are, but that her corpse be thrown out for the dogs to lick up her blood, as a lesson to the wicked, so that they do not persist in their evil but repent.

entries.section: (2) The proclamation of Jehu as king

paragraphs.text: After the prophet fled, Jehu came out of the inner room and sat among the army commanders, the servants of the king, and they asked him what this prophet wanted and called him a madman, because the king and his court, on account of their evils and their distance from God, despised the prophets and considered them mad. Perhaps also the prophet, when he came in, was somewhat agitated because of the difficulty of the mission, so they described him as mad.

And they said to him, "Did he come in peace?" But Jehu tried to evade answering and to hide the matter; perhaps at first he was afraid to declare himself king, lest the army commanders oppose him because of their loyalty to King Jehoram. Their asking about the reason for this prophet's visit and their saying whether he came in peace or not showed that, despite their contempt for him, inwardly they felt the power of God in His prophets, so within them, along with curiosity, there was fear of what news this prophet was bringing.

The word of God may appear in the eyes of the world to be madness, and they despise it. So stand firm in the word of God with true faith and do not doubt because of their opposition to you, for they are troubled inside, and if they see your steadfastness they will back down, and even believe.

entries.section: (2) The proclamation of Jehu as king

paragraphs.text: When the army commanders saw the oil running down on Jehu's head, they were sure that Jehu was hiding the truth from them, so they said to him, "You are lying to us; tell us the truth." Because they knew that oil is poured only on the heads of kings, prophets and priests, they suspected that Jehu had been anointed king. Before this open confrontation Jehu could not hide what had happened, and he informed them that the prophet had anointed him king and told them all that the prophet had said to him.

entries.section: (2) The proclamation of Jehu as king

paragraphs.text: Hasted: hurried.

Each one of them hurried to spread his garment on the top of the stairs in the place where he stood, and they blew the trumpets, proclaiming, "Jehu is king." Thus God put into the hearts of these commanders a fear of Jehu, and perhaps they were troubled by Ahab and his descendants and their evils, so they declared their submission in the manner known at that time, which was for a person to take off his garment and place it under the feet of the one to whom he submits, as the disciples and followers of Christ did when He entered Jerusalem (Mt 21:8). The blowing of the trumpet is known among the Jews at the proclamation of the reign of a new king (1 Kgs 1:34). In this we see that God turns everything to the accomplishment of His purposes: the commanders who could have opposed Jehu submit to him so quickly, in addition to the fact that King Jehoram king of Israel was recovering in Jezreel alone, without his soldiers, while the soldiers were in Ramoth Gilead, which made it easy to proclaim Jehu king in the midst of the army.

entries.section: (2) The proclamation of Jehu as king

paragraphs.text: Thus Jehu became king over Israel and declared his rebellion against Joram, especially as Joram had placed a large division of the army in Ramoth Gilead to guard it, lest Hazael king of Aram attack it, which helped Jehu to proclaim his kingship and the army's submission to him, so that he was able to take control of the kingdom easily by the power of the army.

entries.section: (3) Jehu kills Jehoram

paragraphs.text: Jehoram king of Israel was spending a period of rest and recovery in Jezreel, after being wounded in his battle with Hazael king of Aram. Meanwhile Jehu declared himself king in Ramoth Gilead, and with human wisdom and cleverness he said to the many officers and soldiers who were with him in Ramoth, "If it be your minds, then let none go forth nor escape out of the city to go to tell it in Jezreel to King Jehoram." In this he shares the responsibility with them, so that if the plan of his kingship fails, they would all be condemned before King Jehoram. He also wanted to frighten them so that they would prevent anyone from informing King Jehoram, to make it easy for him to kill Jehoram king of Israel suddenly. But unfortunately this shows a lack of faith in the power of God that supported him; it was God who had anointed him and was able to support him, but he relied on his own strength and cleverness, so there was inside him a fear that his attempt would fail.

entries.section: (3) Jehu kills Jehoram

paragraphs.text: Jehu rode in his chariot toward Jezreel, where Joram lay recovering from his wound. Ahaziah king of Judah was visiting him to see how he was. So to the very last the kings of Judah, in the person of Ahaziah, were tied to the wicked kings of Israel, and this wicked tie brought loss upon the kings of Judah, because it drew them away from God, so He was angry with them, and it benefited the kings of Israel in their wars. Every association with the wicked benefits the wicked by increasing their material strength, and corrupts the righteous by drawing them away from God Himself.

entries.section: (3) Jehu kills Jehoram

paragraphs.text: As was customary at that time, a watchman would stand on a high tower to watch for any military movements or others that threatened the camp he protected, so that the soldiers would be on guard before the enemy came and took them by surprise. A watchman was standing on a tower in Jezreel, and he saw Jehu and his company coming and reported what he saw to Jehoram. Jehoram commanded that a horseman be sent to meet them and ask them whether they came for good. This was because Jehoram wanted to be reassured that Ramoth remained in the hands of his soldiers and that Hazael had not been able to recover it from them.

entries.section: (3) Jehu kills Jehoram

paragraphs.text: A horseman went from Jehoram to find out who was coming and to ask them for news and peace. When he reached Jehu and asked him, Jehu answered him harshly and said to him, "What hast thou to do with peace?" and commanded him to join the soldiers who were with him. The horseman submitted in fear and turned in behind Jehu and joined his soldiers. In this Jehu prevented any news from reaching King Jehoram, so as to surprise him and kill him. The watchman informed King Jehoram that the messenger had not returned to report what he had seen.

entries.section: (3) Jehu kills Jehoram

paragraphs.text: King Jehoram was alarmed and quickly sent another horseman, and when he reached Jehu, Jehu commanded him too to join his soldiers who were behind him.

entries.section: (3) Jehu kills Jehoram

paragraphs.text: The king was informed a second time that the second horseman had also not returned. The company had come nearer and nearer to Jehoram's camp, so the watchman could make out the persons, and he recognized Jehu by the way he drove his chariot, for he drove it furiously, and it seems this was known of Jehu, that is, his sharpness, violence and rashness. So the watchman recognized him and told the king.

entries.section: (3) Jehu kills Jehoram

paragraphs.text: Jehoram's anxiety about Ramoth Gilead increased, and he longed to know its news, especially after the two horsemen he had sent to scout for news did not return, so he went out himself in his chariot, and out of courtesy to him Ahaziah also went out in his chariot to share with him the concern for Ramoth Gilead.

This shows the extent of the ignorance and foolishness into which a person falls because of his evil: in pride he thought that Ramoth must remain with him, so he was not on guard and did not understand the danger coming upon him.

In proportion to your humility and your prayers, God reveals everything to you and protects you from dangers and the devil's tricks. So take care to pray, to learn from those around you and to consult the Fathers, and you will keep your humility and your peace.

entries.section: (3) Jehu kills Jehoram

paragraphs.text: Jehoram hurried to ask Jehu whether his coming was for good. Jehu answered: What good do you expect, so long as the debauchery of your mother Jezebel and her witchcrafts prevail? By the harlotry of Jezebel is meant her spiritual adultery, that is, her worship of idols and her abandonment of the worship of God; and by her witchcrafts are meant the pagan acts of worship offered to foreign gods, with all the sorcery, incantations and strange customs they carry.

entries.section: (3) Jehu kills Jehoram

paragraphs.text: Jehoram turned his chariot the other way, intending to flee, saying to Ahaziah, "There is treachery, O Ahaziah." That is, Jehoram turned back toward Jezreel to escape from the face of Jehu and the army that followed him, and warned Ahaziah to flee as well, because he was certain of the army's rebellion against him under the leadership of Jehu.

Although Jehoram cries out, "Treachery," it is at the same time the fulfillment of God's sentence against him because of his evils: even if he escaped from the hand of Hazael, the sword of Jehu would come upon him, as God said to Elijah (1 Kgs 19:17).

entries.section: (3) Jehu kills Jehoram

paragraphs.text: Jehoram's quickness in fleeing did not help him, for Jehu overtook him with an arrow that pierced his back and went through to his heart, and he fell in his chariot.

entries.section: (3) Jehu kills Jehoram

paragraphs.text: Captain (third man): one of the three guards accompanying Jehu, that is, one of the closest of those near to him, whom Jehu trusted, who rode with him in his chariot.

Jehu said to Bidkar, one of his chief commanders: "Take him up and cast him into the field of Naboth the Jezreelite, and remember how, when you and I were riding together after Ahab his father, the Lord decreed against him this punishment."

Thus God's judgment and punishment are carried out upon Ahab, who killed Naboth the Jezreelite, and he perishes, with his son Jehoram, in the very place that he unjustly seized and whose owner he killed.
Know that God sees all your deeds, so do not wrong anyone, whatever authority you have, for God defends His weak children. Rather, give every person his right, lest God take vengeance on you.

entries.section: (3) Jehu kills Jehoram

paragraphs.text: Jehu repeated the word of God, but briefly, giving the meaning without the text, when he declared Ahab's punishment for seizing the field of Naboth and killing him. God defended the weak and told Ahab that He saw the blood of the wronged Naboth and the blood of his sons. It is understood from this that Jezebel had also killed Naboth's sons, so that they would not avenge their father and there would be no heir to Naboth; and God commanded that in the same place Ahab and his descendant, who is Jehoram, would die. His saying "his little field" is a diminutive of field, and this shows the extent of Ahab's injustice, to kill innocent people in order to seize a small field. It is the height of injustice for a person to make light of the lives of others to satisfy his desires.

And here we see Jehu hiding behind the word of the Lord by repeating the phrase "the Lord commanded," but in truth he is carrying out his own ambitions and his resentment of Jehoram and his desire for domination and possession.

entries.section: (4) Jehu kills Ahaziah

paragraphs.text: The garden house: it is present-day Jenin, fourteen kilometers southeast of Megiddo, at the southern edge of the valley of Jezreel. It appears that the garden was among the possessions of Ahab, next to which was the field of Naboth.
Ibleam: the name of a place west of the river Jordan; its place today is the village of Bal'a, at a distance of seven kilometers south of Jenin and twenty kilometers northeast of Samaria.

Megiddo: it is present-day Tell al-Mutasallim, located at a distance of thirty-two kilometers southeast of Haifa. As for Ahaziah king of Judah, who saw what happened, he too fled, by the way of the garden house, and Jehu and his men pursued him, and Jehu commanded them to strike him, so they struck him in his chariot at the ascent of Gur, which is by Ibleam. His wounds were mortal, and he died at Megiddo.

The book of Chronicles (2 Chr 22:9) tells us that Ahaziah fled to Samaria, and Jehu's men caught him there and brought him to Megiddo, where Jehu was staying, and killed him there. So the addition made by the book of Chronicles is that he fled first to Samaria before dying at Megiddo, as the second book of Kings tells us.

entries.section: (4) Jehu kills Ahaziah

paragraphs.text: After Ahaziah was killed, his men carried his body and took it to Jerusalem and buried him there in the tombs of the kings, in the city of David, in a tomb that he had prepared for himself. Thus Ahaziah died because of his association with the wicked, that is, the house of Ahab, but he was less wicked than they, so God allowed him to be buried in the city of David and his body not to be thrown to the beasts of the earth and the birds of heaven, like Jehoram the son of Ahab.

God appreciates every deed you do, whether good, and He rewards you for it with many blessings, or evil, and He punishes you for it; but if you repent of it and confess and partake of the Holy Mysteries, He removes it from you. So take care to repent, for it is the way of your salvation, and you will have a place in heaven.

entries.section: (4) Jehu kills Ahaziah

paragraphs.text: Ahaziah had become king over Judah in the eleventh year of the reign of Joram the son of Ahab over Israel.
As we mentioned, fractions of a year were not counted here, whereas in (ch. 8:25) fractions of a year were counted, so it said the twelfth year of Joram.

entries.section: (5) Jehu kills Jezebel

paragraphs.text: Jehu entered Jezreel, and Jezebel heard of it, so she painted her eyes and adorned her hair, wanting to show Jehu that she was not afraid of him, for she still had authority, and she looked out of the window. Here the hardness of her heart and her selfishness appear: she was not moved by the death of her son Jehoram and her grandson Ahaziah, and she took care to adorn herself.

entries.section: (5) Jehu kills Jezebel

paragraphs.text: When Jehu arrived, she greeted him with mocking words, saying to him, "Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?"

By this she was hinting to remind him of Zimri king of Israel, who killed Baasha, the king before him, and Zimri remained in power only seven days (1 Kgs 16:9, 10), and then he too was killed in a conspiracy, as though she were telling him that his fate would be like the fate of Zimri. These words carried all the scorn she had toward him and the intense pride that was in her heart, and perhaps she wanted to frighten him.

entries.section: (5) Jehu kills Jezebel

paragraphs.text: Jehu looked up to the window from which she was addressing him and cried out, "Who is on my side? who?" By this he meant to gather the guards and the eunuchs to follow him, as the new king, and rebel against Jezebel, or else they would be exposed to being killed by his hand. Two or three eunuchs looked out to him, and he commanded them to throw her down from the window, and they threw her down, and her blood splashed on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her with his horses. This means that she struck the wall of the palace, so her blood ran down the wall, and then Jehu advanced with his horses and trampled her. This shows the extent of Jehu's fierceness, brutality and boldness, for he is not only carrying out the word of God, but shows the extent of the wrath in his heart, which he bore against the house of Ahab.

entries.section: (5) Jehu kills Jezebel

paragraphs.text: After Jehu trampled Jezebel and killed her, he entered the king's palace, where she used to live, and ate of the food that had been prepared for her and for her son King Jehoram, for he was hard-hearted, sensual and fierce. After he had eaten he said to his men, "Take up the body of Jezebel." He described her as cursed, because of her clinging to the worship of Baal and her seducing her husband Ahab, her sons and her grandsons to worship idols, and her sons and grandsons had become kings over the two kingdoms of Israel and Judah; that is, she corrupted the people of God in both kingdoms and persecuted the prophets of God, especially Elijah, so she became a symbol of evil throughout history, as the Book of Revelation confirms (Rev 2:20). Jehu asked his men to bury her in a tomb, because she was the daughter of a king, who was the king of the Sidonians; that is, he tried to honor her after he had gotten rid of her. In this he shows that he is not carrying out the word of God but his personal purposes, because God had commanded through the mouth of Elijah that Jezebel would be thrown in the field and the dogs would lick up her blood. He confirmed this a second time through the mouth of one of the sons of the prophets, who informed Jehu of it.

entries.section: (5) Jehu kills Jezebel

paragraphs.text: When they went out to bury her, they found of her remains only the skull, the feet and the palms of her hands, because the dogs had eaten her flesh.

entries.section: (5) Jehu kills Jezebel

paragraphs.text: Dung: manure, that is, the droppings of animals.

When Jehu's men returned, they told him what they had found, and he commented on it, saying: This is the fulfillment of what the Lord decreed by the tongue of Elijah the Tishbite, saying, "The dogs shall eat the flesh of Jezebel in the field of Jezreel, and her body shall be as dung upon the field of Jezreel, so that no one will be able to recognize her, and say, This is Jezebel.

The sad end of Jezebel reminds us of the eternal torment that is the end of the wicked. When you remember the judgment every day, you fear God and keep away from sin, however attractive it may seem, for its end is destruction, and so you save your soul and live in repentance and find your life.
Jehu kills his enemies

entries.section: (1) The killing of the house of Ahab

paragraphs.text: Ahab had seventy sons, meaning sons and grandsons, who perhaps had taken refuge in Samaria, the fortified city, and sheltered in it from Jehu. Perhaps the rulers of Israel also took refuge in Samaria to escape from the face of Jehu, so Jehu sent to them, because they had authority in the city, and also because he wanted to share the responsibility with Ahab's guardians, that is, the guardians who cared for the sons and grandsons of Ahab and had a great standing with them. Jehu sent to address them so that he might be able to do away with the sons of Ahab.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the house of Ahab

paragraphs.text: Jehu sent to the officials in Samaria mentioned above, provoking them and testing them, whether they were subject to him or not. He told them in the letter that, since you have with you:
1- the sons of your master Ahab, the former king;
2- chariots and horses, which are the most important equipment in war;
3- your city Samaria, fortified with high walls and strong trumpets;
4- many weapons of war;
then choose the best of your master's sons and set him on the throne in Samaria.

If they were rebellious, they would not answer the letter, and then he would attack them. And if they were subject to him and afraid of him, he could get rid, through them, of his enemies, who are all the descendants of Ahab and whoever is connected with him by kinship, or his supporters.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the house of Ahab

paragraphs.text: The rulers of Jezreel who lived in Samaria, and likewise the guardians responsible for Ahab's descendants, were very afraid of Jehu's letter, because he had killed two kings, Jehoram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah, so how could they stand before him? Especially as they were troubled by having no leader, after the death of Jehoram. They were accustomed to obeying a leader, not to leading the kingdom.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the house of Ahab

paragraphs.text: After the alarm and terror of the rulers of the city of Samaria, who were the one in charge of the city, the one in charge of the royal palace, and likewise the elders of the city and the guardians of Ahab's descendants, they wrote a letter in which they showed their complete submission to Jehu and to all his commands, and declared to him their refusal to set up a king from the descendants of Ahab.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the house of Ahab

paragraphs.text: The city of Jezreel: the most important city of the plain of Jezreel, which lies in the middle of the kingdom of Israel and extends from the river Jordan to the Mediterranean Sea. This city is located southwest of Hebron, at a distance of six miles.

After the letter of the rulers of the city reached Jehu and he learned of their submission to him, he sent them a second letter in which he said that the proof of your submission to me is that you come to me tomorrow with the heads of the seventy men, the sons of Ahab. He did not give them a chance to think, but in their fear and panic he commanded them to kill the sons of their master. Of course the killing of Ahab's sons by the guardians shows their evil and their disloyalty to the house of Ahab and their sharing in this hideous massacre, so they are Jehu's partners in this brutality and evil. Here Jehu's political shrewdness appears in making the rulers of Samaria kill the sons of Ahab, so that it would appear before all the people of Israel that he was not the killer of the house of Ahab but the rulers of Samaria were, and so the people would not be stirred up against him.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the house of Ahab

paragraphs.text: When the letter came to the elders of the city, they carried out Jehu's request, so they killed seventy men, the sons of Ahab, and put their heads in baskets and sent them to him in Jezreel, where he was staying. It is noted that the elders of Samaria did not go to Jehu themselves, for fear of him, but they obeyed his word, killed the sons of Ahab and sent their heads to him, as clear proof that they had killed them and not any other people.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the house of Ahab

paragraphs.text: One of Jehu's servants came and told him of the arrival of the severed heads of the king's sons, and he commanded that they be put in two heaps at the entrance of the gate of the city until morning. Jehu put them at the entrance of the city so that all who entered Jezreel or left it would see them and fear Jehu and submit to him, and so that the news would spread throughout Israel and all the people would fear him.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the house of Ahab

paragraphs.text: In the morning the people of Jezreel gathered around the two heaps of skulls, and Jehu went out to them and proudly declared that he had been able to rebel against his master King Jehoram, and even kill him. But craftily he declared his innocence of killing the sons of Ahab, asking who had killed them! Although it was he who had commanded the elders of Samaria to kill them. He is crafty and politically shrewd, and the truth is that he is a beast and a liar.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the house of Ahab

paragraphs.text: Jehu hid his brutality and crimes behind God's command to Elijah that He would destroy the descendants of Ahab, in order to show himself submissive to God and carrying out His commands, and so win the people to himself. Truly he fulfilled Elijah's prophecy, but he fulfilled it with brutality, because he was wicked and fierce, so he deserved God's wrath, as we shall see at the end of the chapter.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the house of Ahab

paragraphs.text: Jehu was not content with doing away with the sons of Ahab, but also killed all the members of his large family who lived in Jezreel, as well as all his helpers in government and all his friends and his priests, until none of them was left alive.

Jehu followed the course of one who justifies his actions, clothing them with zeal for the Lord and His law, while in truth he was seeking to satisfy his lust for power and the subjection of others. So do not deceive others and cover your sins with verses and teachings of the Church, because justifying faults angers God greatly and keeps you from repentance, and nothing awaits you but destruction.

entries.section: (2) The killing of the brethren of Ahaziah

paragraphs.text: Beth-eked of the shepherds: a town between Jezreel and Samaria. It is present-day Beit Qad, and is also called, for short, "Beth-eked," and it is the place where the shepherds tie up their sheep until they shear them.

The brethren of Ahaziah: the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah are meant (2 Chr 22:8), because Ahaziah's brethren had died (2 Chr 21:17). After Jehu finished killing everyone in Jezreel who had a connection with Ahab, he arose and headed for Samaria, and as he passed by "Beth-eked of the shepherds," he met a group of men and asked them who they were, and they told him that they were the brethren of King Ahaziah, and that they were on their way to visit the children of Ahab and his wife Jezebel, for they did not know that Jehu had killed the whole house of Ahab.

entries.section: (2) The killing of the brethren of Ahaziah

paragraphs.text: Jehu commanded that the brethren of Ahaziah be seized and killed, and they were forty-two men, and this was at the pit of Beth-eked, and perhaps he threw their bodies into this pit.

Do not be violent in your dealings with others, or rejoice that they dread you and fear you, for you are responsible to be a light to the world and salt of the earth, and whatever your authority, be humble and loving to those around you and show it to them. And if you are firm in some situations, do not lose your kindness toward those around you.

entries.section: (3) The agreement with Jehonadab the son of Rechab

paragraphs.text: Jehonadab the son of Rechab: he was the leader of the Rechabites, who were of the descendants of the Kenites. They had lived with the children of Israel when they entered the land of Canaan, and they do not follow the creed of the Jews but have their own way of life, which is distinguished by the following:
1- Abstaining from drinking wine and from planting vineyards, which could lead to the production of wine.
2- Dwelling in tents and not building houses, because of their being strangers to the world, like the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
3- Abstaining from farming, so as not to become attached to the crops they harvest, but to rely on God and work by herding.

Jeremiah mentioned them clearly (Jer 35). Jehu went out from Jezreel headed for Samaria, and on the way he found Jehonadab the son of Rechab coming out to meet him, and Jehu asked him, "Is thine heart right, as my heart is with thy heart?" He meant, are you with me and loyal to me, as I am with you and accept you? Jehonadab answered, confirming his agreement with Jehu. Jehonadab agreed with him in the worship of God and the rejection of evil, whereas Jehu meant Jehonadab's loyalty to him personally, regardless of God. Jehonadab loved Jehu because he removed the evils of Ahab, while Jehu fulfilled the will of God but with brutality and for his personal interests. Jehonadab came out to meet Jehu to declare to him his support for him in removing evil.

Then Jehu stretched out his hand to Jehonadab and shook his hand, declaring their agreement together, and then helped him up into his chariot, that is, to sit beside Jehu, so that all would see Jehonadab's agreement with and support of Jehu by his sitting beside him in the chariot.

The commitment of the Rechabites, which continued until the time of the writing of this book and extended three hundred years, to the days of Jeremiah, inspires us to commit to God's commandments, however heavy they may seem, out of our love for Him, because He loved us first and gave His life for us on the Cross. And when we keep His commandments, He too is committed to our salvation and to granting us peace in our hearts. The commitment of the Rechabites to the teachings of their leader increased when they saw evil increase in the kingdom of Israel, so instead of adapting and becoming lax under the influence of those around them, they became more committed. So stand firm in holding to God's commandments, however much evil increases around you.

entries.section: (3) The agreement with Jehonadab the son of Rechab

paragraphs.text: Jehu said to Jehonadab, "Come with me, and see my zeal for the LORD." So he took him with him in the same chariot. Jehu's words show his pride and his love of display in showing his zeal, in addition to the fact that his zeal was against the house of Ahab and the worship of Baal and not against the worship of idols as a whole, for he continued in the worship of the calves that Jeroboam had set up (v. 29).

entries.section: (3) The agreement with Jehonadab the son of Rechab

paragraphs.text: When Jehu reached Samaria, he destroyed all who were left of Ahab's supporters, thereby fulfilling the Lord's sentence which He spoke to Elijah. We notice that in his destruction of evil two faults appeared in Jehu:

1- He was concerned to gather supporters for himself, to show his power in pride and not for the glory of God, and he did not rely on the power of God but on material power, because his faith in God was weak.
2- He did not turn to Elisha the man of God, who was present at that time, because he did not care about submitting to God.

entries.section: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

paragraphs.text: Jehu used a trick to be able to gather the priests of Baal in one place so as to do away with them easily. In a speech before the people he spread the word that he would worship Baal with more sincerity than Ahab had done. What is meant by saying that Ahab served Baal a little is that Ahab halted between two opinions, serving Baal at times and then declaring that he worshiped God at other times.

entries.section: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

paragraphs.text: All his worshipers: everyone who cares about the worship of Baal.

Jehu showed his concern for the worship of Baal by announcing the offering of a great sacrifice to Baal, calling all the prophets of Baal and his priests and those who worship him to attend the rites of offering the sacrifice, and that no one should be absent, for whoever was absent would be killed. This was a great trick of Jehu in order to do away with the worshipers of Baal; he wanted to gather all the supporters of Baal by stressing that anyone who did not come would be killed, so as to ensure the destruction of Baal worship, so that no one would escape and set up worship of Baal anywhere in Israel.

entries.section: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

paragraphs.text: Solemn assembly: a day set apart for worship (Lev 23:26-33). To carry his trick further, he proclaimed that a solemn assembly must be kept, as a sanctification of the soul, before the feast of the sacrifice, and this call was proclaimed. None of the worshipers of Baal objected, for fear of Jehu.

entries.section: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

paragraphs.text: Jehu summoned all the worshipers of Baal from all over Israel, and no one was left behind, and they entered the temple of Baal, and filled it from end to end.

entries.section: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

paragraphs.text: Jehu commanded the man in charge of the wardrobe to bring out vestments for all the worshipers of Baal, and he did so, for the worshipers of Baal used to take off their clothes and put on special clothes for worship. And because the number of the worshipers of Baal was large and not all of them had brought worship garments, Jehu brought out for them the worship garments from the treasury of the temple. His apparent purpose was to sanctify the worship of Baal by these special garments, but his hidden purpose was to distinguish the worshipers of Baal from others so as to make it easy to kill them.

entries.section: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

paragraphs.text: Jehu went in, accompanied by Jehonadab the son of Rechab, to the house of Baal and called to those inside, asking them to make sure of those present, lest there be among them any who worshiped the Lord, but only the worshipers of Baal. Jehonadab did not take part in Jehu's deceit and lie but appeared here only with Jehu to make sure that none of the worshipers of the Lord was there, so that he would not be exposed to death, because Jehu had told Jehonadab his plan when he rode with him in the chariot.

entries.section: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

paragraphs.text: The rites of offering the sacrifice began, and all went in to offer it to their god Baal. Jehu had set an ambush of eighty men around the temple and charged them that none of the worshipers of Baal should escape, and warned them that their lives would be in place of the lives of any who escaped their hands, for they were to seize and kill any of the worshipers of Baal who tried to flee.

entries.section: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

paragraphs.text: The guard (runners): the guards.
Captains (thirds): those with military ranks, that is, officers.

After the priests of Baal finished offering their sacrifices and the hearts of all the worshipers were attached to Baal, Jehu commanded the guards under him to attack the temple and kill everyone in it, and they killed them all and threw their bodies on the ground. Then they went to the city of Baal, a group of buildings in which the priests of Baal lived, and brought out all the wooden images of the house of Baal and burned them.

entries.section: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

paragraphs.text: They broke down the image of Baal and tore down his temple and turned it into a dunghill, as a sign of its defilement and contempt, and it remained so until the day of the writing of this book. In this Jehu did away with the worship of Baal in Israel.

May you despise and reject everything connected with evil and trample it under your feet, that your heart may be free for the worship and love of God, because God cannot agree with the evils of the world.

entries.section: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

paragraphs.text: But Jehu did not turn completely from idolatry to serve God alone, for he kept Jeroboam's two golden calves, which were in Bethel and in Dan (1 Kgs 12:25-33), which were a national religion in Israel and had become, according to the prevailing custom, recognized.

entries.section: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

paragraphs.text: The Lord rewarded Jehu for his role in carrying out God's judgment on the house of Ahab, which was a just judgment on Ahab's evils and bad deeds, by letting Jehu's sons sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.

God's rewarding of Jehu does not mean His approval of his brutality or pride, but He rewards him only for removing the evil of Ahab. This material reward, the sitting of his sons on the throne of the kingdom of Israel to the fourth generation, does not mean the salvation of his soul or his entering the Kingdom, but He gives him an earthly reward in return for his work.

entries.section: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

paragraphs.text: But Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of the Lord with all his heart, for he continued to commit the sins of Jeroboam, who led Israel after him into transgression and made them sin, that is, he continued in the worship of idols.

entries.section: (5) The death of Jehu

paragraphs.text: In those days: that is, in the days of Jehu's reign.
To cut short (to cut off): to take and cut off lands and cities from the kingdom of Israel and give them to the Gentiles. This is a chastisement and punishment from God upon Israel.

During Jehu's life, the surrounding kingdoms were cutting off parts of his kingdom from every side, especially in the territories of the tribes east of the Jordan, which are fertile lands, for the Lord used Hazael as a rod with which to strike Jehu. This was a judgment from God on his conduct.

If God allows trials to come to you, they are a chastisement to remind you of your sins so that you repent, and not a rejection of you by God. So do not murmur or despair, but return to God, for He is your Father and loves you, and He wipes away all evil from you, and you regain your sonship in Him.

entries.section: (5) The death of Jehu

paragraphs.text: Aroer: a town to the north of the river Arnon.
The valley of Arnon: the Arnon is a river called today "Wadi al-Mujib," in the Kingdom of Jordan, and it flows into the Dead Sea.
Gilead: a mountainous region east of the Jordan, which includes modern Balqa.
Bashan: a province in the land of Canaan, east of the Jordan, between the mountains of Hermon and Gilead.

Hazael struck the children of Israel in all their coasts (borders), beginning from the east of the Jordan, including the land of Gilead and the lands of the Gadites, the Reubenites and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is in the valley of Arnon, and Gilead and Bashan.

entries.section: (5) The death of Jehu

paragraphs.text: As for the rest of the acts of Jehu and all that he did, they were recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel, which is different from the book of Chronicles that is in the Holy Bible.

entries.section: (5) The death of Jehu

paragraphs.text: Jehu died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoahaz succeeded him on the throne of Israel.

entries.section: (5) The death of Jehu

paragraphs.text: The reign of Jehu over Israel in Samaria lasted twenty-eight years.
He reigned a long time, and none reigned longer than he except his grandson Jeroboam II, who reigned forty-one years (ch. 14:23). Athaliah, then Joash, reign over Judah

entries.section: (1) Athaliah reigns over Judah

paragraphs.text: Athaliah: the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, and the only woman who sat on the throne of Judah.

Athaliah, the mother of King Ahaziah, was a wicked woman who always counseled her son to do evil, and no wonder, for she was the daughter of Ahab and his wife Jezebel, and she had the bad qualities of her mother Jezebel and, like her, loved evil and the oppression of others. When Jehu killed her son King Ahaziah, she killed her grandchildren, the sons of Ahaziah, and all who remained of the descendants of David, and so she reigned alone over the kingdom of Judah.

Athaliah grew up in a corrupt family that fostered evil and worshiped Baal, and no wonder, for her father was Ahab and her mother Jezebel. The home is the first school of every person, in which his inclinations and tendencies are formed. It is a great responsibility on the father and mother toward their children. May they labor to plant spiritual principles and sound conduct before they concern themselves with their children's success and health and all their material affairs.

entries.section: (1) Athaliah reigns over Judah

paragraphs.text: Jehosheba: she was the sister of Ahaziah, the daughter of the former king Jehoram, and the wife of Jehoiada the priest.

As for Joash, his aunt Jehosheba rescued him and snatched him from the midst of the slaughter that befell his brothers, and hid him and his nurse in the bedchamber set apart for the priests in the Temple, where her husband lived. For Jehosheba, the sister of King Ahaziah, had freedom of movement within the palace, so she was able to take the child Joash and hide him without anyone noticing, because they were busy killing the children older than he, as his age at the time of his rescue was one year.

entries.section: (1) Athaliah reigns over Judah

paragraphs.text: Joash stayed hidden in the Temple for six years, during which Athaliah was a usurper of the throne of Judah.

Here we see God's providence preserving a descendant of David, Joash, as He promised. But in the kingdom of Israel the royal line did not remain on the throne, because they were wicked, and even if they reigned it was only for a time, whereas the descendants of David endure not only for the whole life of the kingdom of Judah but forever in the person of Christ.

Jehoiada endured many dangers to preserve the son of David. We, in the present times, which are surrounded by many dangers, must bear sufferings while preserving the teachings and principles that the Son of David, Jesus Christ our Lord, gave us.

entries.section: (2) Joash is proclaimed king over Judah

paragraphs.text: Jehoiada: high priest in the days of Ahaziah, Athaliah and Joash, and the husband of Jehosheba, the sister of Ahaziah and the aunt of Joash.
The executioners: a rank of officers.
The guard (runners): they were of the royal guard and carried royal messages on foot, so they were distinguished by speed and strength.

Jehoiada was the high priest, a devout man of strong personality, displeased with Athaliah's usurpation of the throne and her evil conduct in the worship of idols. So after the child Joash grew up and was seven years old, that is, after six years of his hiding in the Temple with Jehoiada, Jehoiada sent and summoned the senior officers of the army, who were five, as the book of Chronicles tells us (2 Chr 23:1). After Jehoiada made sure of their rejection of Athaliah's reign and her evils, he informed them that the true king, the son of Ahaziah, was still alive and showed them the child Joash. They rejoiced greatly and made a covenant before God in the Temple with Jehoiada to reform conditions in the country and restore the kingship to the descendants of David, as the Lord commanded, and to depose Athaliah from the kingship. All this was done in complete secrecy inside the Temple, and Jehoiada agreed with them to report this matter to the heads of the fathers and the Levites in all the kingdom of Judah, as the book of Chronicles tells us (2 Chr 23:2, 3) that these five chiefs went to the cities of the kingdom of Judah and gathered the heads of the fathers and the Levites and brought them to Jerusalem, and they made a covenant before God with the king and the high priest Jehoiada to make the child Joash king and depose Athaliah.

Jehoiada was patient for six years in which his prayers rose, and God guided him to a plan to set matters right and restore the kingship to the house of David, by making Joash king. So be persevering in your striving, and do not be hasty for results and spiritual fruits; raise many prayers before God, but trust that God cares about your prayers and your striving, and in the end He will surely crown your striving with success.

entries.section: (2) Joash is proclaimed king over Judah

paragraphs.text: Under God's guidance Jehoiada made a plan to make Joash king, which included dividing the guards into three companies. The first company, that is, the third, guards King Joash, who is inside the house of the Lord, and Joash is to be installed as king on the Sabbath, for important reasons:
1- This is the day of the Lord, holy to Him, so it is fitting to install the king on it.

2- Large numbers worship God on this day in the Temple and the rest of the people in their homes, and no work is done in the royal palace or anywhere, in sanctification of the day of the Lord; that is, the atmosphere is quiet, so Queen Athaliah is taken by surprise by the installation of the true king Joash and finds no opportunity to call on her guards for help, because everyone is sanctifying the day of the Lord.

3- On the Sabbath the courses of the Levites and priests change, so he can use both courses, the first, which has finished its service, and the second, which is about to begin, and so he has a larger number of priests and Levites under him to guard the new king and take part in installing him as king.

entries.section: (2) Joash is proclaimed king over Judah

paragraphs.text: Of the remaining two thirds of the guards, one stands outside the gate of Sur, which is one of the gates of the Temple and is called the gate of the foundation in (2 Chr 23:5), to repel any attack that Athaliah might try to make. The last third of the guards stands behind this gate, hidden, to help the guards who are outside in the event of any attack. It appears that the second company, which stands outside the gate, was of the guard (runners), that is, the civil guard, and not of the priests and Levites, whereas those inside the house of the Lord guarding the king are of the priests and Levites only, as the book of Chronicles confirms (2 Chr 23:6).

entries.section: (2) Joash is proclaimed king over Judah

paragraphs.text: In this two courses of the Levites will share in guarding the king, because, as we mentioned, the change of the courses of the Levites and priests takes place on the Sabbath, and so Jehoiada uses the course that has finished its service and the course that is about to begin its service in guarding the new king.

entries.section: (2) Joash is proclaimed king over Judah

paragraphs.text: Jehoiada commanded that the guards from the Levites be armed and surround the king, and that if anyone else tried to break through their ranks, they should kill him at once; that is, they guard the little king with a strict guard.

entries.section: (2) Joash is proclaimed king over Judah

paragraphs.text: The five chiefs carried out all that Jehoiada commanded in his well-made plan, and they prepared themselves by dividing themselves in the guard and prepared for the installation of the king.

entries.section: (2) Joash is proclaimed king over Judah

paragraphs.text: Spears: the plural of spear.

Bucklers (shields): the plural of shield, which is a piece of wood covered with leather with a loop at the back into which the warrior puts his arm, and the shield is used to protect himself from any arrows directed at him.
