Jehoiada strengthened the Levites with the weapons stored with him in the house of the Lord from the days of David, that is, they became strongly armed to defend the king against any attack. Here we see David's weapons protecting the son of David and his descendant, who is Joash.
And David's weapons in the Temple signify the spiritual weapons in the Church, that is, prayer, the sacraments, the Holy Bible ..., which protect a person in his spiritual wars against Satan.

entries.section: (2) Joash is proclaimed king over Judah

paragraphs.text: The guards surrounded King Joash and the house of the Lord and the bronze altar, from the right and left sides, that is, from the south and north, in a circle, with their faces toward the king in their midst and toward the door of the Temple which is in the east, in readiness to repel any attack.

entries.section: (2) Joash is proclaimed king over Judah

paragraphs.text: After the guards had taken their stand, each in his place, and the people were filling the outer court of the Temple, because it was the Sabbath, Jehoiada stood and declared to them the evil of Athaliah and her worship of Baal, and this of course distressed all the people present in the house of the Lord to worship the Lord, and that God's command is that the descendants of David should continue on his throne, and that God's providence had kept the son of King Ahaziah alive until this day, and that he was the crown prince and the true king, and not Athaliah, the usurper of the kingship. The people rejoiced greatly where they stood. Then Jehoiada brought out to them the child Joash from the priests' bedchamber and set him in the midst, and put the crown of the king on his head and put in his hand a copy of the law of Moses, as the Law commanded in the book of Deuteronomy, so that the king might keep it in his reign (Deut 17:18-20), and poured on his head the oil of anointing, that is, anointed him king. Then all who stood there clapped their hands and cried out with a loud voice, "God save the king." Thus the proclamation and installation of Joash as king over Judah was completed.

entries.section: (3) The killing of Athaliah

paragraphs.text: While Queen Athaliah was sitting in her royal palace, which is next to the Temple, she heard the sound of loud shouting, "God save the king," and she wondered greatly and asked those around her of the guards, and made sure that everyone heard shouting. So she hurried herself to understand what this gathering and shouting in the Temple was, and she went down herself to the Temple, and perhaps a few guards were with her. She was surprised by huge numbers of Levites and people and saw for herself the child Joash wearing the king's crown with the guard around him, and she saw the guard (runners) outside the Temple, and she went in and saw for herself that a king had been installed in her place. Perhaps this was Athaliah's first visit to the Temple of the house of God, because she worshiped Baal, and at the same time it was her last visit, because she was killed after that.

entries.section: (3) The killing of Athaliah

paragraphs.text: She rent her clothes: a sign of intense grief and despair, and an ancient Eastern custom that remains until now.

There she saw the king standing by the pillar, according to the custom followed at the anointing of a new king, with the army commanders and the senior elders around him, and the trumpeters beside him, and all the people in great joy. Athaliah understood that this was an overthrow of the government, so she rent her clothes, crying out, "Treason, Treason." Athaliah forgot that she was the one who began the treason when she killed her grandchildren to usurp the kingship, and what a man sows, that he also reaps; for her helpers and her people betrayed her and restored the right order by making a descendant of David king, that is, King Joash.

entries.section: (3) The killing of Athaliah

paragraphs.text: Jehoiada commanded the chiefs with him of the army commanders to take Athaliah outside the walls of the house of the Lord, so that she would not be killed within it and would not disturb this great celebration of the installation of the new king, and if any of the personal guards tried to guard her, he was to be killed at once, so that the rest would be afraid. Thus she goes out alone and is killed outside. In this Joash reigns in peace and does not share in the shedding of blood, and the people complete their joy, while the traitor is killed outside.

entries.section: (3) The killing of Athaliah

paragraphs.text: The Horse Gate: one of the gates of the city next to the royal palace.

The army commanders at once seized Queen Athaliah and took her out from among the ranks of the people and the Levites and headed for the gate of Jerusalem nearest to the Temple and the king's palace, which is the Horse Gate, and they killed her there in front of her palace, and no one paid attention to her, because the people hated her for her evil, and they were relieved of her, to begin a new life in peace with God under the rule of the house of David.

This is the end of the wicked. May we take warning and not persist in our evils, because what awaits us is not only earthly chastisement but rather eternal destruction. However persuasive and attractive sin may be, keep away from it as long as it is against God's commandment.
If we compare what King Jehu did with Jehoiada's plan for installing the king, we find the following:
1- Jehu became king by destroying many people with violence and brutality, whereas Jehoiada made Joash king in peace, and only Athaliah, the wicked queen, was killed.
2- Jehu removed the worship of Baal and left the other idolatrous worship, whereas Jehoiada, as we shall see, removed all idolatrous worship at the beginning of the new king's reign.

3- Jehu needed deceit and lying to kill the prophets of Baal, because his plan was human, whereas Jehoiada, because he was a spiritual man, had a plan for installing the king without any lie, and he destroyed the idols with all force and relied on the Law, which he gave to the new king, and the covenant with God made by the chiefs, the Levites and the people to worship Him alone.

4- All the people were in fear and alarm of Jehu at his accession, whereas at the accession of Joash there was a great, majestic and joyful celebration inside the house of the Lord, and peace prevailed afterward among all the people.

Athaliah had to die at the beginning of the reign of the new king Joash. In the same way sin must die when your life with Christ begins. As happens in the sacrament of Baptism, when the nature inclined to evil dies and the nature inclined to good begins, so in the sacrament of confession it is necessary that you cut off sin and die to it, in order to begin a pure new life with Christ.

entries.section: (4) Jehoiada makes a covenant between God and the king and the people

paragraphs.text: After the installation of the new king Joash and the removal of Athaliah, the usurper of the throne, and after the kingdom was settled and peace prevailed, Jehoiada, who was the true leader of the kingdom and to whom King Joash, the child king, owed submission and honor, took care to make a covenant between the king and the people on the one hand and God on the other, that they would keep His commandments and His worship, and so receive all care and providence from God. Then he made another covenant between the king and the people, that the king would take care to look after his people and serve them, and the people would submit to the king and obey him and warn him if he erred. We notice that Jehoiada cared first of all about the relationship with God, and then about ordering the relationship within the kingdom between the king and the people.

entries.section: (4) Jehoiada makes a covenant between God and the king and the people

paragraphs.text: Mattan: he was the chief priest of Baal.

The members of the assembled crowd gathered and went to the temple of Baal and tore down his altars and broke his images and killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, before the altar, and Jehoiada appointed overseers to take care of ordering the worship in the temple of God, because it had been neglected in the days of Athaliah, the Levites had scattered in the land and the people had departed from worship. But after the covenant with God to worship Him and the tearing down of the altars of Baal, they returned to the worship of God. This is the second work that Jehoiada did, that is, after the covenant to worship God, the worship of idols must be got rid of; and the third work was to care for worship in the house of the Lord, that is, he appointed officers over the house of the Lord.

If you want to begin anew with God, then, besides renewing a steady relationship and spiritual practices, you must get rid of all the things connected with evil that you have, that is, everything that causes you to stumble, of friends, pictures, books and places, and keep away from all sources of evil.

entries.section: (4) Jehoiada makes a covenant between God and the king and the people

paragraphs.text: Jehoiada took with him the commanders of the companies and the commanders of the guard and the representatives of the people who were present there, and they brought the king out of the Temple and went with him in a festive procession, by way of the gate of the guard to the palace, where they seated him on the throne. This is Jehoiada's fourth work, that is, the celebration of the king's sitting on his throne in his palace. It is beautiful to see the people following Jehoiada and sharing with him in his works; that is, God gave him grace in their eyes and he became the spiritual and civil leader of the kingdom, which helped the return of the people to God and the Lord's pleasure with them.

entries.section: (4) Jehoiada makes a covenant between God and the king and the people

paragraphs.text: Jehoash: the short form of this name is Joash, so the two names are of one person.
Joy spread to all the people, and tranquility prevailed in the city after the killing of Athaliah. Joash was seven years old when he ascended the throne.

Joash's circumstances seem hard, when he lost his father and all his family and his palace, in which he could have been brought up, and he was at that time one year old. He lived hidden, moving only within narrow limits in a single room. But God's providence allowed these sufferings so that he would keep away from the evil and idol worship that fill the royal palace, and be brought up inside the Temple and love God, and so be prepared for the greatest position in the kingdom, that is, to become a king who worships God. So do not be alarmed by the hard circumstances that you pass through, for they are your way to success and the Kingdom.
Joash king over Judah

entries.section: (1) The good beginning

paragraphs.text: Zibiah: a woman from Beersheba, the wife of Ahaziah and the mother of Jehoash king of Judah.

Jehoash became king over Judah in the seventh year of Jehu king of Israel. His reign lasted forty years, and the capital of his kingdom was Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Zibiah, and she was from Beersheba. The name of his mother is mentioned out of concern and respect for this king, because of his good beginning.

entries.section: (1) The good beginning

paragraphs.text: Throughout the whole period in which Joash was under the guardianship of Jehoiada the priest, he did all that was right.

Seeking the help of spiritual guides leads a person to what pleases the Lord. So let us turn to our spiritual guides; they will light the way for us, that we may reach the harbor of safety. Let us not be proud and refuse to turn to them, lest we stray from the way of God.

entries.section: (1) The good beginning

paragraphs.text: But the problem of the high places remained, although the people sacrificed and offered burnt offerings not to pagan gods but to the true God, Jehovah.
In this there was a violation of the commandment, as we mentioned before, which had appointed one place, the Temple, for offering sacrifices.

Offering sacrifices on the high places was a ritual violation, that is, offering sacrifices in the wrong place, though not with the intention of worshiping idols. The first of the kings to introduce this idea was Solomon (1 Kgs 3:2-4). This led his son Rehoboam to fall into offering on the high places, not to God but to idols. Here the importance of obeying the Law appears, which protects us from turning away from God. The righteous kings of Judah, such as Asa and Jehoshaphat, were not able to remove worship on the high places (1 Kgs 15:14, 1 Kgs 22:43-44). As for the wicked ones, such as Abijam, Jehoram and Ahaziah, they worshiped idols. Then we come to the reign of Hezekiah, the righteous king, who was able to remove the high places and to prevent the offering of sacrifices on them, whether to God or to idols; but sadly they returned in the reign of his son Manasseh, and then Amon. Then there appeared the greatest of the kings of Judah, who walked like David in the worship of God, Josiah the righteous king, who not only removed the high places but also defiled them with the bones of the dead, so that none of the kings after him was able to worship on them.

entries.section: (2) The repair of the Temple

paragraphs.text: Current silver: the silver in circulation.

The greatness and uprightness of Joash appear in his concern, before everything else, for the repair of the house of the Lord. He commanded the priests to collect the silver then in use, which was brought to the Temple in various ways, such as:
1- What was offered for the souls of the people, which was half a shekel of silver (Ex 30:11-16).
2- What was offered as the price of certain offerings, in place of them (Lev 27:11, 12).
3- Any voluntary gifts of silver.

And Joash commanded that this silver be used for the repair of the house of the Lord, which had fallen into ruin after being neglected in the days of the wicked kings Jehoram, Ahaziah and Athaliah, and especially Athaliah, who demolished parts of the Temple (2 Chr 24:7).

entries.section: (2) The repair of the Temple

paragraphs.text: But the Temple remained unrepaired until the twenty-third year of the reign of Joash, because the priests collected the silver but took it for themselves and did not repair the Temple. They were not content to meet their needs from the silver, which the Law permits, but they took all the silver and neglected the repair of the house of the Lord and the carrying out of the king's orders, and this shows their love of money and their neglect of God.

Beware of the love of money, for it is the root of all evils. It begins with meeting your needs; then you become occupied with them and care about luxuries, and the luxuries become necessities without your realizing it, and your heart is taken up with money, so that your concern for the worship of God grows less. Hold to a spiritual rule in your relationship with God, in prayer, the Holy Bible, and a relationship with the sacraments and with repentance, so that you do not draw away from God without realizing it.

entries.section: (2) The repair of the Temple

paragraphs.text: King Jehoash summoned Jehoiada the high priest together with the rest of the priests and rebuked them for not repairing the Temple. And he commanded them to take nothing of the silver coming into the house of the Lord, and consequently they would not be responsible for repairing the house of God. They agreed and obeyed him.

Here we see the vigilance of Joash in rebuking Jehoiada his teacher and all the priests under him. He had mastered what he learned from Jehoiada and held fast to it, even if Jehoiada himself was lax in his love and concern for the house of the Lord. We also find Joash taking up the responsibility for repairing the house of the Lord, since he would collect the silver and use it for the repair, apart from the priests.

Be vigilant and bear your responsibilities, even if others around you are lax, even if they are older than you; for you are responsible before God, and He is the One who will hold you to account and at the same time will help you, if you are diligent in your responsibilities before Him.

entries.section: (2) The repair of the Temple

paragraphs.text: Jehoiada brought a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and set it at the right side of the altar of burnt offering, at the entrance of the Temple. The priests who kept the door put into it all the money that the contributors from the people brought for the house of the Lord. Here we see the cooperation of the priests and their concern to carry out the orders of King Joash, and perhaps this is due to two things:

1- The priests were moved by the words of Joash and repented, because they had cared for their own needs more than for the house of the Lord, and so they expressed their repentance by putting the silver into the chest.
2- Perhaps Jehoiada was moved, and at the same time rejoiced, at the words of his disciple King Joash, so he pressed the priests and commanded them to cooperate in carrying out the king's orders.

entries.section: (2) The repair of the Temple

paragraphs.text: The great priest: he is Jehoiada.

They bound up and counted: they gathered the silver, which consisted of ingots of silver of fixed value that were known at that time, and they counted their value and put each amount in a bag of fixed value.

Whenever the chest was filled with silver, the committee formed of the king's scribe and the high priest would come to count the money inside it, to hand it over to the overseers appointed to supervise the work of repair, so that they might pay from it what was due to the carpenters and builders working on the repair, and also the masons, and buy the timber and stone and meet all the other costs of the repair.
From this we understand several things:

1- The concern of Jehoiada and the king's trust in him. Although the king had reproached him, he trusted his faithfulness. If Jehoiada was lax in pressing the priests to take only what was necessary for their needs, he himself lived his simple life and was faithful in his personal life.

2- His concern that there be a committee of two, so that none of the people would doubt the silver offered to the Temple, lest it be lost? This was especially so since one of the two, Jehoiada the high priest, was completely trusted.

3- The Temple had suffered ruin, damage and neglect at the hands of many of the former kings, because of their preoccupation with the worship of Baal, so the repair of the Temple required a large number of workers skilled in the various branches of building.

entries.section: (2) The repair of the Temple

paragraphs.text: Basins: wide vessels in which water or the blood of the sacrifices was put.
Snuffers: the plural of snuffer.
Bowls: small vessels for sprinkling blood.

The king and all those appointed by him gave priority to repairing the house of the Lord, and they spent none of the silver on completing the vessels and tools needed for the Temple, for this could be completed after making sure that the building was sound and complete. This shows the wisdom of the king and his orderly mind, and it also shows that the house lacked many of the vessels, because the former wicked kings had distributed the golden vessels of the Temple and given them to the enemies of the people of God (1 Kgs 14:26, 15:18). And after he finished the repair of the house, he also completed the vessels inside the Temple, as we understand from the Book of Chronicles (2 Chr 24:14).

entries.section: (2) The repair of the Temple

paragraphs.text: These overseers appointed by the king were known for complete honesty in handling money, so he did not ask them to give an account of what they had spent on the work of repairing the Temple, since the work was very great and there was not time to submit accounts with all the details, and so they relied on their honesty. This shows the love and honesty of the people, which sometimes surpass those of the priests.

entries.section: (2) The repair of the Temple

paragraphs.text: The just King Joash did not neglect the personal needs of the priests, and so he set aside for them the silver of the sin offering and the trespass offering. From this we see two things:
1- The great blessing of the Lord when Joash gave attention to repairing the house, for the silver was plentiful, enough for the needs of the priests and the repair of the house.
2- The priests' exaggeration in the past of their needs beyond what was fitting, as we mentioned earlier, before Joash commanded them to stop collecting the silver.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Gath: one of the five great cities of the Philistines, lying south of the kingdom of Judah and near the Mediterranean Sea; it is an entrance to the kingdom of Judah.
Aram: present-day Syria.

Joash lived uprightly, worshiping God, all the life of Jehoiada the high priest. After the death of Jehoiada he was swayed by the words of the princes of Judah, as the Second Book of Chronicles tells us (2 Chr 24:15-21), and he forsook the Lord and worshiped idols. When Zechariah the priest, the son of Jehoiada, warned him, he was angered at him and stoned him, and Zechariah, at his death, prayed for God's judgment. So God intervened and caused Hazael king of Aram to attack him; after he captured Gath, he advanced toward Jerusalem. This was a chastening from the Lord because of the evil of Joash.

From this the weakness of Joash's character appears: he lived with God because of the guidance of Jehoiada, but after his death he was led, on the counsel of the princes of Judah, to the worship of idols.

Be steady in your relationship with God, committed to a spiritual rule that does not waver, even if circumstances take you away from your father or your spiritual guide. Do not be shaken, but persevere in your striving and trust in the help of God, which will support you.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Jehoash wanted to spare Jerusalem the destruction and ruin that was about to befall it when Hazael invaded it, so he decided to bribe him with money. He took all that his fathers had dedicated for the service of the sanctuary, what Jehoshaphat, Jehoram and Ahaziah had offered, as well as all the gold kept in the treasuries of the Temple and the treasuries of the royal palace, and handed it to Hazael, who accepted it as the price of his turning back from invading Jerusalem; that is, he gave him all the gold and silver found in the house of the Lord.

We notice that Joash, as a result of his neglect of the worship of God, did not think to take refuge in Him to rescue him from the hand of Hazael. He relied on his own mind in offering the money, though it was not his own money but the money of God. And God allowed Hazael to withdraw from Jerusalem out of regard for the goodness of Joash in his earlier life, in the days of Jehoiada; that is, He was content with a limited chastening of Joash. He also chastened him with many diseases (2 Chr 24:25). And so Joash became weak, unable to resist his enemies, and afflicted with diseases, because he had departed from God and lost His support.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: The rest of the acts of Joash and all the events of the period of his reign are written in “the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah,” which is not the Book of Chronicles found in the Holy Bible.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: The end of Joash was a tragic end, for some of his men rose up against him and killed him in “the house of Millo,” which Solomon had built, as Joash was going down by the road leading to the city of Silla.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Jozachar the son of Shimeath: he is the same as Zabad in (2 Chr 24:26), the son of an Ammonite woman, and one of the two who took part in the assassination of Joash.
Jehozabad the son of Shomer: one of the men of Joash who killed him.
Two of his men assassinated him, Jozachar the son of Shimeath and Jehozabad the son of Shomer. He was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Amaziah reigned after him.

Here we find the end of one who begins well and then turns away from God. He did not meet only troubles, but his two servants betrayed him and killed him; for if the king is far from God, worshiping idols, so too his servants easily become idolaters with no principles, and so they kill the king. And because of his turning away from God he was not buried in the tombs of the kings, but was buried only in the city of David. All this was vengeance and chastening from God for the blood of Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, the innocent.
The reign of Jehoahaz, then of his son Joash (1) The reign of Jehoahaz over Israel (vv. 1-9)

1- In the three and twentieth year of Joash the son of Ahaziah king of Judah Jehoahaz the son of Jehu began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned seventeen years. 2- And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, and followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which made Israel to sin; he departed not therefrom. 3- And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and he delivered them into the hand of Hazael king of Syria, and into the hand of Benhadad the son of Hazael, all their days. 4- And Jehoahaz besought the LORD, and the LORD hearkened unto him: for he saw the oppression of Israel, because the king of Syria oppressed them. 5- (And the LORD gave Israel a saviour, so that they went out from under the hand of the Syrians: and the children of Israel dwelt in their tents, as beforetime. 6- Nevertheless they departed not from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who made Israel sin, but walked therein: and there remained the grove also in Samaria.) 7- Neither did he leave of the people to Jehoahaz but fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen; for the king of Syria had destroyed them, and had made them like the dust by threshing. 8- Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? 9- And Jehoahaz slept with his fathers; and they buried him in Samaria: and Joash his son reigned in his stead.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Jehoahaz the son of Jehu took the throne of Israel in the twenty-third year of Joash the son of Ahaziah king of Judah, in fulfillment of the Lord's promise to Jehu that his sons to the fourth generation would sit on the throne of Israel; and here the first generation begins its rule. The reign of Jehoahaz lasted seventeen years, and he was followed by Joash, then Jeroboam II, then his son Zechariah. In this the promise of God is fulfilled that the descendants of Jehu would reign to the fourth generation, which is the longest period that any royal house reigned in the kingdom of Israel. Jehoahaz is not mentioned in the Second Book of Chronicles, because that book concentrated on the kings of Judah, and Jehoahaz had no connection with the kings of Judah. It should be noted that he reigned seventeen years, and during the last three of them his son Joash shared the kingship with him. Many kings made their sons share the rule with them, to encourage them and so that no other person would seize the kingdom; for in the kingdom of Israel there was no obligation that the son inherit the kingship of his father, and so anyone could seize the kingdom.

It is mentioned (ch. 12:1) that Joash king of Judah began to reign in the seventh year of Jehu king of Israel, and it is also mentioned that Jehu reigned twenty-eight years (ch. 10:36), so that the end of the reign of Jehu and the accession of his son Jehoahaz came twenty-one years after the accession of Joash king of Judah. But what is mentioned here is that Jehoahaz began to reign in the twenty-third year of Joash king of Judah, and there is no contradiction, because part of a year is counted as a year. There is a part of a year before the twenty-first year and a part after the twenty-first year, so the total is twenty-three years. This is what the writer reckoned in this chapter, whereas in the other places we mentioned here, the writer did not count the parts of the year.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Jehoahaz walked in the sins of idolatry, which Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the first king of the kingdom of Israel, began, and in which, sadly, all the kings of Israel walked. These sins are summed up in:
1- Bowing down to the idols that Jeroboam made in Bethel and Dan.
2- Appointing priests who were not of the descendants of Aaron, to offer worship to these idols.

3- Establishing feasts other than those prescribed by the Law of Moses (1 Kgs 12:28-33). And the remarkable thing is that at the very time when Jehoahaz begins to do these evils, Joash king of Judah, at the same time, that is in this same year, on the other side is occupied with repairing the house of the Lord.

Be zealous for the worship and honoring of God, however widespread evil becomes around you and however many follow it. And know that God not only rejoices in you and promises you the Kingdom, but also helps you and establishes you in the spiritual life, even if you are alone in the midst of many.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Benhadad: a name repeated among the kings of Aram; he was the commander of the army of his father Hazael, and then reigned after him, and that was after the death of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

The Lord was angry with Jehoahaz and the people of Israel because of their worship of idols, and so He allowed Hazael king of Aram and his son Benhadad to attack the kingdom of Israel, killing many, taking some of their cities and carrying some into captivity, until the kingdom was greatly distressed. And God did not fight for them, so that perhaps they might feel their weakness, repent and return to Him; but sadly they continued in the worship of idols.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Jehoahaz cried out to the Lord in supplication, and He answered his supplication, because He saw the troubles that His people were suffering under the dominion of the king of Aram. But He did not deliver them quickly, so that they might turn from the worship of idols, and God intervened and stopped the attack of the Arameans in the days of King Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz (v. 25).

Despite the turning away of Jehoahaz from the worship of the Lord, the Lord heard him, because He saw the affliction of His people, and the Scripture says, “In their affliction he was afflicted.” The Lord pays attention to any movement toward Him, however weak. God is found by the one who seeks Him, that perhaps he may complete his repentance and worship Him with all his heart.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: God saved His people after the reign of Jehoahaz, in the days of his son Jehoash, when Assyria rose against Aram and weakened it. This helped Jehoash to recover the cities of Israel that had been seized, and the people returned to dwell in safety in their dwellings; that is, the war ended.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: The grove: a tall pole set up on the high places for the worship of the moon, with altars built beside this pole.

Despite what the Lord had done for them, they did not depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who led Israel into transgression, but continued in their evil ways, and the idol of Ashtoreth remained in Samaria. The first to set up such poles in Israel was King Ahab (1 Kgs 16:32, 33). It is understood from this verse that they walked in this worship, that is, they continued in what they were accustomed to of the worship of idols, provoking the Lord. And so we see that their seeking the mercy of God was so that they might enjoy His help, but they also continued in their evils and refused repentance, although God had saved them from their enemies for the purpose of their repentance and not for their own well-being.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: There remained of the army of Jehoahaz only fifty horsemen, ten war chariots and ten thousand foot soldiers (they had been eight hundred thousand in the days of David), because the king of Aram had destroyed the army of Jehoahaz when he held sway over them before, and trampled them as dust is trampled.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: The rest of what Jehoahaz did, and his excess in evil and the worship of idols, is written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. Jehoahaz died and they buried him with his fathers in Samaria, where tombs had been set apart in Samaria for the kings of Israel, and his son Joash took the throne after him.
(2) The reign of Jehoash over Israel (vv. 10-13)

10- In the thirty and seventh year of Joash king of Judah began Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned sixteen years. 11- And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD; he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin: but he walked therein. 12- And the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, and his might wherewith he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? 13- And Joash slept with his fathers; and Jeroboam sat upon his throne: and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz ascended the throne of Israel, the second generation of the dynasty of Jehu. He reigned in Samaria sixteen years, and he reigned with his father Jehoahaz for three years, and then his father died.
The kings of Judah and Israel in the days of Joash king of Judah.

Kings of Judah, years, kings of Israel: Joash king of Judah began to reign; the command to repair the Temple, 23; Jehoahaz king of Israel began to reign; 37; Jehoash king of Israel began to reign with his father Jehoahaz; Amaziah king of Judah began to reign; 40; the death of Jehoahaz and Joash reigns alone over Israel.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Joash too was a wicked ruler; he did not withdraw from the crooked ways in which Jeroboam the son of Nebat walked, and he led the people after him in these same ways.

Leadership is very important and its influence is great, for the wicked kings led their peoples astray. So be careful in your leadership of those around you, whether you are a father or a servant, so that you lead everyone in the way of God, and do not forget that you are the light of the world and the salt of the earth.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: The rest of the acts of Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz, his excess in evil and the details of his war against Amaziah king of Judah, are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. But there was something of goodness in Joash, because he turned to Elisha the prophet, as will appear from the following verses, and he regarded him as a man of God, and this has value in the eyes of God, and perhaps this is what made God grant deliverance from Aram in his days.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Joash died and was buried with his fathers in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and his son Jeroboam sat on the throne of Israel after him, the third generation of the descendants of Jehu.
(3) Elisha prophesies the smiting of Aram (vv. 14-19)

14- Now Elisha was fallen sick of his sickness whereof he died. And Joash the king of Israel came down unto him, and wept over his face, and said, O my father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof. 15- And Elisha said unto him, Take bow and arrows. And he took unto him bow and arrows. 16- And he said to the king of Israel, Put thine hand upon the bow. And he put his hand upon it: and Elisha put his hands upon the king’s hands. 17- And he said, Open the window eastward. And he opened it. Then Elisha said, Shoot. And he shot. And he said, The arrow of the LORD’S deliverance, and the arrow of deliverance from Syria: for thou shalt smite the Syrians in Aphek, till thou have consumed them. 18- And he said, Take the arrows. And he took them. And he said unto the king of Israel, Smite upon the ground. And he smote thrice, and stayed. 19- And the man of God was wroth with him, and said, Thou shouldest have smitten five or six times; then hadst thou smitten Syria till thou hadst consumed it: whereas now thou shalt smite Syria but thrice.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: When Joash king of Israel learned of Elisha’s illness and his approaching death (Elisha was then eighty years old), Joash hurried to him and was deeply moved by the nearness of his departure, and he began to weep beside him until his tears fell on Elisha’s face, and perhaps he was kissing him in great grief. He called to him, “My father, my father,” declaring his submission to him, and he proclaimed to him the well-known words that Elisha had said to Elijah, that he was the chariot of Israel and its horsemen, that is, that he was the true power in the kingdom of Israel, because he was the man of God and his voice. But this passing emotional feeling does not accord with the whole life of Joash, for he walked in evil and worshiped idols.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Elisha said to him, “Take bow and arrows,” and he did so. Then he said to him, “Put your hand upon the bow,” and he drew the bow.
And Elisha put his hand upon the king’s hand, as a sign of the work of God in the war and the victory.

Of course the king’s guards had arrows and bows with them; he took them from them and did as Elisha commanded him. The obedience of the king appears in his submission to Elisha. His obedience represents human striving, while the hand of Elisha upon the king’s hand represents the grace and power of God, which support those who obey the commandments of God.

And here we see that God uses visual aids in conveying His prophecy to the king through the mouth of Elisha, in order to confirm the prophecy and fix it in the heart and faith of the king, as He did with many prophets, such as Jeremiah and Ezekiel, and He uses them with us through the events of our life, that we may know Him and walk with Him.

God had promised Elijah (1 Kgs 19:17) that whoever escaped the sword of Hazael Jehu would slay, and whoever escaped the sword of Jehu Elisha would slay. Although Elisha did not kill anyone, he points in this verse to the sword of the word of God in the hand of Elisha, with which he rebuked the wicked and led all to repentance, whether kings and princes or the people. The sword of Elisha also appears in his support of the kings with the power of God and in the smiting of their enemies, as he supported Jehoshaphat (ch. 3:18) in the smiting of Moab, and as he supported Joash in the smiting of Aram, as appears in this verse.

You must do your duty in spiritual striving against sin and for the acquiring of every virtue, so that you may enjoy the help and support of God, and take care to keep His commandments and obey them, and then His grace will support you.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Aphek: a city east of the Jordan, the same as modern Aphek, which is also called Afiq. It lies five kilometers east of the Sea of Galilee.

Then he said to him, “Open the window eastward,” and he opened it, because the Arameans, the enemies of Israel, dwell to the east of them. And Elisha said, “Shoot,” and he shot the arrow, and Elisha said, “The arrow of the LORD’s deliverance, the arrow of victory over Aram, for you shall smite Aram in Aphek and make an end of them.” It was well known in war that the commander of the army would shoot an arrow into the midst of the city, and the soldiers would move to battle; and the meaning of this is that Joash’s shooting of the arrow, in obedience to Elisha, meant a declaration of war on Aram. This is the first lesson that Elisha taught Joash, that is, obedience to God and confidence that God will not leave him; as for the second lesson, it comes in the next two verses.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Then Elisha said, “Take the arrows,” and he took them, and Elisha said to the king, “Smite upon the ground,” and he smote upon the ground three times, and then stopped.

It appears from this that the king understood from the previous verse that he would be victorious over Aram, and so the striking of the arrows on the ground meant the smiting of Aram; he struck three times only and stopped, and this means the following:
1- The king’s limited faith in the power of God, which would support him in smiting Aram and gaining victory over it; for he did not strike many arrows, but stopped striking quickly.

2- The weakness of his zeal in resisting the enemies to the end, that is, his lack of effort to crush and destroy them. Perhaps there was some slackness in his heart, or he feared that Assyria would make war on him if he destroyed Aram, that is, that Assyria would fear Joash and so fight him and destroy him; or perhaps he wanted two opposing powers, Aram and Assyria, to remain so as to ensure some security. These were human thoughts and a weakness of reliance on God. And this is the second lesson that Elisha wanted to teach the king, which is to strive with all one’s strength, believing in the supporting grace of God, and so to gain complete victory; for according to the measure of one’s striving one receives power from God.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Elisha was angry with Joash and said, If you had struck five or six times, you would have made an end of Aram until they were completely destroyed; but now you will continue your victories over them only three times.

God wanted to save His people with a complete salvation, but Joash was unwilling to do what was needed to achieve that. Is not the conduct of Joash like that of those who content themselves with the very least in their spiritual relationship with the Lord, ignoring the means of spiritual growth, unwilling to strive to climb the ladder of the virtues?
(4) The bones of Elisha bring a dead man to life (vv. 20, 21)
20- And Elisha died, and they buried him. And the bands of the Moabites invaded the land at the coming in of the year.

21- And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, that, behold, they spied a band of men; and they cast the man into the sepulchre of Elisha: and when the man was let down, and touched the bones of Elisha, he revived, and stood up on his feet.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: At the coming in of the year: that is, after a year had passed since the death of Elisha, or it may mean that the Moabites used to attack the kingdom of Israel at the beginning of every year.

Elisha died and was buried, and that was in the year 834 B.C., that is, at the end of the ninth century B.C., and the Church celebrates the feast of his departure on the twentieth of Paoni. It happened at that time, a year after the death of Elisha, that Moab invaded the land of Israel.
This shows the weakness of the kingdom of Israel, for the peoples around it made war on it and penetrated deep into its land.

And we notice that after the death of Elisha the Moabites invade Israel and their invasions are repeated, and this shows that the power of God that was in Elisha had left the people, so that they were exposed to many attacks by enemies, because protection had been removed from them. And despite the promise of God of victory over Aram, we find other enemies, the Moabites, attacking the land. This means the need to be on guard against all the enemies who can fight us from different directions, and not against a single enemy or a single sin.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: While the Jews were carrying a dead man to bury him, they were surprised by the Moabites attacking their land, so they threw the dead man into the nearest grave they came upon and fled. This grave was the grave of Elisha, and when the body of the dead man touched the bones of Elisha, he received power from God, which raised him alive, so that God might show His power in His saints even after their death. And here we see Elisha raising a dead man in his lifetime, the son of the Shunammite, and after his death in this incident. By this Elisha is a type of Christ, who raised the dead while He was on earth, and by His death saves us and raises us from the death of sin and gives us eternal life.

And the raising of this dead man after the death of Elisha and his parting from his people proclaims hope to the people that God is able to raise them, if they worship Him and obey the words of His prophets.

And as God honored Elijah by his ascent to heaven, so also He showed the greatness of Elisha by raising a dead man by the touch of his bones after his death, and this is clear evidence of the intercession of the saints.
The raising of a dead man by the bones of a dead man is the only incident of this kind in the Holy Bible, and it proclaims the following:
1- A reminder to the people of the words of Elisha, that they might obey him and submit to God.
2- That God is present in the midst of His people, even after the death of His prophets, and is ready to act, if the people submit to Him.

The bodies of the saints are a great blessing; they remind us of their lives and urge us to imitate them, relying on their prayers for us. So take care to befriend the saints and to receive the blessing of their bodies, that they may help you in your spiritual striving.
(5) Hazael oppresses the king of Israel (vv. 22-25)

22- But Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz. 23- And the LORD was gracious unto them, and had compassion on them, and had respect unto them, because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy them, neither cast he them from his presence as yet. 24- So Hazael king of Syria died; and Benhadad his son reigned in his stead.

25- And Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz took again out of the hand of Benhadad the son of Hazael the cities, which he had taken out of the hand of Jehoahaz his father by war. Three times did Joash beat him, and recovered the cities of Israel.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Returning to verse 3 of this chapter and Hazael’s oppression of the children of Israel in the days of Jehoahaz, and verse 5, in which the Lord gave Israel a saviour who freed them from the dominion of Hazael; this saviour was Joash the son of Jehoahaz.
Here the description of the situation in which the children of Israel were, and the Lord’s deliverance of them, is repeated.

Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel throughout the reign of Jehoahaz. And because the Lord is compassionate and gracious toward His people, He was distressed at their distress, as the Scripture says, “In all their affliction he was afflicted.” The Lord remembered His covenant with their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and was unwilling to destroy them until that time, or to cast them away. And He did not let Hazael annihilate them. But when they persisted in evil, He was compelled to allow them to be taken captive by Assyria, and that was about a hundred years later.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Hazael king of Aram died, and his son Benhadad sat on the throne of Aram after him.

entries.section: (3) The bribing of the king of Aram and then the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: Joash the son of Jehoahaz recovered the Israelite cities that Hazael had taken in war. Three battles took place between Joash and Benhadad, in all of which Joash was victorious, and he was able to impose his control over those cities again. By this the word of Elisha was fulfilled, when he saw that he had struck only three arrows to the ground, and said to him that he would smite Aram only three times and would not destroy them.

How does this king, who had turned away from the worship of the Lord, become an instrument for the salvation of his people? This is the work of grace. When a person humbles himself before God and a sign of repentance and contrition of heart appears in him, the Lord hastens to offer every help to pluck that soul out of the captivity of sin. Salvation is offered even to the most wretched and the most unworthy of people, so take courage, whatever your sins, and offer repentance, for God loves you and will receive you, and even work through you.
Amaziah and Azariah kings of Judah, and Joash and Jeroboam kings of Israel

entries.section: (1) Amaziah as king over Judah

paragraphs.text: Joash king of Judah was followed in ascending the throne by his son Amaziah. This was in the second year of Joash the son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, which was the second year of his reigning alone, because he had shared in the rule with his father Jehoahaz for about three years.

entries.section: (1) Amaziah as king over Judah

paragraphs.text: He was twenty-five years old when he took the throne, and his reign lasted twenty-nine years, the first fifteen of which coincided with the reign of Joash king of Israel, which was exactly fourteen years and a few months. The capital of his kingdom was the city of Jerusalem. The name of his mother was “Jehoaddan,” of the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

We notice in the history of the kings the role of mothers in the conduct of their children. When the mothers are from Jerusalem, we rarely see the sons turning aside after false gods; but as for pagan mothers, their evil influence is clear in their sons the kings, who worshiped idols and led their peoples astray. The only exception to this is the case of the last four kings before the captivity, when the whole people had sunk low and was occupied with the worship of idols, for their mothers were from the kingdom of Judah.

In your marriage, give attention to a godly wife, who knows God and loves the Church, to secure a holy life in your home, which you and your children will enjoy, and to raise a righteous generation that rejoices the heart of God and rejoices you.

entries.section: (1) Amaziah as king over Judah

paragraphs.text: Amaziah strove to do what was right before the Lord, like Joash his father. But his righteousness did not reach what his great forefather David had reached; that is, he cared about the worship of God in His Temple, but there was some laxity, as will appear in the following verses, and he kept the Law, as appears in (vv. 5, 6).

entries.section: (1) Amaziah as king over Judah

paragraphs.text: One of the things held against him is that he let the people practice their worship of offering sacrifices and burning incense on the high places, even if it was to the true God and not to idols. All the kings from the days of Solomon fell into this error, and it encouraged some of the kings to worship idols on the high places; therefore it is considered no small error.

Do not imitate the people of the world in their habits and mix the conduct of the children of God with the conduct of the people of the world, for then Satan would have a part of your heart; for God wants you to love Him with all your heart and to walk in all your life in a way that pleases Him, and so you will receive all His blessing.

entries.section: (1) Amaziah as king over Judah

paragraphs.text: When the rule was firmly in the hand of Amaziah, he commanded the execution of the men who had killed his father, but he followed what the Law commands in this matter, which is not to kill fathers for the sins of their sons, nor to kill sons for sins committed by their fathers; every person is responsible for the sin he committed himself and is not condemned for the faults of his father or his son (Deut 24:16). This is an upright act that shows the goodness of Amaziah; for most likely some of his servants proposed to him that the sons be killed as well, as was the custom in the past among pagan peoples, to make sure that no one would rebel against him, taking vengeance for his father, but he held to the Law.

entries.section: (1) Amaziah as king over Judah

paragraphs.text: The Valley of Salt: south of the Dead Sea (the Salt Sea). Selah-Joktheel: a fortified city lying on the top of a mountain near the foot of Mount Hor. The name of the fortress of Selah today is Umm al-Bayyara.

The Edomites, whom the king had subdued, had rebelled against Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat, and he fought them, as the Second Book of Chronicles mentions (2 Chr 25:5-14). So Amaziah led his army and went toward the Valley of Salt and killed ten thousand of Edom and took the city of Selah and changed its name to the name by which it remained until the writing of this book, which is Joktheel.

entries.section: (2) Joash king of Israel defeats Amaziah, and then dies

paragraphs.text: After Amaziah triumphed over Edom (v. 7) he became proud, and then some soldiers from the kingdom of Israel attacked him and killed and plundered some of the inhabitants of the kingdom of Judah (2 Chr 25:5-16), and he was greatly angered and decided to make war on the kingdom of Israel, the northern kingdom, whose capital was Samaria.

And he sent to Joash to prepare himself, for he would fight him. It is clear from this that Amaziah relied on his own strength and not on God, indeed he drew away from God; for after his victory over Edom he did not glorify God, but took some of the idols of Edom and bowed down to them (2 Chr 25:14).

entries.section: (2) Joash king of Israel defeats Amaziah, and then dies

paragraphs.text: The thistle: a short, weak thorny plant that grows in Lebanon.
The cedar: the greatest of the trees of Lebanon; it is a strong and tall tree, indeed one of the greatest trees in the world, evergreen, and ships are made from it.

After the victory of Joash king of Israel over the Arameans (ch. 13:25) he became proud, so when Amaziah king of Judah sent to challenge him and make war on him, he was greatly angered and replied to him with a parable in which he mocks Amaziah. He compared Amaziah to the weak thistle that sent to the cedar tree asking that his son marry its daughter, as though the two were on one level, and forgot that he was a mere thistle. So he reminds Amaziah of his weakness and lowliness when compared with the king of Israel and his mighty army, which he compared to a wild beast that passed by and trampled the thistle and crushed it; that is, he reminds Amaziah of his weakness and that he cannot stand before the mighty army of Israel.

entries.section: (2) Joash king of Israel defeats Amaziah, and then dies

paragraphs.text: Then Joash king of Israel said in his message to Amaziah king of Judah that he had become proud after his victory over Edom and thought that he could face the army of Israel, and he advised him to keep his glory and greatness by staying at home, that is, Jerusalem, and warned him that if he fought the army of Israel he and the army of Judah would be defeated, and told him that he was doing himself harm if he attacked one stronger than himself. Joash said this with pride. It is true that the army of Israel was stronger, but it is nothing before the army of the kingdom of Assyria or the army of Egypt; but it is pride that makes a person forget himself, so that he rushes to challenge and collide with others. The purpose of the war was pride and nothing else; otherwise Amaziah would have attacked Israel suddenly to recover what they had plundered from him.

Do not rush in pride and challenge others and fall into the snares of the devil and lose the protection of God. Be humble and bear with others, even the proud among them, and God will support you and you will keep your peace.

entries.section: (2) Joash king of Israel defeats Amaziah, and then dies

paragraphs.text: Beth-shemesh: on the northern border of the land of Judah, twenty miles west of Jerusalem.

Amaziah did not listen to those warnings, and so the two armies met at Beth-shemesh, one of the cities of Judah. We notice that it was the army of Israel that came by the coastal road and then attacked the kingdom of Judah at the city of Beth-shemesh, which is on the road to Jerusalem, and that shows the strength of the army of Israel.

entries.section: (2) Joash king of Israel defeats Amaziah, and then dies

paragraphs.text: Judah was defeated before Israel and the soldiers of the army of Judah fled to their homes.

This was a punishment from God, because Judah, after their victory over Edom, worshiped the gods of Edom, as is stated in (2 Chr 25:20). The Lord is with us as long as we are with Him; if we forsake Him, He forsakes us.

entries.section: (2) Joash king of Israel defeats Amaziah, and then dies

paragraphs.text: The gate of Ephraim and the corner gate: they are in the northwest of the wall of Jerusalem.

Joash king of Israel, after his victory over the army of Judah, was able to seize Amaziah king of Judah at Beth-shemesh, and then took him with him to Jerusalem and broke down part of the wall of the city between the gate of Ephraim and the corner gate, so that Jerusalem would be left without protection. Joash did not intend to enter the city, for he had defeated its army and entered it easily with its king captured under his hand, but he only wanted to humiliate Jerusalem and make it weak, without walls.

entries.section: (2) Joash king of Israel defeats Amaziah, and then dies

paragraphs.text: Hostages: probably a group of the great men of Judah, or of the royal line. Then Joash entered Jerusalem and took all that remained in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and the house of the king of gold and silver, because most of it had been given by Joash king of Judah to Hazael so that he would not make war on Jerusalem (ch. 12:18); then he took a group of the great men of Judah as hostages with him and released King Amaziah to live humbled in Jerusalem, for if he tried to rebel against Joash, Joash would kill the great men of Judah held captive by him. Then Joash returned afterward to Samaria and did not need to leave any of his army in Jerusalem, because he was confident of the weakness of Amaziah, and he also needed his army for his wars with the Arameans.

entries.section: (2) Joash king of Israel defeats Amaziah, and then dies

paragraphs.text: The rest of what Joash did, his excess in evil and the details of his war against Amaziah king of Judah, are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel, which is not the Book of Chronicles found in the Holy Bible. Then Joash died and was buried with his fathers in Samaria, and his son Jeroboam took the throne after him; he is called Jeroboam II, to distinguish him from Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the first to split the kingdom of Israel from Judah.

entries.section: (3) The death of Amaziah and the reign of Azariah over Judah

paragraphs.text: The life of Amaziah extended fifteen years after the death of Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, which is exactly fourteen years and a few months, because the total period of the reign of Amaziah was twenty-nine years. The Holy Bible mentions that Amaziah lived fifteen years and does not say that he reigned, because he lived humbled, with a broken spirit, after his defeat at the hand of Joash and the taking of hostages who may have been of his own offspring and of the great men of Judah, in addition to the taking of the gold and silver, so that he became poor. And that was after his turning away from God and his bowing down to the gods of Edom, so he was defeated and humbled.

entries.section: (3) The death of Amaziah and the reign of Azariah over Judah

paragraphs.text: Everything connected with the acts of Amaziah is recorded in “the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah.”

entries.section: (3) The death of Amaziah and the reign of Azariah over Judah

paragraphs.text: Lachish: a fortified city about thirty-five miles southwest of Jerusalem.

The servants of the king sensed his weakness and conspired to kill him. King Amaziah sensed this, so he left Jerusalem and fled to Lachish, but they followed him there and killed him, just as his father too had been killed in a conspiracy of his servants (ch. 12:20).

entries.section: (3) The death of Amaziah and the reign of Azariah over Judah

paragraphs.text: His men carried him on horses to Jerusalem, where he was buried with his fathers in the city of David.

We notice here the disgrace and contempt with which Amaziah was treated: they did not set him in a chariot like the other kings, but laid only his corpse on the horses, and then he was not buried in the tombs of the kings, but only in the city of David.

entries.section: (3) The death of Amaziah and the reign of Azariah over Judah

paragraphs.text: The people of Judah crowned Azariah the son of Amaziah to succeed to the throne of his father. His age at that time was sixteen years.

entries.section: (3) The death of Amaziah and the reign of Azariah over Judah

paragraphs.text: Elath: a town at the northern tip of the Gulf of Aqaba, near Ezion-geber, a seaport and trading port; it is modern Eilat.
Among his important works was the recovery of the city of Elath from Edom and his rebuilding of it, and that was after the death of his father Amaziah.

Thank God for His support of you and all His gifts, for He is ready to work with you beyond what you ask or think; but if you are lax in giving thanks, the devil will tempt you with the thoughts of the world and draw you away from God, so that your sense of His presence lessens and you lose His help, and then you suffer many troubles.

entries.section: (4) Jeroboam as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Amaziah king of Judah, Jeroboam the son of Joash became king over Israel. The capital of his kingdom was Samaria, and his rule lasted forty-one years. He was the third generation of Jehu. The reign of Jeroboam was strong, and he was the greatest of the kings of Israel in the aspects of civilization: he built houses of hewn stone and planted many vineyards and made an alliance with Assyria, and his army was strong. But his age was accompanied by spiritual decline, and the worship of idols, fornication and drunkenness spread, as is understood from the prophecies of Hosea, Joel and Amos, who were his contemporaries.

entries.section: (4) Jeroboam as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Jeroboam the son of Joash was a wicked king; he permitted the worship of idols, and evil lusts prevailed in his days, such as fornication, drunkenness and the oppression of the poor, in addition to his continuing in the worship of the idols that Jeroboam the son of Nebat had set up.

entries.section: (4) Jeroboam as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: The sea of the plain: the Sea of Lot.
Jonah the son of Amittai: he is the prophet mentioned in the Book of Jonah.
Gath-hepher: it lies near Nazareth and is perhaps the present al-Mashhad, about three miles northeast of Nazareth, and in it is a tomb said to be the tomb of Jonah.
This king was able to recover a large area of land and to annex it again to the kingdom of Israel; this extended strip of land lay between the walls of the city of Hamath and the Dead Sea.

The biblical text teaches us that Jonah the prophet had already prophesied this victory, which was followed by the taking possession of these lands, but this prophecy of Jonah is not recorded in his book in the Holy Bible.

entries.section: (4) Jeroboam as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Shut up: it means children and minors.
Left: adults who move about freely and travel everywhere.

The mercy of God on His people Israel appears, although they were still in their sins, but God had pity on them by supporting Jeroboam, who was mighty, so that wars quieted in his days, that is, the kingdom of Israel was not attacked, and the people lived in freedom and tranquility; and God, by His pity, meant to call them to repentance.

God loves you even while you are in your sins and gives you many blessings, to show you His love and call you to live with Him and to leave your sins, which draw you away from Him; that is, He puts you to shame by His fatherhood and tenderness.

entries.section: (4) Jeroboam as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: The Lord did not decree the blotting out of Israel and the destruction of its people, because of His longsuffering and mercy, and so He used Jeroboam the son of Joash for their deliverance. The Lord decided to bring about deliverance for His people by the hand of this king, who afterward brought wrath upon himself by continuing in evil. The patience of God with His people appears here; because the cup of the wrath of God had not yet been filled, He gives them an opportunity to return to Him, but in the end He will chastise them with captivity, that is, the killing of many and the enslaving of the rest.

entries.section: (4) Jeroboam as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Damascus: the capital of Aram, that is, present-day Syria.

Hamath, which belonged to Judah: it is the city of Hamath that is in the kingdom of Israel, that is, the northern kingdom, but it is attributed here to Judah because David subdued it and it paid tribute to him, and David was of the tribe of Judah, so it was attributed to Judah; so what is meant by Judah here is the kingdom of Israel and not the southern kingdom. The details of the war to recover the lands and all the other acts of Jeroboam and his excess in evil are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

entries.section: (4) Jeroboam as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Jeroboam died and was buried with his fathers the kings of Israel. His son Zechariah sat on the throne of Israel after him, the fourth and last generation of Jehu, and by this the word of God was fulfilled, that the descendants of Jehu would reign to the fourth generation. Azariah and Jotham kings of Judah, and Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah and Pekah kings of Israel

entries.section: (1) Azariah as king over Judah

paragraphs.text: Azariah: Uzziah (2 Chr 26:1). At the death of Amaziah his son Azariah succeeded him on the throne, as was stated before in the previous chapter (v. 21), and that was in the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam II king of Israel. The age of Azariah at that time was sixteen years, and his reign lasted fifty-two years, and Jerusalem was the capital of his kingdom. The name of his mother was “Jecholiah,” of Jerusalem.

But it is to be noted that Amaziah died in the fifteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam (ch. 14:17), and so there is a period of twelve years between the death of Amaziah and the reign of his son Azariah, because Azariah began to reign in the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam. During these twelve years Uzziah was king but a child, and a council of regency was the one that managed the kingdom. In the sixteenth year of Azariah the regency ended and Azariah ruled alone for fifty-two years, that is, he died at the age of sixty-eight.

entries.section: (1) Azariah as king over Judah

paragraphs.text: He followed the steps of his father Amaziah in doing what was right, but the matter of offering sacrifices to God on the high places remained as it was, and the people continued to offer and burn incense on them.
It is beautiful that King Azariah did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, and this is due to two things:
1- His mother was from the kingdom of Judah, from Jerusalem, and it seems that she held fast to the worship of the Lord.

2- The council of regency over the child king Azariah most likely played a good role in leading the kingdom in the worship of God, and so the king, when he came to rule alone at the age of sixteen, continued the worship of God and did what was right in His eyes.

entries.section: (1) Azariah as king over Judah

paragraphs.text: After Azariah was able to build cities and lead his kingdom successfully, he became proud, so that he entered the Holy Place, which may be entered only by the priests, and the Lord struck him with leprosy (2 Chr 26:16-21), and he was confined in a separate house, because he was a king, instead of dwelling in a tent outside the walls of the city (Lev 13:46). With the isolation of Azariah in the house of the sick, the throne became vacant, and Jotham the son of Azariah reigned in the lifetime of his father, and then the reign of Jotham extended another sixteen years alone. The books of Amos and Zechariah mention an earthquake in the days of Azariah (Amos 1:1; Zech 14:5), and most likely this earthquake occurred when the king dared to enter the Holy Place to burn incense on the altar of incense, and God struck him with leprosy.

entries.section: (1) Azariah as king over Judah

paragraphs.text: The rest of the acts of Azariah are all written in “the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah.”

entries.section: (1) Azariah as king over Judah

paragraphs.text: Azariah died and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Jotham took the throne after him. It is not mentioned that he was buried in the tombs of the kings, and perhaps that was because of his leprosy, which remained with him until the end of his life, and this disease represents uncleanness.

Pride lowers a person’s dignity and loses him the care of God, and so he is afflicted with many troubles. So why, my brother, do you attribute the glory to yourself when you achieve success? Thank God and glorify Him, and your success will increase, and you will keep your humility and remain in joy.

entries.section: (2) Zechariah as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Zechariah the son of Jeroboam took the throne of Israel; he represents the fourth and last generation of the descendants of Jehu who ruled Israel, exactly as the Lord said to Jehu, to the fourth generation (2 Kgs 10:30). His taking the throne was in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah. He reigned in Samaria, and his rule lasted only six months.
After the death of Jeroboam II, civil conflicts arose that delayed Zechariah’s sitting on the throne of the kingdom for some years, most likely twelve years, and then Zechariah reigned after that.

entries.section: (2) Zechariah as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Zechariah continued in his evil lusts, such as the worship of the gods of the surrounding pagan nations and various works of uncleanness, in addition to the worship of the idols that Jeroboam the son of Nebat had set up; therefore God allowed him to reign only six months, because of the multitude of his evils.

entries.section: (2) Zechariah as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Shallum the son of Jabesh plotted a conspiracy and killed King Zechariah, and then reigned in his place.

Shallum reigned by a conspiracy and the killing of another, and works that rest on treachery, betrayal and evil of course anger God and expose their doer to many troubles. So do not use any wrong means to achieve your aims, because the end does not justify the means. Be godly in your goals and also in your means, and rely on God, and He will support you in all your steps.

entries.section: (2) Zechariah as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: The rest of the affairs of Zechariah and his acts are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

entries.section: (2) Zechariah as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: What happened was a fulfillment of the word of the Lord, which He had said before to Jehu, the founder of the ruling house, which continued to sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation, that is, the descendants of Jehu, who were Jehoahaz, then Joash, followed by Jeroboam II, and in the end Zechariah.

entries.section: (3) Shallum as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: A full month: what is meant is one month, that is, thirty days.

Shallum is the one who rebelled against Zechariah the son of Jeroboam (v. 10) and killed him and seized the throne of Israel for himself. His reign began in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and his rule lasted only one month.

God hates violence and hardness of heart, so do not hasten toward it, lest violence strike you also. And do not use your power to achieve your interests against the commandments of God, because God is able and is the avenger of the blood of His servants.

entries.section: (3) Shallum as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Tirzah: a large city lying in the north of Ephraim. It was a capital of Israel in ancient times, before the time of Omri king of Israel, who founded Samaria.

It seems that parties had formed within the kingdom of Israel during the period when the throne of the kingdom was vacant after Jeroboam II, so that although Zechariah reigned, one of the parties rose up and killed the king and Shallum reigned in his place, and then another party, centered in Tirzah, rose against King Shallum and killed him, and Menahem reigned in his place.

entries.section: (3) Shallum as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: The rest of the affairs of Shallum and the details of the conspiracy that he led are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

entries.section: (3) Shallum as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Tiphsah: modern Tiphsah, lying ten kilometers southwest of Nablus (Shechem). Menahem attacked Tiphsah and its surroundings and destroyed what was in it, as far as the border of Tirzah, because its inhabitants had shut the gates of the city in his face and had not opened its gates to him. He was not content to destroy the city, but committed atrocities against its people, for he ripped up its women with child, and that was because the city of Tiphsah was loyal to King Shallum and his party.

entries.section: (4) Menahem as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: When Menahem seized the throne of Israel after killing Shallum the son of Jabesh, it was in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah. The capital of his kingdom was Samaria. And he reigned ten years.

entries.section: (4) Menahem as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Menahem walked in evil and the worship of idols, like Jeroboam the son of Nebat, throughout the period of his rule, and in this he led his people astray and led them in the worship of idols and unclean lusts.

entries.section: (4) Menahem as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: A talent of silver: it had various weights ranging from twenty to forty kilograms. During his reign Pul king of Assyria came invading. Menahem worked to avoid his attack on the land of Israel by giving him a thousand talents of silver to confirm him on the throne, and in this Menahem became a slave of the king of Assyria, that is, he could reign only under the protection of the king of Assyria.

The Lord did not overlook the extreme cruelty with which Menahem treated the inhabitants of the city of Tiphsah. So He brings a nation from afar to punish Menahem for his evil deeds. God neither slumbers nor sleeps, and He repays evils to those who do them.

entries.section: (4) Menahem as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: The shekel of silver: the ordinary shekel is 5.8 grams and the shekel of the sanctuary is 11.6 grams.

He imposed a sum of fifty shekels of silver on every man, collecting it from the wealthy, to pay it to the king of Assyria to appease him. So the king of Assyria turned back and did not occupy the land of Israel. But he returned afterward and attacked the kingdom of Israel, and this was the beginning of the Assyrian attacks, which ended in the complete captivity of the kingdom of Israel.

entries.section: (4) Menahem as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: The rest of the accounts of Menahem and all that he did are written in the “book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.”

entries.section: (4) Menahem as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Menahem died and was buried with his fathers, and his son Pekahiah succeeded him.

entries.section: (5) Pekahiah as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Inheritance was not the normal situation for the kings of Israel, but it continued for a period with the descendants of Jehu to Zechariah; then the kingship became again a matter of violence, that is, each one killing his predecessor, until Menahem, who died, and his son Pekahiah inherited the kingship after him; his capital was Samaria and his reign lasted two years, and the beginning of the reign of Pekahiah was the fiftieth year of King Azariah of Judah.

entries.section: (5) Pekahiah as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: Pekahiah continued in evil like his father Menahem, that is, the worship of idols, lusts and injustice, and he persisted in the worship of the idols that Jeroboam the son of Nebat had set up, and in this he led his people in the worship of idols and every evil.

If you are in a position of responsibility or a leader, beware; for your sins greatly affect those around you, and they imitate you and so you draw them away from God. The sin of stumbling others is a great sin, and the Lord Christ affirms that its punishment is destruction, so be careful in your conduct, and if you err, apologize, and if you notice that someone has stumbled, explain to him and care for him, so that you do not draw him away from God.

entries.section: (5) Pekahiah as king over Israel

paragraphs.text: A captain: a great commander very close to the king, the third who rides with the king in his chariot.

Pekah the son of Remaliah was a great commander close to King Pekahiah, and he had power in the kingdom, so he was considered its real mover. He was strong in character, as shown by the fact that his reign lasted twenty years afterward, and he had a political opinion, which was independence from Assyria, because Menahem and his son Pekahiah had submitted to Assyria and paid it tribute. Pekah allied himself with Rezin king of Aram to break away from Assyria and tried to bring Ahaz king of Judah in with him, but the latter refused. And when he found that Pekahiah did not want to break away from Assyria, Pekah rose against him and killed him and killed two of his aides, Argob and Arieh. In this conspiracy Pekah had with him fifty men of the Gileadites, and perhaps Pekah was from Gilead; therefore he sought the help of the Gileadites, and so the conspiracy was carried out and Pekahiah died, and Pekah the son of Remaliah reigned in his place.

entries.section: (5) Pekahiah as king over Israel
