paragraphs.text: After Sennacherib proudly declared in the previous verse his dominion over the kings and rulers of the nations, here, in this verse, he declares his authority over all the peoples of the earth. He says proudly, "I." His drinking strange waters means that he had seized many countries foreign to him, and taken their goods and drunk their waters. Also Egypt, the empire that preceded him and still a strong state: he declares that he entered it with his very great armies and drank its waters until there was no water left in it, and trampled its rivers with the soles of his soldiers' feet, declaring his dominion, his strength and his enormous hosts. These words, too, Sennacherib did not write or declare, as we mentioned in the previous verse.

entries.section: (4) The Lord's answer through Isaiah

paragraphs.text: Hills: plural of hill, which is elevated ground.

Sennacherib said proudly before to Hezekiah in (v. 11), Have you not heard of the power of the kings of Assyria, which shattered all the surrounding peoples? Now God answers the king of Assyria and says to him: Have you not heard what I have done? From of old, that is, from eternity, I planned in My design to make you, Sennacherib, an instrument for shattering peoples. You are merely an instrument in My hand, but you exalted yourself against Me and thought yourself something when many nations submitted to you. And God asks the king of Assyria: Have you not heard of My power in the prophecies of My prophets and My work with My people? How then did you dare to stand before Me and be proud against Me? I divided the Red Sea and indeed dried up the ground in the days of Moses, and likewise in the days of Joshua I stopped the waters in the river Jordan, but you speak of delusions and did not truly dry up the sea.

entries.section: (4) The Lord's answer through Isaiah

paragraphs.text: Blasted: plants that dried up and were burned by the hot wind that blew upon them.

God describes the inhabitants of the countries that the king of Assyria invaded as weak, likening them to people with short hands, unable to defend themselves, because they depend on idols and not on God. He likens them also, when Assyria attacked them and they were afraid and pierced, to weak grass that grows in the fields, and to tender, weak green plants in the beginning of their growth, before they have strong stalks and fruit. He likens them also to the grass on the housetops, which is weak and short because it has no depth; and finally he likens them to small plants whose growth was not complete, upon which hot winds blew, drying them and burning them.

entries.section: (4) The Lord's answer through Isaiah

paragraphs.text: God addresses the king of Assyria, saying that He sees everything: He sees all his movements, his deeds, his words, his pride and his exalting himself against God. God is longsuffering, hoping that he may repent, but of course He will punish him as long as he persists in this pride.

entries.section: (4) The Lord's answer through Isaiah

paragraphs.text: Hook: a metal ring put in the nose of slaves to humiliate them.
Bridle: a piece of iron put in the mouth of a horse to lead it as its rider wishes.

God said to Sennacherib: I have heard your pride and your rage against Me, I who dwell on high, and this pride has come up to Me; and of course I will punish you, as you punished many kings when you seized them and put hooks in their noses. This idea had been devised by the kings of the Assyrians to humiliate those whom they conquered, so now God does it to them, or speaks to them with it, and they understand it; that is, God will humble the king of Assyria like a lowly slave, then master him as the rider masters the horse, and bring him back to his country fleeing before the power of God, as we shall see at the end of this chapter.

Do not be proud toward those around you, for you are being proud toward God; and if, in His longsuffering, He gives you opportunities for repentance, do not waste them, lest He punish you and you be brought down to the ground in lowliness and humiliation.

entries.section: (4) The Lord's answer through Isaiah

paragraphs.text: Aftergrowth: fruit gathered from the same plant that was sown in the land in the previous year. After the harvest is gathered in the first year, the stalks of the plants are left in the ground and give fruit in the following year; this is called aftergrowth.
That which springs of the same: grains that fall during the harvest and give plants and fruit as aftergrowth.

Then God gave Hezekiah signs to reassure him that He was with him and would not forsake him. After Hezekiah is rid of the Assyrians by the power of God, God also takes care to feed His people, so He permits seed to fall while the Assyrians gather the harvests of the Jews, and this seed grows into plants and gives a harvest sufficient for all the Jews remaining in the kingdom of Judah in this year. Then in the following year He makes the same plants bear fruit, sufficient also for His people in the following year, because the following year was a seventh year, in which the Law forbids cultivating the land and it is left to rest; so God, without any sowing, will make the same plants give aftergrowth for His people to eat. It is known in agriculture that the aftergrowth is less and weaker than in the first year, but by the blessing of God He makes the harvest abundant and sufficient for His people. In the third year, they begin to cultivate the land, because they will be secure in God's protection, having restored the fortification and renewal of their cities.

In this we see that God feels for His people, whom the Assyrians wronged, eating their food, so He gives them instead food sufficient for them that they did not sow: the self-sown grain, and then in the second year the aftergrowth.
This prophecy signifies God's blessing upon His people: although Assyria persecuted it and killed many, God blesses the remnant, so that they multiply and become a great nation.

Do not fear the trials that come upon you, or the wrong done to you by others, for God is able to compensate you many times over for all that you have lost. Be reassured, for you are under the protection of your God, who is able to do all things.

entries.section: (4) The Lord's answer through Isaiah

paragraphs.text: God promises His people that after the defeat of the wicked and their flight, the people who escaped destruction will return, and because of the blessings of their God they will become like strong, tall trees with spreading roots and will produce various fruits, as a sign of the revival of the people after the distress. Not only this, but the jealousy of the mighty Lord, the God of hosts, for His name and for His people (His bride) makes Him scatter His enemies and crush everyone who exalted himself against His bride. It can also be said that it is a prophecy about the Church: however weak it may seem at some times, persecuted and lacking strength, its heavenly Bridegroom will defend it, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.

Do not despair at the multitude of trials and the weakness that appears in you, and the multitude of your falls, and even the reproaches of the wicked, for all of them are temporary and will end, as long as you have taken refuge in God in repentance and contrition. He will compensate you for all that you have missed, and you will live with Him in strength and bear much spiritual fruit.

entries.section: (4) The Lord's answer through Isaiah

paragraphs.text: Shield: a piece of wood covered with leather, with a handle at the back into which the soldier puts his hand and moves it in front of his head and body to defend himself.
Siege mound (bank): a wall built by the enemy to take cover behind it and hurl stones or fire from behind it, and to prevent those leaving the besieged city from escaping.
Despite the strength of the Assyrian siege of Jerusalem, God reassures Hezekiah that the enemy will not be able to enter Jerusalem and use his weapons against it, but will return to his own country.

entries.section: (4) The Lord's answer through Isaiah

paragraphs.text: God affirms that He will protect His city Jerusalem for the glorifying of His holy name, which the enemies reproached. The second reason for protecting His city is His honoring of David, great in his godliness, from whose seed comes King Hezekiah who sits on his throne.
God honors His saints and answers their intercession; therefore we take refuge in them and ask for their mediation.

entries.section: (5) The destruction of Sennacherib and his army

paragraphs.text: It happened that night that the angel of the Lord came to the camp of the Assyrians and destroyed a hundred and eighty-five thousand of their soldiers. And when day broke, their corpses filled the camp. We notice that God's punishment was very swift: on the night of the very day on which God announced His punishment, He carried out the sentence on Sennacherib and his army, because their pride was great.

entries.section: (5) The destruction of Sennacherib and his army

paragraphs.text: Sennacherib was able to escape with a small number of his army, and he hurried to Nineveh, his capital.
Perhaps in this he thought that he had escaped the divine punishment, but a punishment awaited him that we cannot imagine, which we shall see in the next verse.

entries.section: (5) The destruction of Sennacherib and his army

paragraphs.text: Ararat: a plateau lying east of present-day Iraq, on which Noah's ark came to rest.

Sennacherib was in deep despair when he returned to Nineveh, so he took refuge in his god Nisroch in his temple, that he might support him, and bowed down before the idol. There God carried out His judgment, in a way Sennacherib did not expect, for his two sons attacked him and killed him with the sword, then fled to the plateau of Ararat.
Then another son of his, called Esarhaddon, reigned after him.
We notice that Hezekiah passed through three stages in his relationship with God in the face of the Assyrian attack:
1- He relied on himself, so he was afraid and sought a human solution; he declared his submission and servitude to the king of Assyria and sent him silver and gold (ch. 18:14-16).
2- When Sennacherib deceived him and attacked him and seized the cities of Judah and besieged Jerusalem, Hezekiah found nothing before him but to take refuge in God, that He might deliver him (v. 1).

3- When Sennacherib reproached the name of God and blasphemed it, Hezekiah asked God to intervene and defend His name, for he was attached to the love of God and jealous for His holy name (v. 16). In the beginning he relied on himself; the second time he felt his weakness and that of his people and his great need of God; but the third time his heart was attached to God and jealous for His holy name. So the distress made Hezekiah grow in his relationship with God.

The power of God is able to do all things and works beyond what a man thinks. Therefore do not be troubled, however great the power of your enemies who wrong you, for God is able to deliver you from their hands, in a way you do not expect.
The lengthening of Hezekiah's life, then his pride

entries.section: (1) God lengthens Hezekiah's life

paragraphs.text: Hezekiah fell gravely ill, and the prophet Isaiah visited him and informed him that he would die of this illness, and advised him to give his children and servants instructions about what he wanted.

entries.section: (1) God lengthens Hezekiah's life

paragraphs.text: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall to pray alone, his face thus being directed toward the temple, which his illness prevented him from reaching, and he implored the Lord, saying: Ah, Lord, remember how I have walked in uprightness and sincerity, and have done what is good in Your sight. And Hezekiah wept bitterly. He begged God to remove the illness from him and not to permit him to die. This shows Hezekiah's faith in God.

entries.section: (1) God lengthens Hezekiah's life

paragraphs.text: After Isaiah announced to Hezekiah that his death was at the door, he left the royal palace and walked in the city of Jerusalem, and minutes later, before he reached the middle of the city, God declared new words to him, that he should return and say them to Hezekiah. God's answer was very swift: He heard with concern the prayer of Hezekiah, which came from the depths of his heart and his contrition before God, which appeared in his tears. So He said to Isaiah: I will heal him of his illness quickly, so that he will recover completely and, after three days, will be able to fulfill his desire, which is to worship before Me and pray in My holy temple. God answers quickly the fervent prayers and spiritual longings, mingled with material requests, of His children who love Him; for Hezekiah does not want healing only, but to enjoy being in the temple of God and praying before Him there.

Hezekiah's illness unto death, then his healing after three days, is a type of the death of Christ and His resurrection, by which He gave us the grace of entering His sanctuary, that is, His Church, and partaking of her sacraments, and then entering the Kingdom, just as Hezekiah entered and prayed in the temple of God.

Hezekiah wept with tears that God might remove death from him, and Christ offered up prayers and supplications, with strong crying and tears, to Him who was able to save Him (Heb 5:7). Christ thus expresses the difficulty of the cup of suffering that He had to pass through for our redemption.

entries.section: (1) God lengthens Hezekiah's life

paragraphs.text: The Lord's answer was swift and specific, for He promised Hezekiah an additional fifteen years of life. This is divine generosity in giving, as long as the one who prays is one of His godly children. He also promises to deliver him from the king of Assyria and to preserve Jerusalem, Hezekiah's capital. Therefore many consider that this event, although it was written in the Bible after the killing of Sennacherib and his army, took place before that, that is, before the siege of Jerusalem, or at least during it. The illness and the healing may also have taken place after the victory over Sennacherib, and God's promise here would be to preserve him and his city from any other attack by Assyria.

God affirms that His preserving of Hezekiah and Jerusalem is for the glorifying of the name of God and for the sake of the prayers and blessing of David, the godly servant of God, and this confirms the doctrine of the intercession of the saints. Also God's saying, "I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria," shows that God delivers Jerusalem for the sake of Hezekiah's godliness, and this is a second confirmation of the intercession and blessing of the saints.
Here we see how God blesses His children and adds to their lifespan. By human nature, Hezekiah should have died, but God prolonged his days because of his godliness and God's love for him.

On the other hand, God does not bless the wicked. Sennacherib, the unjust and hard-hearted, because of his blasphemy against God, saw his army perish by divine destruction at the hand of the angel; then Sennacherib died in a way he could not have expected, killed by his two sons inside the temple of his pagan god, on whom he had relied, which became the cause of his destruction.

Ask God in faith, confident of His love for you, and He will give to you generously because He loves you. And seek the intercession of the saints, because they have a great standing with Him, and He rejoices in your friendship with them.

entries.section: (1) God lengthens Hezekiah's life

paragraphs.text: Boil: an abscess.

Isaiah gave the prescription for healing to those around the sick Hezekiah, which was that they should put a lump of figs on the abscess that he might recover; so they laid it on the boil, and Hezekiah was healed.

The lump of figs was not the source of the healing, but a visible material means through which the grace given by God can be felt. In the same way our Church, according to the commandments of the Gospel, practices the sacraments of the Church through visible material things behind which are hidden the divine graces that God grants to the one who receives the sacrament. In the sacraments, materials such as water and oil are used; and of old Elisha used salt and flour in his miracles, and Christ Himself used clay in healing the man born blind, because man needs tangible things to support his faith.

entries.section: (1) God lengthens Hezekiah's life

paragraphs.text: Hezekiah asked whether there was a sign the Lord would give him confirming that he would be healed, so that he could rise and go to pray in the house of the Lord, which his heart desired. This means that he recovered within three days.

entries.section: (1) God lengthens Hezekiah's life

paragraphs.text: Isaiah answered him: Here is a sign to reassure you that the Lord will do what He promised; so answer me first, shall the shadow go forward ten degrees, or go back ten degrees?

entries.section: (1) God lengthens Hezekiah's life

paragraphs.text: Hezekiah said to himself that the shadow goes forward, and this appears on the sundial, so he asked God that the sign be contrary to nature, which is the shadow's going back, that is, that it should not go forward but return backward ten degrees. The degrees are those that Ahaz arranged by means of a pillar with steps on it, each step showing a division of time, so that when the shadow goes forward or goes back it appears on this pillar, which is what is called the sundial of Ahaz (Isa 38:8).

entries.section: (1) God lengthens Hezekiah's life

paragraphs.text: Isaiah cried to the Lord, and He brought the shadow back by the degrees by which it had gone forward, the degrees of Ahaz, ten degrees.

This miracle has a deep meaning: it means that God is able to change the order of nature, which is what He did by the resurrection of the Savior after the death on the Cross, giving us a sign of eternal life, in the resurrection of us all from death. It also shows that God is ready to change the whole world for the sake of His children whom He loves. The going back of the shadow means the going back of Hezekiah's age to youth, so that he lived with vitality for fifteen years, with energy and strength.

The going back of the shadow was not in Jerusalem only, but in the whole world, and when it happened and the Babylonians and Egyptians observed it, they were greatly alarmed, and learned afterwards that this was because of Hezekiah's prayer, so they were certain of his godliness and his standing with God.

entries.section: (2) Hezekiah boasts of his possessions

paragraphs.text: At that time, that is, in the days of Hezekiah, and that was either before the paying of silver and gold to Assyria or after his victory. Although his treasuries were empty, they were filled with gifts from the surrounding kings, in honor of him after the sun moved for his healing (2 Chr 32:23). The kingdom of Babylon, subject to the Assyrian empire, began to grow strong and tried to show its influence, and in the end it was able to overcome Assyria and to dominate the world. King Merodach of Babylon tried to establish relations with the surrounding states in order to reduce Assyria's dominion. When he heard of Hezekiah's recovery from his illness, accompanied by the going back of the shadow, that is, that the sun which they worshiped had honored Hezekiah, and he also heard that heaven had been with him in his victory over the Assyrian army, he tried to win his favor by sending him letters of praise and showing concern for his health and his kingdom, and even sent him a gift.

entries.section: (2) Hezekiah boasts of his possessions

paragraphs.text: When the letters of Babylon arrived with the envoys to Hezekiah, and he saw the gift and the king of Babylon's exalting of him, he became proud in his heart, and instead of glorifying God and ascribing the credit to Him, he felt his own strength and thought of allying with Babylon, which was gradually growing strong, and wanted to show his wealth. So he showed his great possessions to the envoys of Babylon, whether gold and silver, or luxuries, or military strength, and in this he stole the glory of God and ascribed it to himself. This is completely different from his attitude when the letters of Assyria came to him, and how he humbled himself before God in humility, so God gave him victory over Sennacherib.

The visit of the envoys of Babylon was an opportunity for Hezekiah to proclaim the name of his God and glorify Him before the nations, that perhaps they might believe. He ought to have made clear to them the power of God that appeared in the victory over Sennacherib, and then in his healing, instead of being proud, relying on his wealth and strength. For when man relies on himself, he forgets God, and when he relies on God, he forgets himself.

And he did not take refuge in the prophet Isaiah to seek his counsel, but was proud and relied on his strength, and so he sinned. Had he asked Isaiah, he would have kept him from this error and preserved him from its evil consequences.

If God has bestowed virtues and blessings on you and you have felt them in your life, do not speak much about that, but thank God and hide your virtues, as you hide your sins. And if you want to proclaim your virtues, would you agree to proclaim your sins first?!

entries.section: (2) Hezekiah boasts of his possessions

paragraphs.text: Isaiah went to Hezekiah to alert him to his sin, and asked him who had visited him and from where, and he told him that they were envoys of Babylon who had come from afar to visit him. Isaiah asked him, What have they seen in your house? Hezekiah answered, They have seen all my treasuries and all the glory that is in my house. Here Isaiah does what God did with Adam when He called to him in the garden after the Fall, saying to him, Where are you? to call him to repentance. Isaiah tries to alert Hezekiah, that he may feel his sin and his pride and his attempt to ally with Babylon rather than rely on God.

entries.section: (2) Hezekiah boasts of his possessions

paragraphs.text: Since Hezekiah did not take heed of his sin, Isaiah declared to him God's punishment: because of his pride and his displaying of his wealth and glory before the envoys of Babylon, a time would come when they would carry all his wealth, and what his fathers, the former kings, had stored up, to Babylon; and more than this, Babylon would not only plunder the wealth of Jerusalem, but would take the royal seed, to become slaves to the king of Babylon.

entries.section: (2) Hezekiah boasts of his possessions

paragraphs.text: Hezekiah felt his sin and humbled himself in repentance (2 Chr 32:24-26), and submitted to the divine judgment and thanked God, because all this chastening would not happen in his days, but after him. This indeed happened in the days of his son Manasseh, who walked in evil.

Hezekiah tried to rely on Babylon and ally with it, and this ruin came upon him. So do not try to rely on the world and its strength, lest many troubles befall you. Rely on God alone, for He will keep you and deliver you from all evil.

entries.section: (3) The death of Hezekiah

paragraphs.text: The rest of the acts of Hezekiah and all his achievements and the building works he carried out, such as making the pool and the conduit and bringing water into the city (Jerusalem), are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah. Then Hezekiah died and was buried with his fathers, and his son Manasseh reigned in his place.
Remember every day that you will leave this world, and prepare for your eternity by repentance, love for God and doing good to all who are around you.
The life of Hezekiah king of Judah is recorded in the Bible in (2 Kgs 18:1-20:21, 2 Chr 29:1-32:33, Isa 36:1-39:8).
1- Hezekiah is a Hebrew name meaning "the Lord has strengthened."
2- He was born in 740 BC in Jerusalem.
3- Ahaz, the father of Hezekiah, began to reign with his father Jotham in 736 BC, when Hezekiah was four years old. Ahaz was wicked, but his kingdom was strong.
4- Ahaz died and his son Hezekiah reigned alone in 716 BC; Hezekiah had reigned for a period with his father Ahaz.

5- Hezekiah removed everything connected with the worship of idols; he destroyed the altars built on the high places and the idols, and also cut down the groves and crushed the bronze serpent (ch. 18:4).
6- He opened the doors of the temple, which had been shut in the days of his father Ahaz (2 Chr 29:3), and began the worship himself and encouraged the people, who followed his example (2 Chr 29:20).
7- He cared for the restoration of the house of the Lord, which had been ruined and neglected in the days of his father Ahaz (2 Chr 29:3).

8- He gathered the priests and the Levites and commanded them to sanctify themselves for the service of the house of the Lord, and charged them to remove the uncleanness from it (2 Chr 29:5), and he organized their divisions (2 Chr 31:2) and commanded them to attend to the feasts and festivals according to the Law (2 Chr 31:3-10).

9- He made military preparations to face the Assyrian army, building forts and fortresses around Jerusalem. He arranged the water supply of the city by digging a conduit from the pool of Gihon to supply the city, surrounded it with a new wall, and attended to the arming of his soldiers (2 Chr 32:3, 4), and encouraged his people against Assyria, because God was with them (2 Chr 32:7, 8).
10- He gave much of his wealth for the daily burnt offerings of the house of the Lord and encouraged the people to give, and they gave abundantly (2 Chr 30:24, 31:5, 6).
11- He took care to keep the Passover in the kingdom of Judah, and even invited the remnant from the kingdom of Israel to share with them (2 Chr 30:2, 15).
12- He took care to have the Psalms of David sung at worship in the house of the Lord and encouraged the people to do so, and they sang with the musical instruments of David (2 Chr 29:27, 30).
13- He took care for the upright conduct of his people, so he collected the proverbs of Solomon from chapter twenty-five until
14- Hezekiah fell ill and prayed to God, and He healed him and extended his life by fifteen years (ch. 20:1, 5, 6), and that was in 701 BC.
15- Merodach, son of Baladan, king of Babylon, congratulated him on his recovery and presented him with a gift (ch. 20:12), and that was in 701 BC.
16- Hezekiah showed his treasuries to the envoys of Babylon, and God punished him through Isaiah by the carrying off of these possessions to Babylon, because of Hezekiah's pride (ch. 20:13, 17, 18).
17- Sennacherib attacked and seized the cities of Judah in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah (ch. 18:13).
18- Hezekiah was afraid and paid gold and silver to Sennacherib and declared his submission to him, so that he would leave Jerusalem (ch. 18:14).
19- Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem, and Hezekiah prayed and spread the Assyrian letters of threat in the house of the Lord (ch. 19:14).
20- Isaiah reassured Hezekiah that God would deliver him from Assyria (ch. 19:20).

21- The angel of the Lord killed a hundred and eighty-five thousand of the Assyrian army, and that was in 701 BC; Sennacherib fled, and his two sons killed him in the temple of his god (ch. 19:35-37).

22- Hezekiah died, after God extended his life by fifteen years, so that he had reigned twenty-nine years, and that was in 686 BC, and his son Manasseh succeeded him (ch. 20:21). Manasseh king over Judah and his son Amon

entries.section: (1) The evils of Manasseh

paragraphs.text: Manasseh succeeded his father Hezekiah on the throne of Judah when he was twelve years old, and his reign lasted fifty-five years in Jerusalem. This was the longest period that any king sat on the throne of Israel or Judah, and his mother's name was Hephzibah.

This means that Hezekiah begat Manasseh three years after his healing and God's lengthening of his life, and perhaps he named him so because he felt that God had made him forget the illness and given him a new life and strong health. But sadly he became occupied with the world, in the form of his concern for the gifts that came to him from those who congratulated him, and was proud and displayed his possessions before the envoys of Babylon to boast of them, and he neglected the upbringing of his son Manasseh, who walked in evil and led the people of God astray more than all the kings who preceded him on the throne of Judah.

entries.section: (1) The evils of Manasseh

paragraphs.text: Manasseh did not follow the example of his father Hezekiah, and perhaps the motive for this was the encouragement of some of the leaders and counselors who loved the worship of idols, or perhaps his mother inclined to evil. What matters is that he walked in the way of evil and idol worship and all the abominations that the nations practiced, and so he led the people of God astray, because he submitted to the worship of the nations and did not learn that they were driven out of the land of Canaan because of their evils, and consequently he exposed himself and his people, by evil conduct, to distresses and to being driven out of this land. This indeed happened, for Manasseh was taken captive for a time to Babylon, and then, after a while, the Babylonian captivity of the people took place.

entries.section: (1) The evils of Manasseh

paragraphs.text: Sadly, he rebuilt the temples of the idols on the high places, which his father had torn down, and so he renewed evil in every place in Jerusalem and around it. Among these temples he set up altars for Baal, a famous pagan god. And he followed the evils of Ahab king of Israel and made a grove for the worship of the pagan gods whom they believed to dwell in heaven. In this he offered worship to the stars and the heavenly bodies and abandoned the worship of God.

entries.section: (1) The evils of Manasseh

paragraphs.text: And going further in evil, Manasseh dared with insolence to build altars to the pagan gods inside the house of the Lord, to challenge Him and provoke Him. Solomon had built altars for idols in Jerusalem, but Manasseh set them up inside the house of the Lord. Thus the temple was no longer a place for hallowing the name of God, but for the worship of idols.

entries.section: (1) The evils of Manasseh

paragraphs.text: He built altars for all the host of heaven and defiled the house of the Lord with them. He was not content with setting them up in the outer court of the temple, but brought them into the inner court of the priests, which no one was allowed to enter except the priests.

entries.section: (1) The evils of Manasseh

paragraphs.text: The host of heaven: the heavenly bodies, the stars and planets.
Used enchantments: sought to read the unseen, visions and dreams.
Observed times: seeing good or bad omens in certain persons, or numbers, or days.
Familiar spirits: the ancients used to believe that it was a spirit that answered the call of its owner, and they thought they were good spirits, whereas the familiar spirit is Satan.
The attendant spirit: a jinn, which some eastern peoples anciently believed followed a man wherever he went.

Manasseh went deep into the worship of idols, to the point of offering his son as a burnt offering to the pagan god Molech; he used sorcery and believed all the pagan beliefs, so he used enchantments, observed times and went after the demons that hide behind familiar spirits and attendant spirits. Thus he went on in every kind of evil to provoke God, and in this he violated the Law of God (Deut 18:

entries.section: (1) The evils of Manasseh

paragraphs.text: Manasseh also made an image of the grove, perhaps taking it from Assyria: a pillar adorned with goats' horns, with the figure of a palm tree on top of the pillar, in addition to a metal network on which were figures of palms, buds, pomegranates and sexual organs to arouse the passions. Then he set this image inside the house of the Lord. This shows the extent of his concern for the worship of the pagan gods and his challenge to God, because God had told David and Solomon to hallow this house for the glorifying of the name of God, but Manasseh made the house of the Lord for the glorifying of the pagan gods.

entries.section: (1) The evils of Manasseh

paragraphs.text: The Lord had made it a condition for His people, in order to keep them forever in the land that He gave to their fathers, that they should keep and do His commandments and the Law that Moses gave them.

entries.section: (1) The evils of Manasseh

paragraphs.text: But they did not listen, for Manasseh seduced them, so they increased in their evil even beyond the other nations whom the Lord drove out before Israel. For the nations did not know God, so they worshiped idols; but the people of God, after God had done great miracles with them and they had worshiped Him for many years, returned to the worship of the idols of the surrounding nations.

If you have repented of sins and moved away from them, do not be careless and return to them. For having tasted the sweetness of life with God, how can you return to evil and uncleanness?! Do not keep anything that brings you back to evil, and cut off your relationship with everyone who helps you in this. Remain firm in the life of repentance, that you may enjoy God.

entries.section: (2) The warning to Manasseh and Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Since Manasseh persisted in his evils and the worship of idols, God warned him through the prophets. God arranged that a large number of prophets should be contemporary with him: Isaiah, Hosea, Habakkuk, Nahum and Zephaniah. They would teach him, and if he did not accept, they would rebuke him, and then, as he continued in evil, they would declare God's judgment on him, that perhaps he might repent. But he went further in evil than the original inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, such as the tribes of the Amorites, and led his people astray, for he told them that the worship of these idols was worship of Jehovah, who brought them out of the land of Egypt. And he was cruel: he was not content merely to disregard the words of the prophets, but violently killed Isaiah, sawing him in two without mercy with a wooden saw, as Jewish tradition mentions, although Isaiah was related to him, being of the royal seed.

entries.section: (2) The warning to Manasseh and Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Tingle: his ears cannot bear it and are pained by the very loud sound.

Therefore the Lord declared His judgment, that He would permit a great calamity to fall upon Jerusalem and all Judah, so that everyone to whom news of this calamity came would not bear to hear the news, because of its cruelty.

entries.section: (2) The warning to Manasseh and Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The line: the string that the builder stretches along the wall to ensure that it is straight.

The Lord threatened him, saying: I will bring upon Jerusalem the punishment that I brought before upon Samaria and upon Ahab and his house, and I will wipe Jerusalem out of existence, as a dish is wiped of the remains of food and then turned upside down on its face, so that nothing remains in it. The stretching of the line here is, of course, for pulling down and not for building. We notice that God did not break the dish but emptied everything in it, for He loves His city Jerusalem and His people, and wants only to cleanse them of evil, that the remnant may repent and return to Him, so that He builds Jerusalem anew and brings them back from captivity.

entries.section: (2) The warning to Manasseh and Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: And I will forsake the remnant of My people and deliver them into the hand of their enemies, so that they become captives and their enemies plunder them. By the remnant of His people He means the two tribes, Judah and Benjamin, because He had already rejected the ten tribes when Assyria took them captive. God warns Manasseh and his people with these punishments, that perhaps they may repent and He may turn back from His punishment, but sadly they did not repent.

entries.section: (2) The warning to Manasseh and Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: God declares that the reason for His punishment of the kingdom of Judah is the evils it committed, from the time the people of God were in Egypt until this time, and the Bible mentions them in the books of the Kings and the Prophets, and they are:
1- They practiced pagan worship in Jerusalem, such as bowing down on the housetops to the gods of heaven (Jer 19:13).
2- They made cakes for the queen of heaven (Jer 7:18).
3- They built the high places of Tophet in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and daughters in order to please the pagan gods (Jer 7:31).
4- They built houses for the sodomites by the house of the Lord, that is, they encouraged sexual perversion (ch. 23:7).
5- The women wove hangings for the grove (ch. 23:7), that is, for the god Ashtoreth, the goddess of love among the Phoenicians.

6- The leaders of the people were wicked: the princes were roaring lions, devouring the people, the judges were evening wolves, the prophets were light and treacherous, and the priests polluted the sanctuary and did violence to the Law (Zeph 3:3, 4).
7- There was iniquity in the city, and injustice, plundering, oppression and strife (Hab 1:3, 4). In sum, the people of God worshiped idols and plunged into evil lusts.

entries.section: (2) The warning to Manasseh and Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Among the evils of Manasseh is that he killed all who opposed his religious policy and all who objected to his uncleanness and evils, such as the prophet Isaiah, so that he filled Jerusalem with the blood of the innocent. Manasseh's sins were not limited to himself; all Judah turned aside after him and followed him in his errors and deviations, so he is responsible for leading them astray.

Pride is what drove Manasseh to be immersed in sin, so beware of it, because the proud person does not listen to any advice. Humble yourself before God, confess your sins before your father of confession and accept guidance, and God will deliver you from every punishment, because He loves you.

entries.section: (3) The death of Manasseh

paragraphs.text: The rest of what Manasseh did and the wrong, unclean ways he followed are recorded in the "Book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah." Manasseh repented after he was taken captive to Babylon, late in his life, then returned to Jerusalem and made many religious reforms, mentioned in (2 Chr 33:11-19).

The distress Manasseh went through at his captivity made him repent. So do not be disturbed by distress, because it is your way to cleaving to God, your turning back from your sins and your spiritual growth. Submit to the will of God, for He arranges every good for you.

entries.section: (3) The death of Manasseh

paragraphs.text: The garden of Uzza: it is the garden of Azariah, and it is part of the royal palace.

Manasseh died and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza, and his son Amon reigned after him. Twenty-one kings reigned over the kingdom of Judah, and they were buried as follows:
1- Fifteen in the city of David, which is part of Jerusalem and in which are the tombs of the kings.
2- Two, Manasseh and his son Amon, in the garden of Uzza.
3- One in Egypt, Ahaz.
4- Two in Babylon, Jehoiachin and Zedekiah.
5- One, Jehoiakim, whose place of burial is not known.

entries.section: (4) The evils of Amon and his death

paragraphs.text: Jotbah: at present it is Khirbet Jefat, and it lies in Galilee.

Amon reigned after the death of his father Manasseh, when he was twenty-two years old, and his reign in Jerusalem lasted two years, and his mother's name was Meshullemeth the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.

entries.section: (4) The evils of Amon and his death

paragraphs.text: Amon committed the same transgressions and sins that his father Manasseh committed before he repented.

entries.section: (4) The evils of Amon and his death

paragraphs.text: Amon walked in the ways of his father Manasseh and worshiped the idols that his father had set up. He did not humble himself, as his father Manasseh humbled himself late in his life, but increased in iniquity.
If God has put some sins far from you, do not return to renewing them and attaching yourself to their sources, for this angers God greatly. Be careful, and learn from the mistakes of others.

entries.section: (4) The evils of Amon and his death

paragraphs.text: Amon abandoned the worship of the true God, the God of his fathers, and did not follow His ways or keep His commandments.

entries.section: (4) The evils of Amon and his death

paragraphs.text: His servants conspired against him and rebelled against him and killed him in his house.

entries.section: (4) The evils of Amon and his death

paragraphs.text: The rebels were planning an insurrection, but the people put it down, and the people killed all those who had rebelled against King Amon, and made his son Josiah king in his place, although he was still a child of eight, in fulfillment of the prophecies for the preservation of the house of David. Amon died a young man at the age of twenty-four, and his reign lasted only two years.

Perhaps the people rejoiced at being rid of the wicked Amon and gave no opportunity for one of his wicked servants to reign, but held fast to the word of God and made Josiah the son of Amon king in his place.

entries.section: (4) The evils of Amon and his death

paragraphs.text: The rest of the acts of Amon and what he did during his short reign are recorded in the "Book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah."

entries.section: (4) The evils of Amon and his death

paragraphs.text: He was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and his son Josiah reigned in his place. Josiah king over Judah

entries.section: (1) Josiah repairs the temple

paragraphs.text: Boscath: it lies in the south of the kingdom of Judah, southwest of Jerusalem, near Lachish.

Josiah was eight years old when he succeeded his father Amon on the throne, and his reign lasted thirty-one years in the capital Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Jedidah the daughter of Adaiah of Boscath, who was therefore a Jewess, not a Gentile, and most likely a godly woman, because the Bible mentions her name and immediately after it shows the uprightness of the life of her son, who reigned as a child; and most likely she took care to bring him up spiritually.

entries.section: (1) Josiah repairs the temple

paragraphs.text: Josiah did all that was right and followed in the steps of his great forefather David, and did not turn aside from the straight path to the right or to the left. The Bible's praise of him is not repeated for the kings of Judah except for Hezekiah and Asa. Most likely Josiah's righteousness is due to the following:
1- What he learned from his godly mother.

2- His grandfather King Manasseh repented in the last days of his life, in about the last five years of it, and perhaps he tried to reform his son Amon, who did not respond, so he took care of his grandson Josiah, who had reached the age of six at the death of his grandfather.
3- The presence of spiritual guides in the kingdom with Josiah, such as the prophet Jeremiah, Shaphan the scribe and the prophetess Huldah.

entries.section: (1) Josiah repairs the temple

paragraphs.text: Shaphan: he was the scribe of King Josiah and was godly, and his sons were Ahikam, who rescued Jeremiah from the pit (Jer 26:24), and Gemariah, who was one of the counselors of King Jehoiakim and in whose chamber Baruch read the prophecies of Jeremiah (Jer 36:10). The grandson of Shaphan is the righteous Gedaliah, who governed the kingdom of Judah after the Babylonian captivity and the capture of King Zedekiah.

When King Josiah reached the age of twenty-six, he began his first reforms by sending to the temple Shaphan the scribe, the son of Azaliah, the son of Meshullam, asking him to charge Hilkiah the high priest to count the money that the people donated and that the doorkeepers collected from them, as King Joash did (ch. 12:4-14), to be given to those who oversee the work of renewing the temple, who would pay it to the workmen carrying out the repair of the ruined parts of the temple.
We notice that Jeremiah began his prophecy five years before these reforms (Jer 1:2), and perhaps it was an encouragement to Josiah to carry out these reforms.

Assyria fell in the twelfth year of Josiah, that is, six years before these reforms, and the Babylonian empire began, but Josiah did not pay attention to these political changes in the world and focused his concern on the spiritual reforms of his country.

entries.section: (1) Josiah repairs the temple

paragraphs.text: Josiah commanded that this money be paid to the carpenters, the builders and the masons, and for buying the materials for the building, timber and hewn stone, to repair the temple. From the abundance of the works and materials that were used to repair the temple, we sense the extent of the destruction that had befallen it in the days of Manasseh, then Amon, and consequently the greatness of the reforms and repairs carried out by Josiah.

entries.section: (1) Josiah repairs the temple

paragraphs.text: The overseers of the work of renewing the temple were not asked for an account of how the sums given to them were spent, because of their honesty, and they were Levites (2 Chr 34:12).

How beautiful it is that we care for the Church, the house of the Lord, not only by repairing her walls and caring for her buildings, but also for every service offered in her and for all souls, that they may enjoy God's care within her.

entries.section: (2) The finding of the Book of the Law

paragraphs.text: While Hilkiah the priest was occupied with repairing the house of the Lord, assisted in this by the priests and Levites, he found a copy of the Book of the Law, which was most likely the five books of Moses, or at least the Book of Deuteronomy, and it had been lost amid the neglect in the days of the wicked kings. Also the former kings neglected that each should keep a copy of the Law, as God had commanded. So Hilkiah rejoiced greatly and handed this copy to Shaphan the scribe to give to the righteous King Josiah, who cared for the worship of God. Shaphan read it as soon as he received it, and this shows the extent of Shaphan's godliness and his concern for the word of God. This shows the grace of God given to His children who care for His house and His worship, for He gave them not only help in repairing the house, but also His holy word, that is, the Book of the Law. Whoever strives spiritually receives many blessings from God.

Everyone who strives spiritually and serves God faithfully, God reveals to him many secrets of His knowledge, guides him in his life and satisfies him with His love. So be a persevering striver, confident that God cares for your labor, whatever your falls and weakness.

entries.section: (2) The finding of the Book of the Law

paragraphs.text: Shaphan returned to the king to tell him that his orders for repairing the temple were being carried out, for the chest in which the people entering the house of the Lord put silver had already been emptied (ch. 12:9), and the money was counted and paid to the overseers in charge of repairing the house, to be spent on the workmen.

entries.section: (2) The finding of the Book of the Law

paragraphs.text: Shaphan also told the king that Hilkiah the high priest had given him a book, the Book of the Law, which Hilkiah had found while the temple was being repaired, and then Shaphan read it before the king.

Shaphan mentions that it was a book because the Book of the Law was not known to the king and the people at this time; they had forgotten it because of the departure of Manasseh and Amon from God, a period of nearly sixty years, that is, not a short period, after King Hezekiah. This shows how far the people of God had departed from His holy word.

entries.section: (2) The finding of the Book of the Law

paragraphs.text: When King Josiah heard the words of the Book of the Law, which Shaphan read to him, he believed everything in it and discovered his sins and the sins of his people, and feared God's punishment because of the multitude of their sins (Deut 28:16-68, Lev 26:14-39). He grieved in holy repentance, to the point that he tore his clothes in remorse before God. The tearing of clothes was a well-known eastern custom showing intense grief. It is noticeable that Shaphan, despite his godliness, did not tear his clothes when he read the book before the high priest or before the king, and this shows the depth of the repentance of the righteous Josiah.

entries.section: (2) The finding of the Book of the Law

paragraphs.text: Josiah was not content to be moved by the word of God, but took practical steps for repentance. He gathered his godly counselors, namely Hilkiah the high priest, Shaphan the scribe and his son Ahikam, and two of those close to him, Achbor and Asaiah. And he said to them: Seek for me a prophet, to make known to me and my people the word of God and its interpretation, and to pray for us and guide us how to obey the word of God, that we may be saved from His wrath and not walk in the way of our fathers, who neglected the word of God and His worship and worshiped idols. By this he means the period in which Manasseh and Amon reigned.

entries.section: (3) The prophecy of Huldah

paragraphs.text: The godly envoys of the king searched for a prophet of God to inform them and make them understand the words of the Law, and they found the prophetess Huldah, who lived in Jerusalem, in the second quarter of it, that is, the new quarter, which is different from the first, the old quarter, in which the city of David is. She was the wife of Shallum, who was in charge of guarding the priests' garments in the house of the Lord and any other garments kept in the temple. Huldah lived in her home, exercising her ministry in the area around her, and did not travel about like some prophets, such as Elisha and Isaiah. Among the blessings of God at this time is the presence of other prophets (ch. 23:2) to proclaim His voice in the days of the wicked kings Manasseh and Amon and to support the righteous King Josiah, and among these prophets was the prophetess Huldah. This means that God gives prophecy to men and women, although He gives it more to men, that they may move and travel in different places to proclaim His voice.

entries.section: (3) The prophecy of Huldah

paragraphs.text: The prophetess Huldah declared the voice of God to the king's envoys, that they might convey it to him, namely that the punishments mentioned in the Book of the Law would come upon this place, that is, the kingdom of Judah and all who are in it. The reason for God's wrath and these punishments is His people's worship of idols and their forsaking of Him, and the divine punishment would continue for a long time. This is what happened in the destruction and burning of Jerusalem and the captivity that lasted seventy years.

entries.section: (3) The prophecy of Huldah

paragraphs.text: After the prophetess Huldah declared God's judgment concerning the kingdom of Judah, she gave the second message to King Josiah, who had cared to hear the word of God when Shaphan the scribe read it to him, and was deeply moved and repented of his sins and those of his people when he heard of the punishment coming upon all. God's word to him was: I have heard your prayers and your weeping and your tender heart humbled before Me; therefore this punishment will not happen in your days, and you will depart in peace from this world and be buried with your fathers, because of your repentance and humility. So the king's envoys returned to him and told him the word of God that the prophetess Huldah had declared.

Josiah died at Megiddo, during the war into which he put himself without need, because it was a war between Egypt and Assyria; and they buried him with his fathers, the kings of Judah, in Jerusalem, and he did not see the punishment of Jerusalem in his days, for this happened in the days of his son Zedekiah, when the Babylonian captivity took place. Thus the righteous Josiah lived in peace, he and his country, all his days.

Your repentance changes everything and removes the wrath of God from you, so He wipes out your sins and every punishment, supports you and rejoices in you, and you live anew and enjoy fellowship with Him. So hasten to repentance, however great your sins or however often repeated.
The reforms of Josiah and the reigns of his sons Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim

entries.section: (1) Renewal of the covenant with God

paragraphs.text: The righteous King Josiah was deeply moved by the words of the Law of God, and this led him to repentance and not to despair, despite the severity of the divine punishment. So he called all the elders of his kingdom, whether the elders of Jerusalem or the elders of the cities of Judah, as well as the priests and the prophets and all the people of Jerusalem. This shows the extent of Josiah's bearing of his responsibilities as a shepherd of the people, for he took care that the great and the small, the rulers and all the people should come to make a covenant with God; he is an example of the faithful servant. And they went up to the house of the Lord, which stood on the hills of Jerusalem. There he stood himself to read the book of the Law of God, for it is an honor for him to read the word of God, and it also shows his concern, his fear of God and his humility before Him. His reading of "all the book of the covenant" does not mean reading all five books of Moses, for that would take many hours, but the commandments and laws that were required to be carried out by all the people, which are part of the Book of Exodus and the Book of Deuteronomy, and which include all the duties of the people toward God.

entries.section: (1) Renewal of the covenant with God

paragraphs.text: His testimonies: His commandments.
His statutes: His worship with all its rites.

After Josiah read the book of the Law from a platform, that is, a place higher than the people, all the people stood, and Josiah made a covenant for himself and for all the people to obey the word of God and hold fast to His commandments and worship. They made this covenant with all their hearts, and the king took care of this so that the people would not return to the worship of idols and the doing of evil.

Josiah's reading of the Law to the people is a carrying out of the word of God that had been neglected for a long time, for God commanded that His Law be read to His people every seven years (Deut 31:10-13).

Do not be disturbed when you hear or read the stern words of God, but let this lead you to the fear of God and to being strengthened in spiritual striving, confident that God wants your salvation and will support you in your striving, whatever your weakness.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: The second order: the high priest had a group of deputies, each in charge of a group of priests. The second order means either these deputies, that is, those in authority after him, for he represents the first order, or it means one of the orders, since the priests were divided into several orders, and he chose the second order, perhaps because its priests were distinguished by godliness, zeal and rejection of evil.

The fields of Kidron: fields lying east of Jerusalem, between it and the Mount of Olives. They are beautiful places in which the worship of idols was offered, and also parks for the people. But after Josiah burned the vessels in them, they were turned into a dump where the people of Jerusalem threw all their refuse, which was burned there, and it was afterward named in this way the valley of the son of Hinnom, and the fire was always burning in it because of the abundance of the waste in it, and from it was taken the word Gehenna, whose fire is not quenched (Mt 5:22, 25:41). Josiah began by cleansing the temple, so he commanded Hilkiah the high priest, together with the priests of the second order, assisted by the keepers of the doors of the temple, to gather the vessels that they used for the worship of Baal that were inside the temple of God, because the wickedness of the former kings had reached the point that they worshiped strange gods inside the house of the Lord.

And after they gathered these vessels, they took them out to the fields of Kidron, where the worship of idols was offered, and he burned these vessels there, to defile these places which the people had anciently set apart for idols and which afterward were turned into a dump, as a declaration of the people's rejection of all pagan worship. And to confirm the rejection of the worship of idols, Josiah took the ashes of the burning and carried them to Bethel and scattered them there, to defile the place which the kings of Israel had set apart for the worship of one of the golden calves that Jeroboam made; for he cared not only for the kingdom of Judah but also for the kingdom of Israel, which had been taken captive and no longer had a king who cared for the worship of God in it. Of course, he did not burn these vessels in Jerusalem, so as not to defile the city.

Perhaps Josiah began by cleansing the temple and Jerusalem, and afterwards took care to repair the temple mentioned in the previous chapter. The cleansing, of course, took several years, and consequently Josiah would have begun the cleansing when he was about twenty years old, because he began the repair of the temple when he was twenty-six years old (ch. 22:3).

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: The planets (mazzaloth): a group of mansions in which the pagans believed that the gods came down and dwelt, so they called them the mansions.

Continuing the work of cleansing, Josiah drove out all the priests of the idols who offered worship to Baal, the moon, the planets and all the host of heaven, and in this he put an end to the idolatry that had spread in the days of Manasseh and Amon.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: He also brought out the image of Ashtoreth, the wife of the idol-god Baal, from the temple and from all Jerusalem and threw it into the valley of Kidron, where he burned it and ground it to dust, and scattered the dust on the graves of the common people. And the grove, that is, this idol, which had been set up by the wicked King Manasseh (ch. 21:7, 2 Chr 33:15), he burned and ground and scattered its dust on the graves of the people who shared in the worship of this idol, so that this dust would become unclean in the sight of the people, because the dead were unclean and whoever touched them became unclean. By scattering it on the graves, that is, he defiled it, and in this way no one could make it again or worship it. This shows the extent of Josiah's firmness and his complete removal of evil.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: Josiah also removed the houses that had been built by the house of the Lord and were set apart for sexual perversion, for some perverted men lived in them, so that men would come and commit fornication with them. And the women wove houses of cloth to be set up as tents, within which were placed images of the grove, and sexual perversion was practiced in these tents as well. This shows the extent of the people's degradation in their worship of idols, so Josiah cleansed the temple and what is around it of all these evils. It also shows how the house of the Lord had been turned into a house for the worship of idols in the days of the former wicked kings, and now Josiah restores it to be for the worship of God alone, with worship practiced within it in complete purity and cleanness.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: Geba: a city in Benjamin on the northern edge of Judah.
Beersheba: the capital of the Negev, the farthest south of Judah.

Josiah gathered the priests of the Lord from all the land, from the farthest north to the farthest south of the kingdom of Judah, so that worship would be only in the temple of God in Jerusalem and no worship of God would be offered on the high places, as the kings had permitted, not only the wicked among them but also the righteous, and many of his descendants. He also defiled all the places of worship that had been set up for the Lord, or for the idols, on the hills, by burning the bones of the dead on them or by any means, so that no one would approach them afterward for worship. This included all the high places scattered throughout the kingdom of Judah, from one end to the other. Likewise the people had been accustomed to offer worship at the gates of the city of Jerusalem, where towers were built, which made them high places, so he removed all the images of the idols and the altars set up at the gates, such as the altar set up at the gate of Jerusalem, on the left, which was before the house of Joshua the governor of the city.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: As for the priests who continued to offer sacrifices to the Lord on the high places in the days of Manasseh, Josiah did not allow them to use the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, although he permitted them to eat unleavened bread among their brethren the priests; that is, they did not continue in their priestly work as a punishment for them, because they offered worship in a place other than the house of the Lord, and this is against the Law. But at the same time he took care of their food, so they ate like the rest of their brethren, as was done with the priests who had bodily defects (Lev 21:21-23), so they ate of the bread of the offerings presented in the house of the Lord, which the priests had a right to eat, which is the unleavened bread (Lev 6:16-18).

In your firmness with others, if you are compelled to punish someone, to establish justice and truth, do not forget the needs of the one punished, for he is a human being; that is, be merciful also in your punishment, that you may lead everyone to life with God.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: The valley of the children of Hinnom: it lies southeast of Jerusalem, between the Horse Gate and the well of Job, and the children of Hinnom is the name of a Canaanite tribe.
Tophet: a place in the valley of the children of Hinnom for burning human bodies, where human sacrifices were offered to the god Molech.

Molech: the god of the children of Ammon. They made for him a hollow bronze statue of a seated man with his hands stretched out before him, and lit a fire under it until the bronze became red with heat, then they passed the children between his hands to hallow them and consecrate them to this god, and their bodies were scorched by the extremely hot bronze. They also placed some children on his hands as a sacrifice, and they were burned by the intense heat, and they beat drums loudly so that they would not hear the cries of the children as they died. The word Tophet means a drum, so they called the place Tophet.

One of the most famous places of idol worship near Jerusalem was the area of Tophet, which was set apart for the worship of the god Molech and lies in the valley of the children of Hinnom. King Josiah took care to defile this area, to stop the atrocities that took place there, the passing of children through the fire or offering them as sacrifices to this pagan god.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: The worshipers of the sun set apart chariots drawn by horses, with which they went out before the sun, and the horses, because of their speed, represented the sun, which moves in the sky. The wicked kings before Josiah used to give horses to those who worshiped the sun. So Josiah destroyed the horses that were used in the worship of the sun, so that the people would not think them holy. He also burned the chariots of the sun, to remove any trace of sun worship, and of course he gave no more horses after that to these pagan worships. These horses were near the chamber of Nathan-melech, which was inside the house of the Lord, in one of the colonnades. Nathan-melech was one of the king's eunuchs and perhaps was the one in charge of these horses.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: Ahaz had built an upper chamber on top of one of the buildings of the temple of the Lord, and because he was wicked and neglected worship in the house of the Lord, he may have built this upper room for his private needs, or for the worship of idols. But Manasseh and Amon, the wicked kings of Judah, built altars on it for the worship of the host of heaven; that is, they worshiped idols above the temple of the Lord. King Manasseh also set up altars for the idols in the two courts of the house of the Lord, that is, the inner court for the priests and the outer court for the people. We understand from this how widespread the worship of idols was, not only in Jerusalem, the holy city, but also inside the house of the Lord, in the days of the wicked kings. All this the righteous Josiah removed and broke until it became dust, and he supervised the work himself, then hurried, carrying this dust, and scattered it in the valley of Kidron, where idol worship had been practiced, and defiled it. All this shows Josiah's zeal, for he does the work himself and hurries to get rid of the traces of pagan worship in the temple and to defile the place of idol worship in the valley of Kidron.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: The mount of corruption: the southern part of the Mount of Olives, and the Mount of Olives lies east of Jerusalem and was afterward called by this name because of the abundance of idol worship on it.
The Zidonians: the inhabitants of Sidon, which is on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.
The Moabites: they lived east of the river Jordan and the Dead Sea.
The children of Ammon: they lived east of the river Jordan.

Solomon had set up on the hills south of the Mount of Olives altars for the worship of famous pagan gods, such as Ashtoreth, the unclean goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh, the defiled god of the Moabites, and Molech, the god of the children of Ammon, whose worship God hates. All these altars and the idols before them and the groves, that is, the pillars set up for the pagan gods, the righteous Josiah broke in pieces, and he was not content with removing them, but also defiled their place by putting the bones of the dead on them, and whoever touched these bones became unclean (Lev 21:1), and in this way no one could worship idols in these places again. Thus the places of worship of the pagan gods, who symbolize fertility and life, were turned into places for the bones of the dead; that is, they became a symbol of death and not of life, and by this he meant to remove the idea of idol worship from the minds of the people, that they might hate it.

When you drive out any strange thought that defiles your mind, take care also to repeat the Psalms and prayers, so as to remove every trace of evil from your thinking and replace it with the thoughts of God, remembering also the danger of these thoughts, which lead to judgment and destruction, so that you hasten to drive them out.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: Josiah's heart was inflamed with the love of God, so he wanted to cleanse the whole world of the worship of idols. He was not content with cleansing the kingdom of Judah over which he reigned, but his concern extended to the kingdom of Israel, which had fallen into captivity. As a result of the weakness of the Assyrian empire, which had dominated the whole world and the kingdom of Israel, he moved by the power of God to remove the worship of idols from Bethel, which Jeroboam the son of Nebat had established, who split the kingdom of Israel. That is, Josiah wanted to remove the beginning and the roots of the worship of idols from Israel, so he went to Bethel, the most important place of idol worship, and removed from the high places there the altar and the grove and all the buildings connected with idol worship. He broke them down and burned the wood in them, and crushed everything until it became dust, and scattered it; that is, he protected the land from every trace of pagan worship.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: While Josiah was destroying idol worship in Bethel, he learned of the existence of tombs near the place, so he sent and brought out the bones of the dead and burned them on the altar to defile it, so that no one would try to offer idol worship again in this place. In this he fulfilled the word of God that a prophet had spoken about Jeroboam about three hundred years before, that a king named Josiah would come and remove the idol worship that Jeroboam had made in Bethel (1 Kgs 13:2).

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: Title: a stone or pillar set up to declare the presence of a grave in this place, and sometimes used as a mark on the road.
Out of Samaria: not from the city of Samaria, but from one of its cities; he was from Bethel, which belonged to Samaria.

The king noticed a monument in the place and asked, Whose is it? The men of the city answered him that it was the grave of the man of God who came from Judah and foretold all that he had done at Bethel.

And Josiah commanded that the bones of the prophet not be moved, nor the bones of the other prophet, who was from one of the cities of Samaria, that is, from Bethel, who was buried with him (1 Kgs 13:11), in honor of the prophet who came from Judah, who prophesied the removal of idol worship.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: Josiah was not content with removing idol worship from Bethel, but his cleansing extended also to the various cities of Samaria. He removed from their high places the worship of idols, that is, the altars, groves and buildings set up for it, and burned the bones of the dead on them to defile them so that they would not be used again for worship, and scattered their ashes, as he did at Bethel. We notice from this his continued concern to cleanse of idol worship every place his hand could reach, so that the kingdom of Judah, and also the kingdom of Israel, which had been taken captive, would be clean of pagan worship.

entries.section: (2) The cleansing of the temple, Jerusalem and the cities of Samaria

paragraphs.text: Josiah commanded that all the priests of the high places in Samaria be killed upon their pagan altars, and he burned the bones of the dead on them, then returned to Jerusalem.

Josiah was compelled to slay the priests of the idols during the cleansing from this worship, because God had been longsuffering with them until they led astray many of the simple people, so Josiah had to be firm and stop the source of evil, who were these priests.

And although the people of the kingdom of Israel had walked for many long years in the worship of idols, they accepted what Josiah did, as they accepted what the prophet Elijah did of old when he slew the prophets of Baal (1 Kgs 18:40), because the people know in their depths that God alone is the true God and that all these worships, however many years they may have continued, are vain.

Do not be afraid to proclaim the voice of God with power, however prevalent evil may be, to awaken the conscience of those who are far away, and God will support you; only take care to pray well before you speak, so that the words may be from God and not out of pride or personal motive. You are responsible to speak, to rescue the lost and those far away.

entries.section: (3) The Passover and the removal of sorcery

paragraphs.text: After Josiah's concern for cleansing Jerusalem, Judea and the cities of Samaria, he began the positive side of the reforms by calling for the keeping of the feast of the Passover, which the Law prescribed in the book of the covenant that they had found in the temple. He called all the people of Jerusalem and Judea and also the people of the kingdom of Israel, for Josiah was a preacher of God everywhere (2 Chr 35:18).

entries.section: (3) The Passover and the removal of sorcery

paragraphs.text: The celebration of the Passover that Josiah kept was a magnificent celebration, whose splendor was not equaled by any of the Passover celebrations that the children of Israel held since the days of Samuel, that is, for more than five centuries; that is, Josiah's Passover surpassed in splendor the Passover that Hezekiah kept, and it was said that none like it had been kept since the days of Solomon. The excellence of Josiah's Passover lay in his concern to carry out the Law with all exactness, as God had declared to Moses, and also in his giving from his own wealth very many lambs, numbered in thousands, which encouraged the princes to give lambs also (2 Chr 35:1-19). When this Passover was kept in Jerusalem, King Josiah was twenty-six years old. From this we understand that he began the positive reforms, from the repair of the temple and the Passover, in the eighteenth year of his reign, whereas the cleansing operations were during the preceding years.

May you take care that your worship of God is with all your heart, and also care for His holy feasts and the building of His churches, giving generously, for this shows your love for Him and the extent of your attachment to Him, and stirs your spiritual feelings.

entries.section: (3) The Passover and the removal of sorcery

paragraphs.text: The teraphim: small images of the pagan gods placed in the house for people to worship, in addition to the large images set up in the temples.

Along with his positive reforms, Josiah continued the work of cleansing, not only of the idols set up in the pagan temples but also of the teraphim found in the homes, for he was firm with the people in making them bring the teraphim out of their houses so that he might destroy them. He also did away with the sorcerers and diviners and all who deal with demons to know the future, or any demonic works. In sum, he took care to cleanse Jerusalem and Judea of all causes of evil that violate the Law. And in this he fulfilled the word of God that he found in the book of the Law that was found in the temple.

entries.section: (4) The excellence of the righteous Josiah, then his death

paragraphs.text: God declares clearly here the distinction of Josiah above all the former and later kings of Judah. Though some kings were distinguished, such as Hezekiah and Asa, they come after him in rank, because he took care with all his heart to carry out the Law of God. He was the king who took most care to cleanse his country of the worship of idols and of all the altars set up on the high places. And although he knew of God's punishment that would come upon the kingdom of Judah after the end of his life, he did not grow slack, but on the contrary moved with unusual energy to glorify the name of God in Judah and Israel, after His name had been insulted for long years before. He is a symbol of hope, righteousness and perseverance in spiritual striving, in addition to firmness and strength in declaring the truth, so that he deserves to be called the second of the kings after David in spiritual rank, for he resembled his forefather David in that he arose in the midst of a wicked generation far from God and clearly proclaimed the name of God.

entries.section: (4) The excellence of the righteous Josiah, then his death

paragraphs.text: Despite the greatness of the reforms that Josiah made, God did not turn back from His decision to punish the kingdom of Judah, because the people, who had gone astray in the days of Manasseh and his son Amon and responded to Josiah, responded superficially and not from the whole heart, as is proved by the fact that the kings who came after Josiah, who were his sons, walked in evil and returned to the worship of idols, so they deserved divine punishment. This shows two things:
1- The extent to which evil had spread and ruled over the hearts of the people of God.
2- The greatness of Josiah, who appeared in a wicked generation, for the kings before him and after him were wicked.

entries.section: (4) The excellence of the righteous Josiah, then his death

paragraphs.text: Because of the evils of the people of God, God insisted on His decision to abandon the kingdom of Judah, as He had abandoned the kingdom of Israel, and to leave His temple to be torn down and burned in the destruction of Jerusalem and Judea. All this was because of the superficiality of His people's worship and the attachment of their hearts to idols.

Beware of superficial worship, practicing everything formally, without understanding or feeling, and being content with the appearance without the substance, for this does not please God but provokes Him. Ask God's help to repent of your sins and try to understand every act of worship you offer Him, and He will grant you, not only forgiveness, but also that you feel Him and delight in being with Him.

entries.section: (4) The excellence of the righteous Josiah, then his death

paragraphs.text: The rest of the works that Josiah did are recorded in the "Book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah."

entries.section: (4) The excellence of the righteous Josiah, then his death

paragraphs.text: In the thirty-first year of the reign of Josiah, the king of Egypt, Pharaoh Necho, attacked the king of Assyria, who had become weak at this time, and Pharaoh seized the opportunity to take possession of the territories belonging to him in Syria. Josiah felt fear for his country, lest Pharaoh seize it, so he went out to fight him and did not consult God, and Pharaoh tried to keep him out of the war, because he wanted to fight the king of Assyria, but Josiah erred and attacked Pharaoh, and Pharaoh killed him at the city of Megiddo, inflicting on him a mortal wound. We notice that Solomon is a type of Christ in the building of the temple, as Christ founded the Church. Hezekiah is also a type of Christ in the extension of his life by fifteen years after he had been condemned to death by his illness, and Christ after His death had His life extended forever. As for Josiah, he is a type of Christ in his death outside Jerusalem at the hands of his enemies at Megiddo, as Christ was crucified outside Jerusalem at Golgotha.

entries.section: (4) The excellence of the righteous Josiah, then his death

paragraphs.text: The soldiers under Josiah carried their king with his mortal wound until they reached Jerusalem, and he died there (2 Chr 35:24) and they buried him, then his son Jehoahaz reigned after him. For the original word translated in the previous verse as "killed him" means, in its origin, that he was wounded with a mortal wound and did not die at once.

entries.section: (5) Jehoahaz reigns over Judah and is taken captive
