paragraphs.text: Libnah: it lies thirty-two kilometers from Jerusalem and is thirteen kilometers from Lachish to the northeast, southwest of Jerusalem.

Jehoahaz was not the firstborn, who should have reigned in place of his father, but was fourth in order among his brothers. The sons of Josiah are: the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum, who is also called Jehoahaz. The people thought he was the best of his brothers, so they made him king after his father Josiah.

Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when the people anointed him king, and his reign lasted only three months. His mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of the town of Libnah, and he is, of course, not the prophet Jeremiah, who was from Anathoth, not Libnah.

These three months in which Jehoahaz reigned are the period after the death of his father in the war, when Pharaoh of Egypt, who was called Necho, killed him; this Pharaoh went on his way with his armies to Carchemish, which lies west of the river Euphrates, then returned, leaving his armies at Carchemish, and to show his authority over the kingdom of Judah, he deposed Jehoahaz, took him captive and brought him to Egypt. After that he went to Carchemish and was defeated before Nebuchadnezzar, and the king of Babylon took possession of the region of the Levant as far as Egypt.

entries.section: (5) Jehoahaz reigns over Judah and is taken captive

paragraphs.text: Neither the Book of Kings nor the Book of Chronicles mentions the evils of Jehoahaz, but the writer of the Book of Kings was content to mention the summary, which is that he did evil in the sight of the Lord, following in this the footsteps of his forefathers, that is, Manasseh and Amon.

But we can deduce from (Jer 23:10-17 and Ezek 19:1-5) that he committed many evil deeds. Ezekiel describes him in (Ezek 19:1-5) as one who "learned to catch the prey; it devoured men." He devoured his people, and came to work for himself and not for the kingdom.

And we wonder how he was able in only three months to show his evil, and this shows that he learned nothing from his righteous father and seized the opportunity of his reign to hasten to evil. This also shows that the people's choice of him was not on the basis of righteousness and goodness, but by human standards, because the people had not repented truly in the days of Josiah. It seems that Josiah was firm in his cleansing of evil, but he was not given great opportunity to teach the people, so their repentance was weak.

May we not love ourselves, but be like our beloved Shepherd and Redeemer, who did not seek His own but ours, who said, "The Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister." "He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life shall find it."

entries.section: (5) Jehoahaz reigns over Judah and is taken captive

paragraphs.text: Riblah: a city in the land of Hamath, in the present state of Syria, lying north of the Sea of Galilee. A talent of silver: it has several weights, ranging between 20 and 40 kg.
A talent of gold: equal to 17.4 kg.

Pharaoh Necho returned to Riblah, which is north of the kingdom of Judah, and summoned Jehoahaz and arrested him and sent him to Egypt as a prisoner, and he ordered an enormous tribute upon Judah, amounting to a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold. The people of the kingdom paid this sum, whereas in the days of Hezekiah the gold and silver were paid from the treasuries of the house of the Lord and the house of the king and the gold stripped from the house of the Lord, and it did not burden the people, although the sum paid in the days of Hezekiah was far greater than that required in the days of Jehoahaz and his brother Jehoiakim, who reigned after him (ch. 18:

entries.section: (5) Jehoahaz reigns over Judah and is taken captive

paragraphs.text: Jehoiakim: its meaning is "Jehovah will raise up," whereas Eliakim means "God will raise up." Pharaoh changed his name as a kind of imposition of authority, but, by God's arrangement, the men of Judah suggested this name to him, and it is a name with a beautiful spiritual meaning, because Jehovah is the God of Israel and not just any god, perhaps in order to benefit the king of Judah; but sadly he did not learn from his new name and departed from God.

Necho made Eliakim, the elder brother of Jehoahaz, king in his place and changed his name from Eliakim to Jehoiakim. Jehoahaz came to Egypt and died there, in fulfillment of the prophecy of Jeremiah, who said of him: "Thus saith the Lord touching Shallum the son of Josiah (Shallum is the original name of Jehoahaz, before his name was changed when he ascended the throne), which went forth out of this place; he shall not return thither any more: but he shall die in the place whither they have led him captive, and shall see this land no more" (Jer 22:10-12). This is the first time a brother, and not a son, reigned on the throne of the kingdom of Judah. Because of the evil of Jehoahaz, Pharaoh of Egypt deposed him and took him captive, imposed a tribute on the land of Judah and made his brother king in his place. But when the people believed in the days of Moses and sought God, He smote Pharaoh and his people and brought them out with an uplifted arm; so when we are with God, He protects us and gives us victory over our enemies the demons, but when we walk in evil, He forsakes us, and we are humbled.
Hold fast to the commandments of God and to His worship, and He will protect you and give you victory in all your wars with the demons, and you will live in peace however much troubles surround you.

entries.section: (6) Jehoiakim reigns over Judah

paragraphs.text: Taxed: assessed.
Jehoiakim undertook to pay the tribute of silver and gold to Pharaoh, but he imposed taxes on the people of the land, according to what they possessed, so as to be able to pay it.

entries.section: (6) Jehoiakim reigns over Judah

paragraphs.text: Rumah: it is Khirbet Rumah, ten kilometers north of Nazareth.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign over Judah in the capital Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zebudah the daughter of Pedaiah of the town of "Rumah."

entries.section: (6) Jehoiakim reigns over Judah

paragraphs.text: Sadly, Jehoiakim walked in evil like his brother Jehoahaz and learned nothing from the righteousness of his father. The Book of the prophet Jeremiah gives us details of this king's evils: he was selfish, seizing the rights of others, far from God (Jer 26:21-24).

May you learn from the righteousness and virtues of those around you, and also take warning from the evils of others, because all these are messages sent to you. Jehoiakim did not learn from the righteousness of Josiah nor from the evils of his brother Jehoahaz, who was taken captive to Egypt.
Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin and Zedekiah, the last kings of Judah

entries.section: (1) Judah's submission to Babylon

paragraphs.text: Nabopolassar king of Babylon triumphed over Egypt in the battle of Carchemish and took all its possessions, among them the kingdom of Judah, and the commander of the army was Nebuchadnezzar, the son of Nabopolassar. Thus the new king of Judah, Jehoiakim, submitted to the king of Babylon, after the deposing of his brother Jehoahaz. Jehoiakim remained in submission for three years and no longer paid tribute to Egypt.

Three years after Jehoiakim began to reign, Nabopolassar died and his son Nebuchadnezzar became king of Babylon (Jer 25:1, 46:2). He was occupied with wars against some of the surrounding countries to subdue them, so Jehoiakim seized the opportunity and rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar.

entries.section: (1) Judah's submission to Babylon

paragraphs.text: God had ordered the chastening of Judah for its evils, and the king of Judah did not listen to the prophet Jeremiah about submitting to Babylon, so God stirred up the Chaldeans, who were the inhabitants of southern Mesopotamia, and also the neighbors of Judah, the Arameans, the Moabites and the children of Ammon, and perhaps this was at the instigation of the king of Babylon, in addition to their long-standing enmity toward Judah. This was a severe chastening for Judah, and three thousand and twenty-three of the Jews were taken captive (Jer 52:28) and sent to Babylon.

entries.section: (1) Judah's submission to Babylon

paragraphs.text: God abandoned His people in the kingdom of Judah and commanded their scattering and the loss of their existence as an independent state, for two reasons:
1- The evils of King Manasseh, which appeared in his worship of strange gods.
2- The people's wronging of one another and the shedding of innocent blood.

God is just, so do not persist in your snare, like Manasseh, and neglect the word of God. He is longsuffering, but He will surely punish if you do not repent. So submit to Him and return to Him, that you may enjoy His mercies. Do not wrong others, because their cry reaches God. Be merciful, and you will obtain the mercies of God.

entries.section: (1) Judah's submission to Babylon

paragraphs.text: The life of Jehoiakim and all the evils that took place in it were written in a special book, the history of the kings of Judah, which is other than the Book of Chronicles found in the Bible.

entries.section: (1) Judah's submission to Babylon

paragraphs.text: Jehoiakim died and was buried with his fathers, and his son Jehoiachin took the kingship after him. The king of Babylon had bound him with chains of bronze and wanted to take him captive to Babylon, but changed his mind, and most likely killed him and cast his body on the ground, as Jeremiah says, like the carcass of a donkey (Jer 22:19), and because of his evils his people did not mourn for him.

entries.section: (1) Judah's submission to Babylon

paragraphs.text: The king of Egypt no longer made any raids outside his own land, because the king of Babylon had taken all the lands lying from the border of Egypt to the river Euphrates, which Egypt had occupied before.

entries.section: (2) The captivity of Jehoiachin

paragraphs.text: Elnathan: one of the princes of Judah (Jer 36:12). Jehoiachin succeeded his father on the throne of Judah when he was eighteen years old, and his reign lasted only three months, in Jerusalem, the capital of his kingdom, and his mother's name was Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan, of the city of Jerusalem. The Book of Chronicles mentions (2 Chr 36:9) that Jehoiachin began to reign when he was eight years old, and there is no discrepancy between what is mentioned in the Book of Chronicles, because Jehoiachin reigned with his father Jehoiakim for ten years, and this was the practice with many kings, in order to secure the throne for their sons, because Jehoiakim reigned after his brother Jehoahaz, and likewise after Jehoiachin, Zedekiah the brother of Jehoiakim reigned, that is, the brothers of the king had ambitions for the kingship. At the age of eighteen, Jehoiachin reigned alone, after the death of his father, and what confirms his reigning at the age of eighteen is that he had wives, as mentioned in (v. 15).

entries.section: (2) The captivity of Jehoiachin

paragraphs.text: Jehoiachin walked in evil from the beginning of his reign, although he reigned only three months, but he learned evil from his father Jehoiakim, who shared the kingship with him for ten years, that is, from the childhood of Jehoiachin. This evil appears in the following:
1- The worship of idols.
2- Various lusts and injustice.

entries.section: (2) The captivity of Jehoiachin

paragraphs.text: After the arrest of Jehoiakim and his being killed by the king of Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar sent his armies, and they besieged Jerusalem. This shows the power of Nebuchadnezzar and his dominion over the kingdom of Judah, and also shows God's abandonment of the kingdom of Judah because of their evils, so He permitted Jehoiakim to be killed and the city to be besieged, then Jehoiachin to be arrested only three months after he began to reign, as will appear in the following verses.

entries.section: (2) The captivity of Jehoiachin

paragraphs.text: Nebuchadnezzar was besieging the city of Tyre, then came himself to his armies besieging Jerusalem, and that was about three months after Jehoiachin began to reign, and consequently the situation became dangerous and the city was on the verge of falling and being destroyed by Babylon.

entries.section: (2) The captivity of Jehoiachin

paragraphs.text: Jehoiachin was afraid of Babylon's storming the city and destroying it and killing him and those with him in the palace, so he preferred to surrender himself in order to live. Some think that he did this to preserve the city from destruction, so he went out, he and his mother, his servants, the rulers of his kingdom and the eunuchs in charge in his palace, and surrendered himself to the king of Babylon, and that was in the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign over Babylon.

entries.section: (2) The captivity of Jehoiachin

paragraphs.text: The king of Babylon seized the contents of the treasuries of the temple and the treasuries of the royal palace and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold which Solomon king of Israel had made and put in the temple, and these were the large vessels and tables, such as the altar of incense and the table of the showbread. As for the small vessels, Nebuchadnezzar took them in his first attack (v. 6), and they are the vessels from which his grandson King Belshazzar drank (Dan 5:2), and these vessels are the ones that returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel (Ezra 1:7-11). Thus the word of the Lord was fulfilled, which Isaiah spoke to King Hezekiah (ch. 20:17), that everything in the treasuries, which Hezekiah proudly showed to the Babylonians when he recovered from his illness, would be taken

entries.section: (2) The captivity of Jehoiachin

paragraphs.text: Smiths: blacksmiths.

The king of Babylon took captive the notables of Jerusalem, ten thousand in number, who were the rulers and leaders of the people and the skilled craftsmen and the smiths; and they left in Jerusalem none but the simple common people, in order to weaken the city, so that there would be none in it to revolt against him or try to gain independence, and it would always remain in need of Babylon's help. If the notables were only ten thousand, this shows that the inhabitants of the city were few, and its weakness increased when the strong were taken from it.

entries.section: (2) The captivity of Jehoiachin

paragraphs.text: In this way the king of Babylon took captive Jehoiachin king of Judah, his mother, his wives, his eunuchs and his mighty men, and all the notables of the land, seven thousand persons, and the skilled craftsmen and smiths, a thousand persons, and all the officers and strong soldiers, about two thousand, so that the total is ten thousand, as mentioned in (v. 14). The king of Babylon took them all captive and carried them off to Babylon, and Jehoiachin remained imprisoned in Babylon for about thirty-seven years; as for the notables, after Nebuchadnezzar had boasted of them in Babylon, he distributed some of them in the lands of his kingdom.

The natural result of evil is divine chastening, so may you learn from your mistakes, that you may repent and return to God and not be careless until calamities befall you. And if trial comes to you, do not murmur, but accept it from God and examine yourself, for perhaps you are the cause, through your sins and your shortcomings in the love of God. And be sure that God seeks your salvation through trials and awaits your return to Him, to compensate you for all you have missed.

entries.section: (3) The reign of Zedekiah and his rebellion against Babylon

paragraphs.text: When Zedekiah began to reign he was twenty-one years old, and his reign lasted eleven years in Jerusalem, the capital, and his mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of the town of Libnah. His name was formerly Mattaniah, and he was the uncle of King Jehoiachin, who was taken captive to Babylon, and the brother of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar killed, and consequently he was the son of Josiah, the righteous king, and the full brother of Jehoahaz, because their parents were Hamutal and Josiah.

entries.section: (3) The reign of Zedekiah and his rebellion against Babylon

paragraphs.text: Zedekiah followed in the steps of Jehoiakim king of Judah, who preceded him, in walking in evil.

entries.section: (3) The reign of Zedekiah and his rebellion against Babylon

paragraphs.text: Zedekiah was not content with doing evil and leading his people astray, but at the end of his reign he also rebelled against the king of Babylon, and this was a motive for the king of Babylon to attack him and take him prisoner, kill his sons and his men, and destroy Jerusalem and burn it, as the prophets foretold; that is, the wrath of God and His chastening of His people for their evils were fulfilled.

Do not be evasive and treacherous in your promises, like Zedekiah, but pledge yourself to God to walk with Him and ask His help, and He will help you. And if you fall short, return to Him, for He is tender toward the weak, but hates the presumptuous and the rebellious.
The captivity of Judah

entries.section: (1) The fall of Jerusalem and the capture of Zedekiah

paragraphs.text: Zedekiah king of Judah was subject to Babylon and visited it, declaring his loyalty to Nebuchadnezzar, but when he returned to Jerusalem and learned that Tyre had rebelled against Babylon, he thought of allying with Tyre, Sidon, Moab, the children of Ammon and Edom, the countries surrounding the kingdom of Judah, and even of allying with Egypt, and in this way rebelling against Babylon. When Nebuchadnezzar learned of it, he sent his armies to Jerusalem, while he himself was staying at Riblah, which lies in a central place between Tyre and Jerusalem, so that from it he could attack both.

The armies of Nebuchadnezzar reached Jerusalem and besieged it on the tenth day of the tenth month in the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, and Nebuchadnezzar built siege works around Jerusalem, which were heaps of earth on which he built towers, so that from them he could shoot arrows and hurl missiles from catapults at the city. The city was in danger and no one could go out of it, and the battering of the city began.

The army of Babylon had taken the cities of Judah, except Lachish and Azekah, because they were two fortified cities near Egypt (Jer 34:7), in addition to its besieging of Jerusalem. When Egypt found the army of Babylon divided among a number of cities, it seized the opportunity to fight Babylon and came out with its armies, and then Babylon was compelled to gather its armies to attack Egypt (Jer 37:5). The Egyptians were afraid and withdrew, and Babylon returned with all its armies to besiege Jerusalem.

entries.section: (1) The fall of Jerusalem and the capture of Zedekiah

paragraphs.text: The siege of Jerusalem by Babylon lasted about a year and a half, and on the ninth day of the fourth month of the eleventh year of Zedekiah's reign (Jer 52:6), the famine grew severe in Jerusalem and the people almost died, so that their notables searched for food in the dumps, and the women ate their children, and their skin cleaved to their bones; then not a few of them died, and plague spread and killed many of them also (Ezek 5:12).

entries.section: (1) The fall of Jerusalem and the capture of Zedekiah

paragraphs.text: Broken up: the king's guards broke a part of the wall and made an opening in it.

The way of the gate between two walls: the pool of Siloam was in the city of Jerusalem, in the southeast of it, at the meeting of two walls, between which was one of the gates of the city, most likely the Fountain Gate (Neh 3:15), and there was a road beside the wall leading to this gate. In this road, which is before the king's garden, the guards opened a breach in the wall.
The king's garden: a large garden belonging to the king.

When Zedekiah king of Judah saw that the Chaldeans had built towers and begun to aim arrows from them and catapults, from which they hurled stones and burning balls on the city, he felt that the city was about to fall into their hands, so he hurried with his officers and his retinue to flee from Jerusalem by night, and commanded his guards to open a breach in the wall at the pool of Siloam, so that he could slip out through it and flee with his face covered, so that the people or the Babylonian soldiers would not see him. He went out of the city at the meeting of the valley of Kidron and the valley of the son of Hinnom, and fled by the way of the wilderness leading to the city of Jericho.

entries.section: (1) The fall of Jerusalem and the capture of Zedekiah

paragraphs.text: The Chaldeans did not know of the king's flight by night, but in the morning they saw the breach and learned of the flight of a group from the city, and pursued them until they overtook them in the wilderness of Jericho, and seized the king, while his men fled and left him alone in the hands of the Chaldeans. Perhaps Zedekiah wanted to cross the river Jordan at Jericho and take refuge with the Moabites, but he was seized before he could accomplish his purpose.

entries.section: (1) The fall of Jerusalem and the capture of Zedekiah

paragraphs.text: The soldiers of Nebuchadnezzar led King Zedekiah to the city of Riblah, where Nebuchadnezzar was staying, to condemn him there before the king of Babylon.

entries.section: (1) The fall of Jerusalem and the capture of Zedekiah

paragraphs.text: Before Nebuchadnezzar they humiliated Zedekiah by killing his sons before his eyes, and they were children, because Zedekiah was thirty-two years old at that time; then they put out his eyes and bound him with two chains of bronze, one for his hands and the other for his feet, which is what was done to criminals and the very wicked, or to those whom they wanted to humiliate and control completely. In this the prophecies of Jeremiah and Ezekiel were fulfilled (Jer 32:4, 5, Ezek 12:13).

The natural result of distance from God and walking in evil is extreme humiliation. So be careful of sin and consider its terrible results, that you may keep away from it, and so save yourself and live in peace in the hands of God your Father.

entries.section: (2) The burning of the temple and Jerusalem and the captivity of the people

paragraphs.text: The siege of Jerusalem by Babylon lasted a year and a half, for it began on the tenth day of the tenth month in the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign (v. 1) and continued until the seventh day of the fifth month of his eleventh year, and the city had been breached and King Zedekiah fled from it, then the king of Babylon seized him (vv. 4, 5). The eleventh year of King Zedekiah corresponds to the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign over Babylon, and at this time Jerusalem fell. Nebuzaradan, a servant of the king of Babylon, held a high position in the Babylonian state, the captaincy of the guard, which roughly corresponds to the minister of defense.

entries.section: (2) The burning of the temple and Jerusalem and the captivity of the people

paragraphs.text: When Jerusalem fell into the hand of Nebuzaradan and he entered it, he burned the house of the Lord, which Solomon had built three hundred years before, and he also burned the king's palace and the palaces of the notables and the houses of Jerusalem in general, and in this the prophecies of the prophets were fulfilled (Jer 21:10, Ps 79:1).

entries.section: (2) The burning of the temple and Jerusalem and the captivity of the people

paragraphs.text: The armies of the Chaldeans broke down the walls around Jerusalem.

entries.section: (2) The burning of the temple and Jerusalem and the captivity of the people

paragraphs.text: Nebuzaradan took captive the rest of the people who remained in the city and the deserters who had taken refuge with the king of Babylon, surrendering, during the siege of Jerusalem.

entries.section: (2) The burning of the temple and Jerusalem and the captivity of the people

paragraphs.text: And Nebuzaradan left the simple poor people to be vinedressers and husbandmen.

Satan wants to tear down your life and leave nothing in you but weakness and humiliation, so hold fast to the commandments of God and do not surrender to him, however much you fall, for God will never leave you as long as you hold fast to Him, and in this way Satan fears you, and you even gain authority over him, to trample his power. Do not be careless about any sin, because your enemy is fierce, but he is greatly afraid of God and of everyone who trusts in Him.

entries.section: (2) The burning of the temple and Jerusalem and the captivity of the people

paragraphs.text: The Chaldeans had plundered, in their former attacks on Jerusalem, the silver and gold and all the precious vessels (Dan 1:2, ch. 24:13), and now, before they burned the temple, they broke in pieces the two pillars of bronze, which were extremely beautiful, as (v. 17) shows, and they also broke the sea, which was an enormous bronze basin, and its bases of bronze, for they were all of great size, and they carried this bronze to Babylon.

entries.section: (2) The burning of the temple and Jerusalem and the captivity of the people

paragraphs.text: Shovels: plural of shovel, that is, a spade.
Snuffers: a tool like scissors for cutting off the burnt part of the wick.
The soldiers of the king of Babylon also seized the pots, shovels, snuffers, dishes and all the bronze vessels that were used in the temple.
